surahs: She that is to be examined
flows: Praise to Allah, Lord of the worlds, the Merciful, Sovereign of the Day of Recompense; Him alone we worship and ask for help and for guidance to the straight path.
The surah opens with the disjointed letters Alif, Lam, Meem.
This Book guides those conscious of Allah, who believe in the unseen, pray, spend and are certain of the Hereafter, while Allah has sealed the hearts of those who disbelieve.
Some say they believe in Allah and the Last Day but do not; they think they deceive Allah and the believers, and their hearts hold a disease.
Told not to cause corruption on the earth, they claim to be reformers, yet they are the corrupters without perceiving it.
They call the believers foolish, tell their evil ones they were only mocking, and have bought error in exchange for guidance, a trade that brings no profit.
They are like one whose kindled fire goes out, leaving him in darkness, or like people in a rainstorm of darkness, thunder and lightning who walk only when it flashes.
People are told to worship their Lord, who created them, made the earth a bed and the sky a ceiling, and sent rain, and not to attribute equals to Allah.
Those in doubt about what was sent down to the Prophet are challenged to produce a surah like it, and warned of the Fire whose fuel is men and stones.
Believers who do righteous deeds are given good tidings of gardens with flowing rivers, familiar fruits and purified spouses, where they will abide eternally.
Allah gives even the example of a mosquito; believers know it is the truth, disbelievers question it, and by it He guides many and misleads the defiantly disobedient.
The defiantly disobedient break Allah's covenant, sever what He ordered to be joined and cause corruption on earth, and they are the losers.
People are asked how they can disbelieve in Allah, who gave them life, will cause them to die and revive them, and created the earth and the seven heavens.
Allah tells the angels He will place a successor on earth, teaches Adam the names, Iblees refuses to prostrate, Satan makes Adam and his wife slip, and Adam repents.
The Children of Israel are told to remember Allah's favor, fulfill His covenant, believe in what confirms their Scripture, not hide the truth, pray, and fear a Day without intercession.
They are reminded Allah saved them from Pharaoh, forgave the calf, revived them and sent manna and quails, yet some changed the words given them and they wanted lesser food.
Those who believe in Allah and the Last Day and do righteousness, whether believers, Jews, Christians or Sabeans, have their reward with their Lord without fear or grief.
Their covenant is taken under the raised mount, Sabbath-breakers become apes, and they resist slaughtering the cow Moses orders, by which Allah revives a slain man, yet their hearts harden.
Believers should not expect them to believe: some distorted the Torah, some write scripture with their own hands, and they claim the Fire will touch them only a few days.
They broke their covenant to worship Allah alone, do good to parents and the needy, and not shed each other's blood, believing in part of the Scripture and rejecting part.
They denied or killed messengers sent after Moses, rejected the Book they recognized, took the calf, and though claiming the Hereafter is theirs, will never wish for death.
Whoever is an enemy to Gabriel, who brought the Quran down, or to Allah's angels and messengers, has Allah as his enemy; only the defiantly disobedient deny His clear verses.
They followed the devils' teaching in Solomon's reign: magic, and what the angels Harut and Marut taught at Babylon, which separates spouses and leaves no share in the Hereafter.
Believers are told not to say Ra'ina; many People of the Scripture envy them and wish they would disbelieve; Allah replaces any abrogated verse with a better or similar one.
Jews and Christians claim only they will enter Paradise and each says the other has nothing to stand on, but whoever submits to Allah and does good has his reward.
None is more unjust than those who stop Allah's name being mentioned in His mosques and seek their ruin, facing disgrace in this world and great punishment in the Hereafter.
To Allah belong the east and the west, so wherever one turns, there is the Face of Allah.
They claim Allah has taken a son, but exalted is He; all in the heavens and earth obey Him, the Originator who says Be, and it is.
Those who do not know demand that Allah speak to them or send a sign, but the Prophet is sent with the truth to give good tidings and warn.
Jews and Christians will not approve of the Prophet until he follows their religion, but Allah's guidance is the only guidance.
Those given the Book who recite it as it should be recited believe in it, and whoever disbelieves in it is among the losers.
The Children of Israel are again told to remember Allah's favor in preferring them, and to fear a Day when no soul can help another.
Abraham, tried and made a leader, raises the House with Ishmael, prays for a messenger, submits to Allah and, like Jacob at death, tells his sons to die as Muslims.
Told to become Jews or Christians, believers answer that they follow Abraham's religion and believe in all the prophets were given without distinction, for Allah's religion is best.
Those who argue about Allah are asked whether they know better than Allah when they say Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac and Jacob were Jews or Christians.
The foolish question the change of qiblah, but believers, a just community, are told to face al-Masjid al-Haram wherever they are; the People of the Scripture know it is true.
Allah sent a messenger from among them to recite His verses, purify them and teach them the Book and wisdom, so remember Him and be grateful.
Believers seek help through patience and prayer; those killed in Allah's way are alive, and the patient who say in disaster they belong to Allah receive blessings and mercy.
As-Safa and al-Marwah are among Allah's symbols, so there is no blame on whoever makes Hajj or 'umrah for walking between them.
Those who conceal the clear proofs and guidance Allah sent down are cursed by Allah and by those who curse, except those who repent, correct themselves and make it clear.
Those who die as disbelievers have the curse of Allah, the angels and all people upon them forever, with no lightening of the punishment and no reprieve.
Your god is one God; there is no deity except Him, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful.
The creation of the heavens and earth, night and day, ships at sea, rain reviving the earth, creatures, winds and clouds are signs for people who use reason.
Some take equals besides Allah and love them as Allah, but when they see the punishment, leaders and followers disown one another, and they will never leave the Fire.
People are told to eat the lawful and good and not follow Satan, a clear enemy who orders evil, immorality and saying about Allah what they do not know.
Called to follow Allah's revelation, they follow their fathers instead; the disbelievers are like cattle that hear only calls and cries, deaf, dumb and blind.
Believers are told to eat good things Allah provided and thank Him; only dead animals, blood, swine and what is dedicated to other than Allah are forbidden, except under necessity.
Those who conceal what Allah sent down of the Book for a small price fill their bellies with Fire, having exchanged guidance for error and forgiveness for punishment.
Righteousness is not facing east or west but belief in Allah, the Last Day, angels, Book and prophets, giving to those in need, prayer, zakah, keeping promises and patience.
Legal retribution is prescribed for those murdered, with pardon and payment allowed as a mercy, and in legal retribution there is life for people of understanding.
One leaving wealth at death should make a fair bequest to parents and relatives; whoever alters it sins, but correcting an unjust bequest is no sin.
Fasting is prescribed in Ramadhan, the month the Quran was revealed, with days made up by the ill and traveler, relations allowed at night, and Allah near to answer supplication.
Do not consume one another's wealth unjustly or send it to the rulers to take a portion of people's wealth in sin, knowingly.
The new moons mark times for people and for Hajj, and righteousness is not entering houses from the back but fearing Allah.
Fight in Allah's way those who fight you without transgressing, not at al-Masjid al-Haram unless they fight there, until there is no fitnah, and stop if they cease.
Fighting in the sacred month answers aggression in the sacred month, and violations bring legal retribution, so answer an assault in kind while fearing Allah.
Spend in the way of Allah, do not throw yourselves into destruction, and do good, for Allah loves the doers of good.
Complete Hajj and 'umrah for Allah, with sacrifice or fasting where due, no sexual relations or disputing in Hajj, departing from 'Arafat, and remembering Allah during the numbered days.
Some speak pleasingly and call Allah to witness, yet are fierce opponents who spread corruption, destroying crops and animals, and pride seizes them when told to fear Allah.
Some people sell themselves seeking the approval of Allah, and Allah is kind to His servants.
Believers are told to enter Islam completely and not follow Satan, are warned against deviating after clear proofs, and are reminded that all matters return to Allah.
Worldly life is made attractive to disbelievers who ridicule the believers, and those given the Scripture differed out of envy while Allah guided the believers to the truth.
No one enters Paradise without trials like those before, who were shaken by poverty and hardship until they asked when Allah's help would come, and it is near.
What is spent of good goes to parents, relatives, orphans, the needy and the traveler, and Allah knows whatever good is done.
Fighting is prescribed though it is hated, for people may hate what is good for them and love what is bad, and Allah knows while they do not.
Fighting in the sacred month is a great sin, but averting people from Allah's way and from al-Masjid al-Haram and expelling its people are greater, and apostates' deeds become worthless.
Those who believed, emigrated and fought in the cause of Allah hope for His mercy, and He is Forgiving and Merciful.
Wine and gambling hold great sin and some benefit, but their sin is greater, and what should be spent is the excess beyond needs.
Give thought to this world and the Hereafter; improving the orphans' affairs is best, they are your brothers, and Allah knows the corrupter from the amender.
Believers must not marry polytheistic men or women until they believe; a believing slave is better, for polytheists invite to the Fire while Allah invites to Paradise.
Keep away from wives during menstruation until they are pure, then come to them as Allah ordained; wives are a place of sowing, and Allah loves those who purify themselves.
Do not make oaths by Allah an excuse against righteousness and making peace; Allah does not blame unintentional oaths, only what hearts have earned.
A vow of abstention allows four months, divorced women wait three periods, divorce is twice before the final third, and wives are released kindly and not stopped from remarrying.
Mothers may nurse their children two full years, the father provides for them fairly, neither parent is harmed through the child, and weaning or a wet nurse is by consent.
Widows wait four months and ten days, and men may hint at a proposal during this time but not contract marriage until the term ends.
Divorce before the marriage is consummated: a gift of compensation if no dowry was set, otherwise half of it, and foregoing it is nearer to righteousness.
Guard the prayers, especially the middle prayer; in fear pray on foot or riding, and when secure remember Allah as He taught you.
Wives left behind at death have a bequest of a year's maintenance without being turned out of their homes.
Divorced women are owed a fair provision, a duty upon the righteous, and Allah makes His verses clear so people may reason.
Thousands who left their homes fearing death were told by Allah to die and were then restored to life, yet most people do not show gratitude.
Fight in the cause of Allah and know that Allah is Hearing and Knowing.
Whoever gives Allah a goodly loan will have it multiplied many times over, for Allah withholds and grants abundance, and to Him all return.
After Moses, the Children of Israel asked their prophet for a king to fight in Allah's way, but when fighting was prescribed most of them turned away.
Allah appoints Saul king despite objections, the chest carried by angels is his sign, and after a test at a river his few faithful soldiers pray for patience against Goliath.
They defeat Goliath's army by Allah's permission, David kills Goliath and is given kingship and prophethood, and Allah checks some people by others to keep the earth from corruption.
These are the verses of Allah recited to the Prophet in truth, and he is one of the messengers.
Allah raised some messengers above others, spoke to some and gave Jesus clear proofs, yet those after them differed and fought, some believing and some disbelieving.
Believers are told to spend from what Allah provided before a Day with no exchange, friendship or intercession.
Allah, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer: no sleep overtakes Him, none intercedes without His permission, and His Kursi extends over the heavens and the earth.
There is no compulsion in religion; whoever rejects Taghut and believes in Allah holds the firmest handhold, as Allah brings believers into light and Taghut takes disbelievers into darkness.
Abraham silences King Nimrod, who argued about his Lord, by challenging him to bring the sun up from the west.
A man who asked how a ruined town could live again is made to die a hundred years and revived, and Abraham is shown how Allah revives the dead.
Spending in Allah's way is like a grain that grows seven spikes of a hundred grains each, and Allah multiplies reward for whom He wills.
Charity must not be spoiled by reminders, injury or showing off, but given from good earnings for Allah's approval, disregarding Satan's threat of poverty.
Allah gives wisdom to whom He wills, and whoever is given wisdom has been given much good.
Allah knows whatever is spent or vowed, and the wrongdoers have no helpers.
Open charity is good and secret charity to the poor better; it is for the poor restricted in Allah's cause, and those who spend night and day are rewarded.
Those who consume interest stand like one beaten into insanity by Satan; Allah permits trade and forbids interest, destroying it while increasing charities.
Those who believe, do righteous deeds, establish prayer and give zakah have their reward with their Lord, without fear or grief.
Believers must give up remaining interest or be at war with Allah and His Messenger, and if they repent they keep their principal, neither wronging nor wronged.
A debtor in hardship is given time until ease, and giving up the debt as charity is better.
Fear a Day when all are returned to Allah and every soul is paid in full for what it earned, without injustice.
Debts for a set term are written justly, witnessed by two men or a man and two women, and on a journey without a scribe a security deposit is taken.
All in the heavens and earth belongs to Allah, who will bring people to account for what they show or conceal, forgiving or punishing whom He wills.
The Messenger and the believers believe in Allah, His angels, books and messengers without distinction, and say they hear and obey and seek His forgiveness.
Allah charges no soul beyond its capacity, and the believers pray not to be blamed for forgetting or erring, nor burdened beyond their ability, but pardoned, forgiven and given victory.
The surah opens with the disjointed letters Alif, Lam, Meem.
Allah, there is no deity except Him, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of existence.
Allah sent down the Book in truth confirming what came before, as He revealed the Torah and the Gospel, and those who disbelieve His verses face severe punishment.
Nothing on earth or in the heaven is hidden from Allah, who forms people in the wombs as He wills; there is no deity except Him.
The Book has precise verses that are its foundation and unspecific ones the deviant follow seeking discord, while those firm in knowledge believe all of it is from their Lord.
Those of understanding pray that their hearts not deviate after guidance and that Allah grant them mercy.
They affirm that Allah will gather the people for a Day about which there is no doubt, for Allah does not fail in His promise.
The wealth and children of those who disbelieve will not avail them against Allah, and they are fuel for the Fire.
Their way is like that of Pharaoh's people and those before them, who denied Allah's signs and were seized for their sins.
Those who disbelieve are told they will be overcome and gathered to Hell, a wretched resting place.
The two armies that met at Badr, one fighting in Allah's cause and one disbelieving, are a sign and lesson that Allah supports with His victory whom He wills.
Love of women, sons, gold, silver, horses, cattle and land is made attractive, but better are gardens, purified spouses and Allah's approval for those who fear Him.
Those who fear Allah pray, saying they have believed and asking Allah to forgive their sins and protect them from the punishment of the Fire.
They are the patient, the true, the obedient, those who spend in Allah's way and those who seek forgiveness before dawn.
Allah, the angels and those of knowledge bear witness that there is no deity except Him, maintaining creation in justice.
The religion with Allah is Islam; those given the Scripture differed out of jealousy, killed prophets, refused the Scripture's arbitration and claimed the Fire would touch them only briefly.
Allah, Owner of sovereignty, gives and takes kingship, honors and humbles, merges night and day, brings the living from the dead and provides without account.
Believers must not take disbelievers as allies instead of believers, except as a precaution, for Allah warns of Himself and to Him is the return.
Allah knows whatever is concealed or revealed in the breasts and all that is in the heavens and the earth, and He is over all things competent.
On the Day every soul finds its good and evil deeds before it, it will wish its evil were far away, and Allah is kind to His servants.
Whoever loves Allah should follow the Prophet so that Allah loves and forgives him, and all are told to obey Allah and the Messenger.
Allah chose Adam, Noah and the families of Abraham and 'Imran; 'Imran's wife pledged her unborn child, bore Mary, and Allah raised her in Zechariah's care with His provision.
Zechariah prays for good offspring and is given tidings of John despite old age and a barren wife, with the sign that he cannot speak for three days.
The angels tell Mary that Allah has chosen and purified her above all women and give her tidings of the Messiah Jesus, though no man has touched her.
Jesus is sent to the Children of Israel with the Torah, the Gospel and miracles; the disciples support him, Allah raises him, and his creation is likened to Adam's.
The People of the Scripture are called to worship Allah alone, told Abraham was neither Jew nor Christian, and rebuked for misleading, betraying trusts, breaking covenants and altering Scripture.
No prophet would tell people to worship him, angels or prophets, and Allah took the prophets' covenant to believe in and support a messenger confirming what they had.
All in the heavens and earth submit to Allah, believers believe in what all the prophets were given, and no religion other than Islam will be accepted.
Allah does not guide those who disbelieve after believing and seeing clear signs; the curse of Allah, the angels and the people is on them, except those who repent.
Repentance is not accepted from those who increase in disbelief after belief, and those who die disbelievers could not ransom themselves with the earth's fill of gold.
No one attains the good reward until they spend from what they love, and Allah knows whatever is spent.
All food was lawful to the Children of Israel except what Israel forbade himself before the Torah; whoever invents lies about Allah after that is a wrongdoer.
Allah has told the truth, so follow the religion of Abraham, who inclined to truth and was not a polytheist.
The first House of worship for mankind is at Makkah, with the standing place of Abraham; whoever enters is safe, and pilgrimage to it is due from those able.
The People of the Scripture are asked why they disbelieve and avert believers; obeying a party of them would return believers to disbelief, but holding to Allah guides.
Believers are told to fear Allah, hold together to His rope without dividing, remember how He made them brothers, and enjoin good, unlike those who divided.
On the Day some faces turn white and some black: those who disbelieved after believing taste punishment, while the white-faced abide forever in Allah's mercy.
These are Allah's verses, recited in truth, and Allah wants no injustice to the worlds.
To Allah belongs everything in the heavens and the earth, and to Him all matters return.
Believers are the best nation produced for mankind, enjoining right, forbidding wrong and believing in Allah; it would have been better had the People of the Scripture believed.
The disobedient People of the Scripture can only annoy believers and are humiliated for killing prophets, but some recite Allah's verses at night, prostrate, believe and are righteous.
Wealth and children will not help the disbelievers against Allah; what they spend in this life is like a frosty wind destroying a harvest.
Believers must not take as intimates those other than themselves who wish them hardship and rejoice at their harm; patience and fearing Allah make their plots harmless.
At Uhud two parties nearly lost courage; Allah recalls the victory at Badr and the promise of angels as reassurance; victory and the decision to forgive or punish are His.
Believers must not consume usury doubled and multiplied, but fear Allah and the Fire prepared for disbelievers, and obey Allah and the Messenger.
Hasten to forgiveness and a garden as wide as the heavens and earth, prepared for the righteous who spend, restrain anger, pardon people and seek forgiveness after sinning.
Similar situations have passed before, so travel the earth and see the end of those who denied.
This is a clear statement to the people, and guidance and instruction for those conscious of Allah.
Do not weaken or grieve; the other people were wounded too, and Allah alternates days to reveal believers, take martyrs, purify them and show who fights and is steadfast.
Muhammad is only a messenger like those before him; if he died or were killed, turning back would not harm Allah, who rewards the grateful.
No one dies except by Allah's permission at a set time; whoever wants the reward of this world or the Hereafter is given it, and the grateful are rewarded.
Many religious scholars fought alongside prophets without weakening or submitting; they prayed for forgiveness, firm feet and victory, and Allah rewarded them in this world and the Hereafter.
Obeying the disbelievers would turn believers back as losers; Allah is their protector and the best of helpers.
Allah will cast terror into the disbelievers' hearts for associating with Him what He gave no authority for, and their refuge is the Fire.
Allah kept His promise until believers lost courage, disputed and disobeyed; He tested them with distress upon distress, sent calming drowsiness, and forgave those whom Satan made slip.
Believers should not say, like disbelievers, that the dead would have lived had they stayed; Allah gives life and death, and to Him all will be gathered.
By Allah's mercy the Prophet was lenient with them; he is told to pardon them, seek forgiveness for them, consult them, then rely on Allah.
If Allah aids you no one can overcome you, and if He forsakes you no one can aid you, so believers should rely on Allah.
No prophet would act unfaithfully over war booty; whoever betrays brings what he took on the Day of Resurrection, and one seeking Allah's pleasure is unlike one earning His anger.
Allah favored the believers by sending a Messenger from among them to recite His verses, purify them and teach them the Book and wisdom.
When disaster struck the believers at Uhud, though they had struck twice as hard at Badr, it was from themselves, and it came by Allah's permission to reveal the believers.
The hypocrites, asked to fight or defend, said they would have followed had they known there would be fighting, and said the killed would have lived had they obeyed.
Those killed in Allah's cause are not dead but alive with their Lord, provided for, rejoicing in His bounty and in good tidings about those yet to join them.
After injury, believers answered Allah and the Messenger at Hamra' al-Asad; warned that people had gathered against them, they said Allah is sufficient, and Satan only frightens with his supporters.
Those hastening into disbelief will never harm Allah; they have no share in the Hereafter, and their extended time only increases their sin before a humiliating punishment.
Allah will separate the evil from the good among believers; He does not reveal the unseen to them but chooses messengers, so believe in Him and His messengers.
Those who withhold what Allah gave them of His bounty should not think it good for them; it will encircle their necks on the Day of Resurrection.
Allah heard the Jews who called Him poor and records their killing of prophets; they refuse a messenger without a fire-consumed offering, yet earlier messengers were denied despite clear proofs.
Every soul will taste death and be fully repaid on the Day of Resurrection; whoever is saved from the Fire and enters Paradise succeeds, and worldly life is delusion.
Believers will be tested in possessions and selves and hear much abuse from those given the Scripture and polytheists; patience and fearing Allah show determination.
Those given the Scripture were bound to make it clear but threw it away for a small price; those who love praise for what they did not do face punishment.
To Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and He is competent over all things.
The creation of the heavens and earth and the alternation of night and day are signs for those of understanding.
Those of understanding remember Allah, reflect on creation and pray for protection from the Fire, forgiveness and to die with the righteous; their Lord answers that no work is lost.
The disbelievers' movement through the land is a small enjoyment ending in Hell, while those who feared their Lord abide forever in gardens beneath which rivers flow.
Some of the People of the Scripture humbly believe in Allah and what was revealed to both, not selling His verses, and their reward is with their Lord.
Believers are told to persevere, endure, remain stationed and fear Allah so that they may succeed.
Mankind is told to fear their Lord, who created them from one soul and its mate and spread many men and women, and to fear Allah and the wombs.
Give orphans their property, do not swap your defective things for their good ones, and do not consume their property into your own, a great sin.
Fearing injustice to orphan girls, men may marry two, three or four women, or one or those their right hand possesses if they fear injustice, and must give bridal gifts.
Provide for the weak-minded from property in your care; test orphans until marriageable age, release their property with witnesses once they show sound judgement, and do not consume it hastily.
Men and women have a set share of what parents and relatives leave; relatives, orphans and the needy present at the division are given something, and guardians must fear Allah.
Those who unjustly devour the property of orphans only consume fire into their bellies, and they will burn in a Blaze.
Allah fixes the shares of children, parents, spouses and siblings after any bequest or debt; these are His limits, with gardens for the obedient and the Fire for transgressors.
Women who commit unlawful sexual intercourse, proven by four witnesses, are confined to houses; two who commit it are dishonored, but left alone if they repent and reform.
Allah accepts the repentance of those who do wrong in ignorance and repent soon after, not of those who repent only when death comes or die as disbelievers.
Men may not inherit women by compulsion or pressure them to return gifts; they must live with them in kindness and not take back a wife's gifts when replacing her.
Fathers' wives and listed relatives are forbidden in marriage, as are married women except those the right hand possesses; others are lawful with bridal gifts, including believing slave girls.
Allah wants to make things clear, guide to the practices of those before, accept repentance and lighten burdens, while followers of passions want deviation; mankind was created weak.
Believers must not consume one another's wealth unjustly, only through trade by mutual consent, nor kill themselves; whoever does so in aggression and injustice will be driven into a Fire.
If you avoid the major sins you are forbidden, Allah will remove your lesser sins and admit you to a noble entrance.
Do not wish for what Allah gave others over you; men and women each have a share of what they earned, so ask Allah of His bounty.
Allah has made heirs to what parents and relatives leave, and those bound by oaths must be given their share.
Men are in charge of women; wives whose arrogance is feared are advised, forsaken in bed and struck, but not once they obey; in dissension, each family sends an arbitrator.
Worship Allah alone and do good to parents, relatives, orphans, the needy, neighbors, companions, travelers and those your right hands possess; Allah dislikes the self-deluding and boastful.
Allah dislikes those who are stingy and conceal His bounty, or spend to be seen without believing, with Satan as companion; believing and spending would have cost them nothing.
Allah does no injustice and multiplies good deeds; He will bring a witness from every nation, and that Day disbelievers will wish the earth covered them.
Believers must not approach prayer intoxicated or in janabah until washed; if ill, traveling or without water after relieving or contact with women, they wipe with clean earth.
Those given a portion of the Scripture buy error; some Jews distort words and defame the religion, and they are told to believe before faces are obliterated or cursed.
Allah does not forgive association with Him but forgives anything less for whom He wills; associating others with Him is a tremendous sin.
Some claim to be pure, but it is Allah who purifies whom He wills, wronging no one; they invent untruth about Allah, a manifest sin.
Those given a portion of the Scripture who believe in superstition and false objects of worship, calling disbelievers better guided than believers, are cursed by Allah, with no helper.
They have no share of dominion and would give nothing if they did; they envy people Allah's bounty, though He gave Abraham's family the Scripture, wisdom and a great kingdom.
Those who disbelieve in Allah's verses burn in a Fire with their skins replaced, while believers who do righteous deeds abide forever in gardens with purified spouses.
Allah commands rendering trusts to whom they are due and judging between people with justice.
Believers must obey Allah, the Messenger and those in authority, and refer any disagreement to Allah and the Messenger.
Some claim belief yet want to refer judgement to Taghut; the hypocrites turn away from the Messenger, then swear they meant only good, and Allah knows their hearts.
Messengers are sent to be obeyed; people do not truly believe until they accept the Messenger's judgement, and whoever obeys Allah and the Messenger is with the prophets and righteous.
Believers are told to take precautions, go forth, fight in Allah's cause for the oppressed and against Satan's allies, and not fear people as some did when fighting was ordained.
Death overtakes people even in lofty towers; they credit good to Allah and blame evil on the Prophet, but all is from Allah, and one's misfortune is from oneself.
Whoever obeys the Messenger obeys Allah; some pledge obedience but plot otherwise by night, so the Prophet should leave them and rely on Allah.
Had the Quran been from other than Allah, they would have found much contradiction in it, so they should reflect upon it.
When news of security or fear reaches them they spread it, though referring it to the Messenger and those in authority would let the discerning understand it.
The Prophet is told to fight in Allah's cause, being responsible only for himself, and to encourage the believers, so Allah may restrain the disbelievers' might.
Whoever intercedes for a good cause shares in its reward, and whoever intercedes for an evil cause shares in its burden.
Return a greeting with a better one, or at least the same, for Allah takes account of all things.
There is no deity except Allah, who will surely assemble all for the Day of Resurrection, about which there is no doubt.
Believers should not split over the hypocrites; take none as allies until they emigrate, and seize and kill those who turn away, except those linked by treaty or offering peace.
A believer who kills a believer by mistake frees a believing slave and may owe compensation, or fasts two months; killing one intentionally brings Hell, Allah's anger and curse.
Believers going forth in Allah's cause must investigate and not deny the faith of one who greets them with peace for worldly gain, for they were once like that.
Believers staying home, other than the disabled, are not equal to those who strive with wealth and lives; Allah promised both the best but raised the strivers by degrees.
Those the angels take while wronging themselves, claiming oppression though Allah's earth was spacious for emigration, face Hell, except the helpless; emigrants for Allah find abundance and reward.
Prayer may be shortened when traveling in fear; in danger it is prayed in groups carrying arms, and once secure the regular prayer at its specified times is re-established.
Do not weaken in pursuing the enemy; if you are suffering, they suffer too, but you hope from Allah what they do not.
The Book was revealed so the Prophet judges between people; he must not argue for deceivers, who hide from people but not from Allah, nor have defenders on Resurrection Day.
Whoever does wrong or wrongs himself and then seeks Allah's forgiveness will find Him Forgiving and Merciful; a sin is earned only against oneself.
Whoever commits an offense or sin and then blames it on an innocent person carries slander and manifest sin.
By Allah's favor and mercy a group failed to mislead the Prophet; Allah revealed to him the Book and wisdom and taught him what he did not know.
There is no good in much private conversation except enjoining charity, what is right or reconciliation; doing so for Allah's approval earns a great reward.
Whoever opposes the Messenger after guidance is clear and follows other than the believers' way will be driven into Hell.
Allah does not forgive association with Him; those who associate have strayed far, calling on female deities and, in truth, on a rebellious Satan.
Cursed Satan vowed to take a portion of Allah's servants, mislead them, stir desires and make them alter Allah's creation; his promises are delusion and his followers' refuge is Hell.
Believers who do righteous deeds, male or female, will enter Paradise forever; it is not gained by wishful thinking, and whoever does wrong will be recompensed for it.
None is better in religion than one who submits to Allah, does good and follows Abraham's upright religion; Allah took Abraham as an intimate friend.
To Allah belongs everything in the heavens and the earth, and He encompasses all things.
Asked about women, Allah gives a ruling on them, on orphan girls denied their due whom men wish to marry, on oppressed children, and on justice for orphans.
A wife fearing her husband's contempt may make a settlement; husbands cannot be equal between wives but must not leave one hanging, and if they separate Allah enriches each.
Those given the Scripture and believers were instructed to fear Allah, who owns the heavens and earth, needs no one, can replace people, and holds the reward of both worlds.
Believers must stand firm in justice as witnesses for Allah, even against themselves, parents or relatives, rich or poor, without following personal inclination.
Believers are told to believe in Allah, His Messenger, His Book and earlier Scripture; whoever disbelieves in Allah, His angels, books, messengers and the Last Day has strayed far.
The hypocrites, who waver between belief and disbelief, take disbelievers as allies, wait to profit from either side and pray lazily to be seen, face a painful punishment.
Believers must not take the disbelievers as allies instead of the believers, giving Allah a clear case against themselves.
The hypocrites will be in the Fire's lowest depths, except those who repent, reform, hold fast to Allah and become sincere; Allah gains nothing by punishing the grateful.
Allah dislikes public mention of evil except by one who was wronged; whether good is shown or hidden or an offense is pardoned, Allah is Pardoning and Competent.
Those who believe in some messengers and reject others are truly disbelievers facing a humiliating punishment, while those who believe in all without distinction will be rewarded.
The People of the Scripture ask for a book from heaven, as they asked Moses to see Allah; they took the calf, broke the covenant, killed prophets and slandered Mary.
They claimed to have killed the Messiah, Jesus son of Mary, but they did not kill or crucify him; Allah raised him to Himself, and he will witness against them.
For their wrongdoing, usury and averting people, the Jews were forbidden some good foods, but those firm in knowledge among them and the believers will be given a great reward.
Allah revealed to the Prophet as He did to Noah and later prophets, spoke directly to Moses, and sent messengers with good tidings and warnings so mankind has no argument.
Allah bears witness to what He revealed to the Prophet, sent down with His knowledge, and the angels bear witness too.
Those who disbelieve, avert people from Allah's way and do wrong have strayed far; Allah will not forgive or guide them except to Hell forever.
Mankind is told the Messenger has brought the truth from their Lord, so believing is better; if they disbelieve, everything in the heavens and earth belongs to Allah.
The People of the Scripture are told the Messiah Jesus was only Allah's messenger and word, Allah is one with no son, and the Messiah never disdained serving Allah.
Mankind has received conclusive proof and a clear light from their Lord; those who believe and hold fast to Allah will be given mercy and guided on a straight path.
Allah rules on one with neither descendants nor ascendants: a lone sister gets half, two sisters two-thirds, and with brothers and sisters the male gets two females' share.
Believers must fulfill contracts; grazing livestock is lawful to them except what is recited, but hunting is not permitted while in ihram.
Believers must not violate Allah's rites, the sacred month, the sacrificial animals or those coming to the Sacred House, nor let hatred drive them to transgress, but cooperate in righteousness.
Dead animals, blood and pork are forbidden and the religion is perfected; good foods, the food of those given the Scripture and marriage to their chaste women are lawful.
For prayer, wash faces, arms to elbows and feet to ankles and wipe heads; purify after janabah, and without water wipe with clean earth, for Allah wants no hardship.
Remember Allah's favor and the covenant He took when believers said, 'We hear and we obey', and fear Allah, who knows what is in hearts.
Believers must stand firm for Allah as just witnesses and not let hatred of a people stop them being just, for justice is nearer to righteousness.
Believers who do righteous deeds are promised forgiveness and great reward, while those who disbelieve and deny Allah's signs are companions of Hellfire.
Remember Allah's favor when a people meant to attack the believers and He held back their hands, so fear Allah and rely on Him.
Allah took a covenant from the Children of Israel with twelve leaders; they broke it, were cursed and distort words, and those calling themselves Christians also forgot part of theirs.
Allah's Messenger has come to the People of the Scripture revealing much they concealed, with a light and a clear Book by which Allah guides those seeking His pleasure.
Those who say Allah is the Messiah, son of Mary, have disbelieved; none could stop Allah if He willed to destroy him, his mother and everyone on earth.
The Jews and Christians claim to be Allah's children and beloved; they are asked why then He punishes them, since they are humans He created.
After a gap between messengers, Allah's Messenger has come to the People of the Scripture as a bringer of good tidings and a warner, leaving them no excuse.
Moses urged his people to remember Allah's favors and enter the Holy Land; they refused while a mighty people held it, so they wandered forty years barred from it.
Adam's son whose offering was rejected killed his brother, who would not raise his hand against him; a crow showed him how to hide the body, and he regretted it.
Allah decreed for the Children of Israel that killing a soul, except for a soul or corruption, is like killing all mankind, and saving one like saving all mankind.
The penalty for waging war on Allah and His Messenger and spreading corruption is death, crucifixion, cutting off opposite hands and feet, or exile, unless they repent before capture.
Believers are told to fear Allah, seek the means of nearness to Him and strive in His cause so they may succeed.
Even the whole earth twice over would not ransom disbelievers from the punishment of the Day of Resurrection; they will wish to leave the Fire but never will.
The hands of a male or female thief are cut off as recompense and deterrent from Allah, but Allah forgives whoever repents after wrongdoing and reforms.
To Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and earth; He punishes and forgives whom He wills and is competent over all things.
The Messenger should not grieve over those who say 'We believe' without belief and some Jews, who listen to falsehood, distort words and seek his judgement despite having the Torah.
Allah sent down the Torah with guidance and light, by which prophets, rabbis and scholars judged; those who do not judge by what Allah revealed are the disbelievers.
The Torah prescribed a life for a life, an eye for an eye and retribution for wounds; forgoing it is expiation, and those not judging by Allah's revelation are wrongdoers.
Allah sent Jesus, son of Mary, confirming the Torah and gave him the Gospel with guidance and light; its people must judge by it, or they are defiantly disobedient.
The Prophet was given the Book confirming earlier Scripture, to judge by it and not follow others' inclinations; each was given a law, and none judges better than Allah.
Believers must not take Jews and Christians as allies, who are allies of one another; those with diseased hearts hasten to them fearing misfortune and will come to regret it.
Whoever reverts from his religion, Allah will bring a people He loves and who love Him, humble to believers, powerful against disbelievers, striving and fearless of blame.
Allah, His Messenger and believers who pray and give zakah are the believers' only allies, not those who ridicule their religion and the call to prayer.
The People of the Scripture resent believers; many hasten to sin unchecked by their scholars, the Jews called Allah's hand chained, and upholding the Torah and Gospel would bring provision.
The Messenger is told to convey what was revealed to him, or he has not delivered Allah's message, and Allah will protect him from the people.
The People of the Scripture stand on nothing until they uphold the Torah, the Gospel and their revelation; the Prophet's revelation increases many of them in disbelief.
Believers, Jews, Sabeans and Christians who believe in Allah and the Last Day and do righteousness will have no fear and will not grieve.
Allah took the Children of Israel's covenant and sent messengers; some they denied and some they killed, and thinking no punishment would follow, they became blind and deaf.
Those calling Allah the Messiah or the third of three disbelieve; the Messiah, who told the Children of Israel to worship Allah, was only a messenger who ate food.
People are asked why they worship besides Allah what cannot harm or benefit them, and the People of the Scripture are told not to exceed limits in religion.
The disbelievers among the Children of Israel were cursed by the tongue of David and Jesus for disobeying and not forbidding wrong, and many took disbelievers as allies.
The Jews and polytheists are most hostile to believers, while those calling themselves Christians are nearest in affection; some weep at the revelation, believe and are rewarded with gardens.
Believers must not forbid the good things Allah made lawful, nor transgress, but eat what He provided that is lawful and good, and fear Him.
Allah does not blame meaningless oaths, but a broken intended oath is expiated by feeding or clothing ten needy people, freeing a slave, or fasting three days.
Intoxicants, gambling, stone altars and divining arrows are Satan's defilement, used to stir hatred and turn people from remembering Allah and prayer; avoid them and obey Allah and the Messenger.
Allah tests believers with game within reach; killing game in ihram is forbidden and requires an equivalent offering, feeding the needy or fasting, while sea game is lawful.
Allah made the Ka'bah, the Sacred House, standing for the people and sanctified the sacred months and sacrificial animals, so people know He knows all things.
Allah is severe in penalty yet Forgiving and Merciful; the Messenger's duty is only to deliver, and Allah knows what people reveal and conceal.
The evil and the good are not equal, even if the abundance of evil impresses, so those of understanding should fear Allah.
Believers should not ask about things that would distress them if shown; a people before asked such questions and then became disbelievers.
Allah did not appoint bahirah, sa'ibah, wasilah or ham; disbelievers invent lies about Allah and hold to their fathers' ways even though their fathers knew nothing.
Believers are responsible for themselves; those who have strayed cannot harm them once guided, and all will return to Allah to be told their deeds.
When death approaches at a bequest, two just witnesses are taken and sworn by Allah if doubted; if found guilty of perjury, two others with rightful claim swear instead.
On the Day Allah assembles the messengers and asks their response, they will say they have no knowledge and that He knows the unseen.
Allah will remind Jesus of His favors, the disciples' faith and their request for a table from heaven; Jesus will deny telling people to worship him and his mother.
On that Day the truthful benefit from their truthfulness, with gardens beneath which rivers flow forever, Allah pleased with them and they with Him.
To Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and earth and all within them, and He is competent over all things.
Praise is due to Allah, who created the heavens, the earth, darkness and light, and created people from clay with a set term, yet the disbelievers equate others with Him.
He is Allah in the heavens and the earth, knowing what people keep secret, what they make public and what they earn.
They turn from every sign and mock the truth, though generations before were destroyed for their sins; even a written scripture would be called magic, and they demand an angel.
Messengers before were ridiculed and the mockers were overtaken by what they mocked; travel through the land and see the end of the deniers.
Everything in the heavens and earth belongs to Allah; He has decreed mercy upon Himself, will assemble all on the Day of Resurrection, and hears and knows all.
The Prophet takes no protector but Allah, fears the punishment of a tremendous Day, knows only Allah removes harm, and declares Him one God, with the Quran revealed to warn.
Those given the Scripture recognize it as they recognize their own sons, but those who lose themselves will not believe.
No one is more unjust than one who invents a lie about Allah or denies His verses, and the wrongdoers will not succeed.
On the Day of gathering the polytheists will be asked where their claimed partners are, and they will swear they never associated others, lying about themselves.
Some listen with covered hearts and deaf ears, would not believe any sign, call the revelation legends of former peoples, and keep others away from the Prophet, destroying only themselves.
Standing before the Fire, they will wish to be returned and not deny the signs, but if returned they would repeat what was forbidden, for they are liars.
They say there is only worldly life and no resurrection, yet before their Lord they will admit the truth, taste punishment, and regret when the Hour comes suddenly.
Worldly life is only amusement and diversion, while the home of the Hereafter is better for those who fear Allah.
They reject Allah's verses, not the Prophet; earlier messengers bore denial patiently, had Allah willed He would have united them on guidance, and only those who hear respond.
Allah can send the sign they demand; every creature and bird forms a community gathered to its Lord, while deniers of His verses are deaf and dumb in darkness.
If Allah's punishment or the Hour came, people would invoke Him alone, and He would remove it if He willed, while they forget what they associated with Him.
Nations before were seized with poverty and hardship to humble them; when they hardened and forgot, Allah opened every good to them, then seized them suddenly and eliminated the wrongdoers.
If Allah took away hearing and sight and sealed hearts, no other deity could restore them; and if His punishment came, only the wrongdoing people would be destroyed.
Messengers are sent only to bring good tidings and warn: believers who reform have no fear or grief, while those who deny the verses will be punished.
The Prophet says he holds no depositories of Allah, does not know the unseen and is not an angel; he only follows what is revealed to him.
The Prophet is told to warn with the Quran those who fear the gathering, not to send away those who call on their Lord, and to greet believers with peace.
The Prophet declares he is forbidden to worship what they invoke, stands on clear evidence from his Lord, and does not hold what they impatiently demand; the decision is Allah's.
Allah holds the keys of the unseen and knows everything on land and in the sea, every falling leaf and grain, all written in a clear record.
Allah takes souls by night and revives people by day until their term ends; guardian angels watch them until His messengers take them at death, and all return to Him.
Allah alone rescues people from the darknesses of land and sea, yet they associate others; He can send affliction from above or below or confuse them into sects.
The Prophet's people deny the truth; he is to turn from those who talk offensively of the verses, leave those who take religion as amusement, and remind with the Quran.
Believers will not invoke what neither benefits nor harms after Allah has guided them, for Allah's guidance is the only guidance; they are commanded to submit, pray and fear Him.
Allah created the heavens and earth in truth; when He says Be, it is, His is the dominion on the Day the Horn is blown, and He knows the unseen.
Abraham rebukes his father Azar for taking idols, sees a star, the moon and the sun set, turns to the Creator alone, and argues with his people.
Allah guided Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, Noah, David, Solomon, Job, Joseph, Moses, Aaron, Zechariah, John, Jesus, Elias, Ishmael, Elisha, Jonah and Lot; follow their guidance.
Those who say Allah revealed nothing to a human are asked who revealed the Scripture Moses brought, which they make into pages, showing some and concealing much.
This blessed Book confirms what came before, to warn the Mother of Cities and those around it; those who believe in the Hereafter believe in it and maintain their prayers.
No one is more unjust than one who falsely claims revelation; at death the angels demand the wrongdoers' souls, and they come to Allah alone, without their claimed intercessors.
Allah splits grain and seed, brings the living from the dead, makes the night, sun, moon and stars, produced people from one soul, and sends rain for crops and fruit.
They make the jinn partners with Allah and invent sons and daughters for Him, but He has no companion or son; there is no deity except Him, the Creator.
Insight has come from Allah, so whoever sees benefits himself; the verses are varied so the disbelievers say the Prophet studied, and to make the Quran clear.
The Prophet is told to follow what is revealed to him and turn from those who associate others with Allah, for he is not their guardian or manager.
Do not insult those they invoke besides Allah, lest they insult Allah in enmity without knowledge; every community's deeds are made pleasing to it.
They swear they would believe if a sign came, but they would not, even if angels came down and the dead spoke to them, unless Allah willed.
Every prophet was given enemies, devils from mankind and jinn, who inspire one another with decorative speech that draws those who disbelieve in the Hereafter.
Allah has revealed the Book explained in detail, and those given the Scripture know it is true; His word is fulfilled in truth and justice, and none can alter it.
Most people on earth would mislead from Allah's way, following only assumption, and Allah knows best who strays from His way and who is guided.
Eat what Allah's name has been mentioned over and not what it has not; what is forbidden is detailed except under compulsion, and leave sin, apparent and concealed.
One who was dead and given life and light to walk among people is not like one in darkness who never emerges.
Every city has its greatest criminals conspiring, but only against themselves; they demand what the messengers were given and will suffer debasement and severe punishment.
Allah opens the breast of whom He would guide to Islam and constricts whom He would misguide; His path is straight, and those who remember have the Home of Peace.
On the Day of gathering, the jinn and their human allies who made use of each other will be told the Fire is their eternal residence.
Jinn and mankind will admit messengers came to warn them; Allah would not destroy cities for wrongdoing while their people were unaware, and all have degrees by their deeds.
Allah is free of need and merciful, able to replace people with others; what is promised is coming, and the wrongdoers will not succeed.
The polytheists assign shares of crops and livestock to their partners, kill their children, and forbid animals by their own claim, inventing lies about Allah, and so have lost.
Eat of the crops and livestock without excess; their bans are questioned, and the Prophet's revelation forbids only carrion, spilled blood, swine and what is dedicated to other than Allah.
The polytheists will say that had Allah willed they would not have associated; they follow assumption, and if they bring witnesses to their bans, do not testify with them.
Allah instructs: associate nothing with Him, be good to parents, kill no child for poverty nor any soul unlawfully, avoid immoralities, guard orphans' property, give full measure, follow His path.
Allah gave Moses the Scripture, completing His favor, explaining all things, as guidance and mercy so that they might believe in meeting their Lord.
This blessed Book was revealed so none could say Scripture came only to two groups before, or that they would have been better guided; whoever turns from it is punished.
They wait for angels, their Lord or signs, but when some signs come, faith will not benefit a soul that had not believed before or earned good through it.
The Prophet has nothing to do with those who divided their religion into sects; their affair is with Allah, who will inform them of what they did.
Whoever comes with a good deed will have ten like it, and whoever comes with an evil deed is recompensed only its like, and none will be wronged.
The Prophet declares his religion is the straight way of Abraham, his prayer, sacrifice, life and death are for Allah alone, and each soul bears only its own burden.
Allah made people successors on earth and raised some above others in rank to test them through what He gave; He is swift in penalty, yet Forgiving and Merciful.
After the letters Alif Lam Meem Sad, the Book is revealed to the Prophet to warn and remind believers, and people are told to follow it and no other allies.
Many cities were destroyed, the punishment coming at night or while they slept at noon, and their only cry was that they had been wrongdoers.
Those sent messengers and the messengers themselves will be questioned, deeds will be related and weighed in truth: heavy scales bring success, light scales loss.
Allah established people on earth and made livelihood for them there, yet little are they grateful.
Iblees refuses to prostrate to Adam and vows to waylay people; Satan deceives Adam and his wife into eating from the tree, and they repent and descend to earth.
Allah gave the children of Adam clothing to conceal their private parts and as adornment, but the clothing of righteousness is best.
The children of Adam are warned not to let Satan tempt them as he removed their parents from Paradise; he and his tribe see them from where they cannot see.
They excuse immorality by their fathers and claim Allah ordered it, but Allah orders justice and sincere worship; some are guided, others took devils as allies.

Take adornment at every masjid, eat and drink without excess; Allah's adornment and good provision are not forbidden, only immoralities, sin, oppression, associating partners and speaking of Him without knowledge.
Every nation has a term, and when its time comes they can neither delay it by an hour nor bring it forward.
When messengers bring the children of Adam Allah's verses, those who fear Him and reform have no fear or grief, while those who deny them arrogantly abide in the Fire.
Those who lie about Allah or deny His verses admit disbelief at death, enter the Fire cursing each other, and never enter Paradise until a camel passes a needle's eye.
Those who believe and do righteous deeds abide in Paradise, freed of resentment, praising Allah for guiding them and told they inherited it for what they did.
Across a partition, the people of Paradise and of the Fire call to each other, the men on its elevations address both, and the Fire's people beg for water.
Allah brought them a detailed Book as guidance and mercy; when its outcome comes, those who ignored it will wish for intercessors or a return, but have lost themselves.
Allah created the heavens and earth in six days, then established Himself above the Throne; the night, day, sun, moon and stars are subjected by His command.
Call upon your Lord humbly and privately, in fear and aspiration, and cause no corruption on earth; Allah's mercy is near to the doers of good.
Allah sends winds and rain to a dead land and brings forth fruits, and so He will bring forth the dead; good land yields growth, bad land only sparsely.
Noah calls his people to worship Allah alone; their leaders say he is in clear error, and those who deny him are drowned while he is saved in the ship.
Hud calls 'Aad to worship Allah alone; their leaders call him foolish and a liar and cling to their fathers' worship, so the deniers are eliminated and he is saved.
Salih brings Thamud the she-camel of Allah as a sign; the arrogant leaders reject him, hamstring the camel and challenge him, and the earthquake seizes them.
Lot's people approach men with desire instead of women; rebuked, they call to evict him, but he and his family except his wife are saved, and rain falls on them.
Shu'ayb tells Madyan to worship Allah, give full measure and stop averting believers; the leaders threaten to evict him unless he returns to their religion, and the earthquake seizes them.
Cities that denied their prophets were tried with hardship, then ease, then seized suddenly; had they believed, blessings would have opened, and none should feel secure from Allah's plan.
Moses, sent with signs to Pharaoh, asks him to send the Children of Israel with him; when Pharaoh demands a sign, Moses' staff becomes a serpent and his hand white.
Pharaoh's chiefs call Moses a magician and magicians are gathered; his staff devours their magic, and the magicians believe, praying for patience under Pharaoh's threat to crucify them.
Urged by his chiefs, Pharaoh vows to kill the sons of Moses' people and keep their women alive; Moses tells his people to seek help through Allah and be patient.
Pharaoh's people suffer famine, flood, locusts, lice, frogs and blood, break their word to believe, and are drowned, while the oppressed Children of Israel inherit the blessed land.
After crossing the sea, the Children of Israel ask Moses for a god like the idol-worshippers' gods; he rebukes them, and Allah reminds them of their rescue from Pharaoh's people.
Moses keeps his forty-night appointment, leaving Aaron in his place, asks to see his Lord, falls unconscious when the mountain is leveled, repents, and receives the tablets.
Allah turns away from His signs the arrogant, who take the way of error; the deeds of those who deny His signs and the meeting of the Hereafter are worthless.
Moses' people worship a calf; Moses returns angry, throws down the tablets and prays for forgiveness; when the earthquake seizes his seventy men, Allah says His mercy encompasses all things.
Those who follow the unlettered prophet, written of in the Torah and Gospel, will succeed; he declares he is Allah's Messenger to all mankind, to be believed and followed.
Among Moses' people is a community guiding by truth; Allah divided them into twelve tribes, gave them water, manna and quails, and punished those who changed the words given them.
The people of the town by the sea transgressed over the sabbath when fish came openly that day; those who forbade evil were saved and the transgressors made despised apes.
Allah declared He would send upon them, until Resurrection, those who afflict them; He scattered them as nations, their successors took worldly gain, and He raised the mountain over them.
Allah took from the children of Adam their descendants and made them testify He is their Lord, so they cannot plead unawareness or blame their fathers' associating.
One given Allah's signs detached from them, was pursued by Satan and followed his desire, like a dog panting whether chased or left: the example of deniers of the signs.
Whom Allah guides is guided and whom He sends astray is lost; many jinn and people are made for Hell, with hearts, eyes and ears they do not use.
To Allah belong the best names, so invoke Him by them and leave those who deviate concerning His names.
Among those Allah created is a community that guides by truth and by it establishes justice.
Deniers of the signs are led on gradually and given time; their companion is no madman but a warner, and whom Allah sends astray has no guide.
Asked when the Hour will come, the Prophet says its knowledge is only with Allah; it weighs on the heavens and earth and will come unexpectedly.
The Prophet holds no power to benefit or harm himself except as Allah wills, does not know the unseen, and is only a warner and bringer of good tidings.
Allah created people from one soul and its mate; a couple who prayed for a good child ascribe partners to Him in what He gave them.
The partners they associate create nothing and are created, cannot help their worshippers or themselves, have no feet, hands, eyes or ears, and cannot hear a call to guidance.
The Prophet is told to take what is given freely, pardoning people, to enjoin what is good, and to turn away from the ignorant.
When an evil suggestion comes from Satan, seek refuge in Allah; those who fear Allah remember Him and see clearly, while the devils increase their brothers in error.
Asked why he has not contrived a sign, the Prophet says he only follows revelation; the Quran is insight, guidance and mercy, so listen attentively when it is recited.
Remember your Lord within yourself humbly and in fear, quietly, morning and evening; those near your Lord are not too arrogant to worship, exalt and prostrate to Him.
Asked about the bounties of war, the Prophet says they belong to Allah and the Messenger, and the believers are told to fear Allah, set things right and obey.
True believers fear when Allah is mentioned, grow in faith when His verses are recited, rely on Him, pray and spend; they have ranks, forgiveness and noble provision.
Some believers were reluctant to go out, but Allah promised them one of two groups, sent a thousand angels, drowsiness and rain, and cast terror into the disbelievers.
Believers must not turn their backs on advancing disbelievers, except as a tactic or to join another company; whoever flees returns with Allah's anger, and Hell is his refuge.
It was Allah, not the believers, who killed them and threw, to test the believers and weaken the disbelievers' plot; if the disbelievers desist, it is better for them.
Believers are told to obey Allah and His Messenger and respond to his call, not to be like those who say they hear but do not, the worst of creatures.
Fear a trial that will not strike only the wrongdoers among you, and know that Allah is severe in penalty.
Believers are reminded how Allah sheltered and supported them when they were few and oppressed and provided them good things, so that they might be grateful.
Believers must not betray Allah and the Messenger, nor knowingly betray their trusts.
Your properties and your children are only a trial, and with Allah is a great reward.
If believers fear Allah, He will give them a criterion, remove their misdeeds and forgive them.
The disbelievers plotted to restrain, kill or evict the Prophet, but Allah also plans, and He is the best of planners.
They boast they could say the like of the verses, call them legends and ask for stones from the sky; Allah would not punish them with the Prophet among them.
They deserve punishment for barring people from al-Masjid al-Haram, whose guardians they are not; they spend wealth to avert from Allah's way and will be gathered to Hell.
If disbelievers cease, their past is forgiven; fight them until there is no fitnah and religion is all for Allah, and if they turn away, Allah is the believers' protector.
A fifth of war booty belongs to Allah, the Messenger, his near relatives, orphans, the needy and the stranded traveler.
Allah brought the two sides together in the valley and made each appear few to the other, even in the Prophet's dream, to accomplish a matter already destined.
When meeting an enemy company, believers must stand firm, remember Allah much, obey Allah and His Messenger, avoid disputes that sap their strength, and be patient.
Believers must not be like those who marched out boastfully to be seen; Satan made their deeds pleasing and promised protection, but disowned them when the two armies met.
The hypocrites and those with disease in their hearts said the believers were deluded by their religion, but whoever relies on Allah finds Him Exalted in Might and Wise.
The angels take the souls of the disbelievers, striking their faces and backs, telling them to taste the burning Fire for what their hands put forth.
Like Pharaoh's people and those before them, they denied Allah's signs and were destroyed for their sins; Allah does not change a favor on a people until they change themselves.
The worst creatures are those who disbelieve and break their treaty every time; if betrayal is feared from a people, throw their treaty back to them on equal terms.
The disbelievers will not escape; prepare whatever power and war steeds you can to terrify the enemy of Allah and your enemy, and spending in Allah's cause is repaid.
If they incline to peace, incline to it and rely on Allah; He suffices against their deception, having supported the Prophet and brought the believers' hearts together.
Allah suffices the Prophet and his believing followers; he is to urge them to battle, twenty steadfast overcoming two hundred, later lightened so a hundred overcome two hundred.
A prophet is not to hold captives until he has inflicted a massacre in the land; the booty is lawful, and captives with good in their hearts are promised better.
Emigrant believers who fought and those who sheltered and aided them are allies of one another, unlike believers who did not emigrate; disbelievers too are allies of one another.
Those who emigrated and fought and those who sheltered them are the true believers; later emigrants are of them, and blood relatives are more entitled to one another.
Allah and His Messenger declare disassociation from the polytheists they had treaties with, giving them four months, but treaties with those who kept them are honored to their term.
When the sacred months pass, kill, capture and besiege the polytheists unless they repent, pray and give zakah; one who seeks protection is granted it and escorted to safety.
Only treaties made at al-Masjid al-Haram hold with polytheists, while they stay upright; they keep no pact toward believers, yet if they repent, pray and give zakah, they are brothers.
If they break oaths and defame the religion, fight the leaders of disbelief; the oath-breakers who sought to expel the Messenger began first; Allah will punish them by your hands.
Believers will not be left until Allah makes evident who strives and takes no intimates besides Allah, His Messenger and the believers.
Polytheists, witnessing against themselves with disbelief, may not maintain Allah's mosques; only those who believe in Allah and the Last Day, pray, give zakah and fear only Allah should.
Giving pilgrims water and maintaining al-Masjid al-Haram do not equal believing and striving; those who believed, emigrated and strove with wealth and lives are greater, promised mercy and gardens.
Believers must not take fathers or brothers who prefer disbelief as allies, and are warned if family, wealth, trade or homes are dearer than Allah, His Messenger and jihad.
At Hunayn their great numbers did not help and they fled, until Allah sent down tranquillity and unseen soldiers and punished the disbelievers; He accepts repentance from whom He wills.
The polytheists are unclean and may not approach al-Masjid al-Haram after this year; if believers fear poverty, Allah will enrich them from His bounty if He wills.
Fight those given the Scripture who neither believe in Allah and the Last Day, nor forbid what Allah forbade, nor follow the true religion, until they pay the jizyah, humbled.
The Jews say Ezra is the son of Allah and the Christians say the Messiah is the son of Allah, words of their mouths imitating earlier disbelievers.
They took their scholars, monks and the Messiah as lords besides Allah and want to extinguish His light, and hoarders of gold and silver will be seared with it.
Allah's register has twelve months, four of them sacred, in which not to wrong yourselves; fight the disbelievers collectively as they fight you, and postponing sacred months increases disbelief.
Believers who cling to the earth when told to go forth are warned; Allah aided the Prophet in the cave, so go forth and strive with wealth and lives.
Hypocrites would have joined an easy trip but swore false excuses to avoid the long journey to Tabuk; the Prophet is asked why he excused them, as only doubters ask.
The hypocrites are distressed when good befalls the Prophet and rejoice at his misfortune; believers say only what Allah has decreed will strike them, and they rely on Him.
Their spending is not accepted because they disbelieve, come to prayer lazily and give unwillingly; they swear they belong to the believers, and some criticize how charities are distributed.
Zakah is for the poor, the needy, its collectors, bringing hearts together, freeing captives, debtors, the cause of Allah and the stranded traveler, an obligation from Allah.
Hypocrites abuse the Prophet, swear to please the believers, call their mocking of Allah's verses mere play, and hypocrite men and women, enjoining wrong, are promised Hell.
Like earlier, stronger and richer peoples, they enjoy their portion and their deeds become worthless; the peoples of Noah, 'Aad, Thamud, Abraham, Madyan and the overturned towns wronged themselves.
Believing men and women are allies of one another, enjoining right, praying, giving zakah and obeying; Allah promises them gardens and His approval, which is greater.
The Prophet is told to fight the disbelievers and hypocrites; some swore falsely, broke a pledge to give charity, ridiculed those who gave, and will not be forgiven.
Those who stayed behind from Tabuk rejoiced, saying do not go out in the heat; they may never go out with the Prophet, nor may he pray over their dead.
The Messenger and those who believed with him fought with their wealth and lives; for them are good things, success and gardens beneath which rivers flow.
No blame is on the weak, the ill, those with nothing to spend, or those who wept for want of mounts, but on the rich who asked to stay behind.
Hypocrites will make excuses and swear when the believers return, to be left alone; they are not believed, their refuge is Hell, and Allah is not satisfied with them.
The bedouins are stronger in disbelief and hypocrisy; some count their spending a loss, while others believe and count it a means of nearness to Allah.
Allah is pleased with the first forerunners among the Muhajireen and the Ansar and those who followed them in good conduct, and has prepared gardens for them.
Among the bedouins around and the people of Madinah are hypocrites the Prophet does not know but Allah knows; they will be punished twice, then a great punishment.
Others admitted their sins, having mixed good and bad deeds; the Prophet takes charity to purify them, Allah accepts repentance and sees all deeds, and some await His decision.
Do not pray in a mosque taken for harm, disbelief and division; one founded on righteousness from the first day is worthier, unlike a building on a crumbling bank.
Allah has bought the believers' lives and wealth for Paradise as they fight in His cause, promised in the Torah, Gospel and Quran; they repent, worship and keep His limits.
The Prophet and believers are not to ask forgiveness for polytheists, even relatives, once clearly for Hellfire; Abraham disassociated from his father once he saw him as Allah's enemy.
Allah does not let a people stray after guiding them until He makes clear to them what they should avoid.
To Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth; He gives life and causes death, and besides Him there is no protector or helper.
Allah forgave the Prophet, the Muhajireen and the Ansar who followed him in the hour of difficulty, and the three left behind once the earth closed in on them.
Believers are told to fear Allah and be with those who are true.
Madinah and nearby bedouins should not stay behind the Messenger, as every hardship in Allah's cause is recorded; yet not all should go, some staying to learn religion and warn.
Believers are told to fight the disbelievers adjacent to them and let them find harshness, knowing that Allah is with the righteous.
Each revealed surah increases believers in faith but adds evil to those with diseased hearts; tested every year, they neither repent nor remember, and slip away when a surah comes.
A Messenger has come from among them, grieved by their suffering, kind and merciful to believers; if they turn away, he relies on Allah, Lord of the Great Throne.
These are verses of the wise Book; people are amazed that a man among them was told to warn and give good tidings, and the disbelievers call him a magician.
Allah created the heavens and the earth in six days, established Himself above the Throne and arranges every matter; none intercedes without His permission, so worship Him.
All return to Allah; He begins creation and repeats it to reward justly those who believed and did righteous deeds, while disbelievers get scalding water and painful punishment.
Allah made the sun a shining light and the moon a light with phases for counting years; the alternation of night and day and all He created are signs.
Those content with this world and heedless of the signs end in the Fire; righteous believers are in Gardens, glorifying Allah, greeting with peace, praising the Lord of the worlds.
If Allah hastened the evil people invoke as He hastens good, their term would end; man calls on Him in affliction, then, relieved, carries on as if he never called.
Generations before were destroyed when they did wrong and would not believe their messengers' clear proofs; then you were made successors in the land to see how you would act.
Asked for a different Qur'an, the Prophet says he only follows revelation and lived among them a lifetime before it; none is more unjust than one who lies about Allah.
They worship besides Allah what neither harms nor benefits them, calling these their intercessors, as if informing Allah of something He does not know.
Mankind was one community and then differed; but for a word that preceded from the Lord, their differences would already have been judged.
They ask why no sign is sent down to him from his Lord; he is told to say the unseen belongs to Allah, so wait, and he waits with them.
Given mercy after adversity, people plot against Allah's verses; caught by a storm at sea they pray to Him sincerely, then commit injustice on earth once He saves them.
Worldly life is like rain that makes the earth bloom until, when its people think they control it, Allah's command makes it a harvest as if it never flourished.
Allah invites to the Home of Peace; those who do good have the best reward and more in Paradise; evildoers are repaid in kind, faces darkened, in the Fire forever.
On the Day all are gathered, the 'partners' say they were unaware of being worshipped, and every soul is tried for its deeds and returned to Allah.
Allah provides, controls hearing and sight, brings the living from the dead and arranges every matter; none of their 'partners' begins creation or guides to truth, and most follow assumption.
This Qur'an could only come from Allah and confirms earlier scripture; deniers are challenged to bring one surah like it, and some believe in it while others do not.
If they deny the Prophet, each has his own deeds; some listen and look but are like the deaf and blind he cannot guide, and Allah wrongs no one.
When gathered, they will feel they stayed an hour; each nation is judged justly when its messenger comes; deniers ask when the promise comes, and wrongdoers will taste eternal punishment.
Asked if resurrection is true, the Prophet swears it is; wrongdoers would offer all on earth as ransom; Allah owns all, gives life and death, and all return to Him.
