Instruction, healing for the breasts, guidance and mercy have come from the Lord; people should rejoice in Allah's bounty and mercy, which is better than what they accumulate.
People are asked whether Allah permitted them to make some of His provision lawful and some unlawful, or whether they invent lies about Him.
Allah witnesses every deed and every recitation of the Qur'an; not an atom's weight in the earth or heaven is absent from Him, and all is in a clear register.
The allies of Allah, who believed and feared Him, have no fear and will not grieve, and have good tidings in this life and the Hereafter.
Do not be grieved by their speech, for all honor belongs to Allah and all in the heavens and earth are His; those who invoke 'partners' follow only assumption.
Allah made the night for rest and the day for sight; in that are signs for people who listen.
They say Allah has taken a son, but He is exalted and free of need; those who invent lies about Allah will not succeed and will taste severe punishment.
Noah tells his people he relies on Allah and asks no payment; they deny him, so Allah saves him and those with him in the ship and drowns the deniers.
Messengers were sent after Noah to their peoples with clear proofs, but they would not believe what they had denied before.
Moses and Aaron bring signs to Pharaoh and his establishment, who call them magic; few believe, and Pharaoh drowns pursuing the Children of Israel, his body saved as a sign.
The Children of Israel were settled in a good place and provided for; they differed only after knowledge came, and Allah will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection.
If in doubt about what was revealed, ask those who read the Scripture before; the truth has come from the Lord, so never doubt or deny the signs of Allah.
Those on whom the word of the Lord has come into effect will not believe, even if every sign comes to them, until they see the painful punishment.
No city's belief benefited it except the people of Jonah: when they believed, the punishment of disgrace was removed from them and they were given enjoyment for a time.
Had the Lord willed, all on earth would have believed; the Prophet is asked whether he would compel people to believe, and no soul believes except by Allah's permission.
The Prophet tells them to observe the heavens and earth, but signs avail nothing for disbelievers, who await only what befell those before; Allah saves His messengers and believers.
The Prophet worships only Allah, never what they worship, and must not invoke what cannot benefit or harm, for only Allah removes adversity and none can repel His bounty.
The truth has come from the Lord; guidance or straying affects only one's own soul, and the Prophet follows the revelation and is patient until Allah judges.
A Book whose verses are perfected and detailed by One Wise and Acquainted, with the message to worship none but Allah, from a warner and bringer of good tidings.
Seek forgiveness and repent to the Lord for good provision for a set term; those who turn away are warned of a great Day, and all return to Allah.
The disbelievers turn away to hide, yet Allah knows what they conceal and declare; He provides for every creature and knows its dwelling and storage, all in a clear register.
Allah created the heavens and the earth in six days, His Throne upon water, to test who is best in deed; the disbelievers call resurrection after death obvious magic.
If the punishment is delayed, they ask what detains it; on the Day it comes it will not be averted, and what they ridiculed will envelop them.
Man despairs and is ungrateful when mercy is withdrawn and boastful when favor follows hardship, except those who are patient and do righteous deeds, who have forgiveness and great reward.
The Prophet, distressed by demands for a treasure or angel, is only a warner; if they cannot bring ten invented surahs like it, know the Qur'an came with Allah's knowledge.
Those who desire only this world's life and adornments are fully repaid in it, but in the Hereafter they have only the Fire, and what they did is lost.
Those upon clear evidence from their Lord, with the Scripture of Moses before it, believe in the Qur'an, while factions that disbelieve in it are promised the Fire.
Those who invent lies about Allah and avert people from His way will be presented before their Lord, cursed, their punishment multiplied, and in the Hereafter the greatest losers.
Those who believe, do righteous deeds and humble themselves to their Lord abide in Paradise; the two parties are like the blind and deaf against the seeing and hearing.
Noah calls his people to worship only Allah; the eminent reject him, calling his followers the lowest; he will not drive the believers away, and they demand the threatened punishment.
Interrupting the story, the Prophet answers the charge that he invented it: if he had, the crime would be his, but he is innocent of what they commit.
Told no others will believe, Noah builds the ship amid ridicule; the flood drowns the deniers and his son, the ship rests on Judiyy, and Noah disembarks in security.
Noah's story is news of the unseen revealed to the Prophet, unknown to him and his people before; so be patient, for the best outcome is for the righteous.
Hud calls 'Aad to worship Allah alone and seek forgiveness; they will not leave their gods, he relies on Allah, he and the believers are saved, and 'Aad are cursed.
Salih calls Thamud to worship Allah; they doubt him and hamstring the she-camel given as a sign, so Salih and the believers are saved and the shriek seizes the wrongdoers.
Messengers bring Abraham good tidings and do not touch his roasted calf; his wife is told of Isaac and Jacob; Abraham argues about Lot's people, but their punishment is decreed.
When messengers come to Lot, his people hasten to him; he offers his daughters, is told to leave by night with his family except his wife; the city is overturned.
Shu'ayb calls Madyan to worship Allah and give full measure and weight; they mock him and threaten him; he and the believers are saved and the shriek seizes the wrongdoers.
Moses is sent with signs to Pharaoh and his establishment, who follow Pharaoh's command; he will lead his people into the Fire, cursed here and on the Day of Resurrection.
These are the stories of cities, some still standing and some mown down; they wronged themselves, their gods did not help them, and the Lord's seizure is painful and severe.
A sign for those who fear the Hereafter's punishment: a witnessed Day when people are gathered, delayed only for a set term, when no soul speaks except by His permission.
The wretched will be in the Fire and the prosperous in Paradise, each abiding as long as the heavens and earth endure, except what the Lord wills.
Do not doubt what these people worship; they worship only as their fathers worshipped before, and they will be given their share in full.
Moses was given the Scripture and it came under disagreement; but for a preceding word they would have been judged, and the Lord will fully repay each for their deeds.
Stay on a right course as commanded, with those who turned back with you, do not transgress, and do not incline toward wrongdoers, lest the Fire touch you.
Establish prayer at both ends of the day and as night approaches; good deeds remove misdeeds; be patient, for Allah never lets the reward of doers of good be lost.
Few in the generations before forbade corruption, while the wrongdoers pursued their luxury; the Lord would not destroy cities unjustly while their people were reformers.
Had the Lord willed, mankind would be one community, but they keep differing, except those given mercy; His word to fill Hell with jinn and men will be fulfilled.
The stories of the messengers are related to make the heart firm, bringing the truth, an instruction and a reminder for the believers.
Disbelievers are told to work by their position and wait; to Allah belong the unseen of the heavens and earth and every matter, so worship Him and rely upon Him.
These are the verses of the clear Book, sent down as an Arabic Qur'an to be understood, relating the best of stories to one who was unaware before it.
Joseph dreams that eleven stars, the sun and the moon prostrate to him; his father tells him to keep it from his brothers and says his Lord will choose him.
Saying their father loves Joseph more, his brothers put him in a well and claim a wolf ate him; travelers find him, and he is sold for a few dirhams.
Bought by a man from Egypt, Joseph reaches maturity; the man's wife tries to seduce him, he refuses, and his shirt torn from the back shows she lied.
Women of the city blame al-'Azeez's wife; at her banquet they cut their hands on seeing Joseph; he prefers prison to their invitation and is imprisoned for a time.
Two prisoners ask Joseph to interpret their dreams; he calls them to worship Allah alone, says one will serve wine and one be crucified, and stays imprisoned several years.
The eminent ones cannot interpret the king's dream of seven fat cows eaten by seven lean; Joseph foretells seven years of planting, seven difficult years, then a year of rain.
The king summons Joseph, who asks about the women who cut their hands; al-'Azeez's wife admits she sought to seduce him, and Joseph asks to oversee the land's storehouses.
Joseph's brothers come to him without recognizing him; he tells them to bring their brother from their father, who demands their promise by Allah to bring him back.
Joseph tells his brother who he is and puts the king's measure in his bag; accused of theft, the brothers set the penalty, and Joseph keeps his brother.
Told his son has stolen, Jacob grieves for Joseph until his eyes whiten and sends his sons to seek him; Joseph reveals himself and forgives his brothers.
Joseph sends his shirt; Jacob finds Joseph's smell and regains sight from the shirt; the family enter Egypt, his parents prostrate to Joseph, and his earlier vision is fulfilled.
This news of the unseen is revealed to the Prophet, who was not there when they plotted; most people are not believers, yet he asks no payment for this reminder.
People pass by the signs in the heavens and earth, and most believe in Allah only while associating others; the Prophet invites to Allah with insight and associates none.
The messengers before were men of the cities given revelation; when they despaired, victory came and whoever Allah willed was saved, and His punishment is not turned from criminals.
Their stories hold a lesson for people of understanding; the Qur'an is no invented narration but confirms what came before, explains all things, and is guidance and mercy.
These are the verses of the Book; what has been revealed from the Lord is the truth, but most people do not believe.
Allah raised the heavens without visible pillars, subjected sun and moon, spread the earth with mountains, rivers and fruits, and makes crops watered by one water differ; these are signs.
They ask whether, once dust, they will be a new creation; those are the ones who disbelieved in their Lord, with shackles on their necks, abiding in the Fire.
They urge evil before good, though similar punishments came before; they ask why no sign is sent, yet he is only a warner, and every people has a guide.
Allah knows what every female carries, the unseen and the witnessed; concealed or open speech, and one hidden by night or seen by day, are alike to Him.
Angels guard each person by Allah's decree; He does not change a people's condition until they change themselves; He shows lightning, raises clouds and strikes with thunderbolts whom He wills.
Those called on besides Allah do not answer; all in the heavens and earth prostrate to Him; their allies own no benefit or harm; Allah is Creator of all things.
Like the foam on a torrent or on heated ore, falsehood vanishes while what benefits people remains; this is Allah's example of truth and falsehood.
Those who respond to their Lord, keep His covenant, are patient, pray and spend enter gardens greeted by angels; covenant-breakers who spread corruption get the curse and Hell.
Allah extends and restricts provision for whom He wills; people rejoice in the worldly life, though compared to the Hereafter it is only brief enjoyment.
To the demand for a sign, the answer is that Allah leaves astray whom He wills and guides those who turn to Him, whose hearts find assurance in His remembrance.
The Prophet recites revelation to those disbelieving in the Most Merciful; were any qur'an to move mountains or make the dead speak, it would be this; the affair is Allah's.
Messengers before were ridiculed too; Allah gave the disbelievers time, then seized them, and terrible was His penalty.
Allah maintains every soul, yet they attribute partners to Him; challenged to name them, they are averted from the way, and none guides whom Allah leaves astray.
Disbelievers face punishment in this world and worse in the Hereafter; the Paradise promised to the righteous has rivers, lasting fruit and shade, while the disbelievers' end is the Fire.
Some given the Scripture rejoice at the revelation while some factions deny part of it; it is revealed as an Arabic legislation, and their inclinations must not be followed.
Messengers before had wives and descendants and brought signs only by Allah's permission; Allah eliminates or confirms what He wills, and with Him is the Mother of the Book.
The Prophet's duty is only to convey, and the account is Allah's; He reduces the land from its borders, none can adjust His decision, and all planning belongs to Him.
The disbelievers say he is not a messenger; he answers that Allah, and whoever has knowledge of the Scripture, is sufficient witness between them.
A Book is revealed to bring mankind out of darknesses into the light, to Allah's path; woe to disbelievers who prefer this world and avert others from His way.
Every messenger was sent speaking his people's language to make things clear; Allah sends astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills.
Moses is sent to bring his people into the light and reminds them Allah saved them from Pharaoh's people; gratitude brings increase, denial severe punishment; Allah is free of need.
The peoples of Noah, 'Aad, Thamud and those after doubted their messengers and threatened to expel them; Allah promised to destroy the wrongdoers, and every obstinate tyrant faces Hell.
The deeds of those who disbelieve in their Lord are like ashes blown by the wind on a stormy day; they can keep nothing of what they earned.
Allah created the heavens and the earth in truth; if He wills He can do away with people and bring a new creation, and that is not difficult for Him.
All come out before Allah; the weak ask the arrogant to avail them against the punishment, and the arrogant say they have no escape, whether impatient or patient.
When the matter is concluded, Satan says he promised and betrayed, had no authority except to invite, and tells his followers to blame themselves, not him.
Those who believed and did righteous deeds are admitted to gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding forever by their Lord's permission, greeted with peace.
A good word is like a good tree, firmly rooted and always fruitful, and a bad word like an uprooted tree; Allah keeps believers firm with the firm word.
Those who exchanged Allah's favor for disbelief settled their people in Hell; they set up equals to Allah to mislead; let them enjoy themselves, for their destination is the Fire.
Believers are told to establish prayer and spend from what they are given, secretly and publicly, before a Day with no exchange and no friendships.
Allah created the heavens and earth, sends rain for fruits and subjected the ships, rivers, sun, moon, night and day; His favors cannot be counted, yet mankind is ungrateful.
Abraham prays for a secure city, protection from idol worship and provision for descendants settled near the sacred House, thanks Allah for Ishmael and Isaac, and asks forgiveness.
Allah delays the wrongdoers for a Day of staring eyes, when they will beg for respite; the earth and heavens are replaced, and criminals are shackled in garments of pitch.
This is a notification for people, that they be warned by it, know that He is one God, and that those of understanding be reminded.
These are the verses of the Book and a clear Qur'an.
Disbelievers may wish they had been Muslims; let them enjoy themselves; every nation has its term; they call the messenger mad and demand angels, sent down only with truth.
Allah sent down the Qur'an and will be its guardian.
Every messenger to the former peoples was ridiculed; denial enters the criminals' hearts, and even a gate opened into heaven would be called dazzled eyes and magic.
Allah placed stars in the heaven, protected it from devils pursued by flames, spread the earth with mountains and means of living, and sends winds and rain in known measure.
Allah gives life and causes death and is the Inheritor; He knows the earlier and the later generations and will gather them all.
Adam is created from black mud and the jinn from fire; Iblees refuses to prostrate to him, is expelled and reprieved, vows to mislead, and Hell awaits his followers.
The righteous will be in gardens and springs, entering in peace, freed of resentment, as brothers on thrones facing each other, never tired and never removed.
Allah's servants are told that He is the Forgiving, the Merciful, and that His punishment is the painful punishment.
Abraham's guests give him good tidings of a learned boy in his old age and say they are sent to criminals, sparing Lot's family except his wife.
The messengers tell Lot to leave by night; his people come rejoicing for his guests, and the shriek seizes them at sunrise as stones rain on the overturned city.
Shu'ayb's people, the companions of the thicket, were also wrongdoers, so Allah took retribution from them; their city and Lot's lie on a clear highway.
Thamud, Salih's people, denied the messengers and turned from the signs given them; secure in houses carved from mountains, they were seized by the shriek at early morning.
The heavens and the earth were created only in truth and the Hour is coming, so forgive graciously; the Lord is the Knowing Creator.
The Prophet is given seven often repeated verses and the great Qur'an, told not to covet the disbelievers' enjoyment, and those who made the Qur'an into portions will be questioned.
Declare what is commanded and turn away from the polytheists; Allah suffices against the mockers who make another deity with Him, and they will come to know.
Allah knows the Prophet's breast is constrained by what they say; he is told to exalt his Lord with praise, prostrate, and worship until certainty comes.
Allah's command is coming; He is above what they associate, and sends angels with inspiration to whom He wills, to warn that there is no deity but Him.
Allah created the heavens and earth, man from a sperm-drop, and livestock, horses, mules and donkeys that give people warmth, food, beauty, transport and riding.
Allah shows the right way while some paths deviate, and had He willed He could have guided everyone.
Allah sends rain and grows crops, and subjects night and day, sun, moon, stars and the sea; He set mountains, rivers, roads and landmarks so people are guided.
He who creates is not like one who does not; Allah's favors are countless, and those invoked besides Him create nothing, are created, and are dead.
Those who do not believe in the Hereafter are arrogant; they call the revelation legends of former peoples and will bear their own burdens and some of those they misguide.
Earlier plotters had the roof fall on them when Allah came at their building's foundations, and on Resurrection Day He will disgrace them and ask where their partners are.
Those taken in death while wronging themselves will enter the gates of Hell, while the righteous, greeted by the angels with peace at death, enter Paradise.
The disbelievers wait only for the angels or Allah's command, as those before them did, who wronged themselves and were overtaken by what they ridiculed.
Polytheists say that had Allah willed they would not have worshipped others; messengers only convey clearly, and one was sent to every nation: worship Allah and avoid Taghut.
They swear Allah will not raise the dead, but it is His true promise, to show them what they differed over; He says to a thing Be, and it is.
Those who emigrated for Allah after being wronged will be settled well in this world, with a greater reward in the Hereafter, being patient and relying on their Lord.
The messengers before were men given revelation, clear proofs and scriptures, and the message was revealed to the Prophet to make clear to people what was sent down.
Those who plan evil deeds should not feel safe from the earth swallowing them or punishment seizing them suddenly or gradually, yet your Lord is Kind and Merciful.
Shadows, all creatures in the heavens and earth, and the angels prostrate humbly to Allah, fearing their Lord above them and doing as they are commanded.
Allah forbids taking two deities, for He is one God; all in the heavens and earth is His, and worship is due to Him constantly.
People cry to Allah in hardship, yet once it is lifted some associate others with Him and give a share of His provision to what they do not know.
They attribute daughters to Allah, yet a man told of a female's birth darkens with grief, unsure whether to keep her in humiliation or bury her in the ground.
Allah defers punishment for wrongdoing to a fixed term; those attributing to Him what they dislike will have the Fire, and Satan, who beautified earlier nations' deeds, is their ally.
The Book was revealed to the Prophet only to make clear what they differed over, and as guidance and mercy for a believing people.
Rain revives the dead earth, livestock give pure milk, palms and vines yield intoxicant and good provision, and the bee, inspired by its Lord, produces a healing drink.
Allah creates people and then takes them in death, and some are returned to a decrepit old age, knowing nothing after having known.
Those favored in provision would not share it equally with those their right hands possess; Allah gave spouses, children and provision, yet they worship what provides nothing.
Allah contrasts a helpless owned slave with one who spends from good provision, and a dumb man who brings no good with one commanding justice on a straight path.
Allah owns the unseen of the heavens and earth; the command of the Hour is but a glance of the eye or nearer, for He is competent over all things.
Allah gives people hearing, sight and intellect, holds the birds aloft, and provides homes, tents, shade, shelter and garments; they recognize His favor, then deny it.
On the Day a witness is raised from every nation, disbelievers get no excuse, the partners they invoked call them liars, and the Prophet is witness over his nation.
Allah orders justice, good conduct and giving to relatives, and forbids immorality, bad conduct and oppression.
Fulfill Allah's covenant and do not break oaths or use them to deceive, like one unraveling her spun thread, nor sell it cheaply, for what Allah has lasts.
Whoever does righteousness, male or female, while a believer will be given a good life and rewarded for the best of what they did.
When reciting the Quran, seek refuge in Allah from Satan, who has no authority over believers who rely on their Lord, only over those who take him as an ally.
When a verse replaces another they call the Prophet an inventor taught by a human, but the Pure Spirit brought this clear Arabic Quran down from the Lord.
Whoever willingly disbelieves after believing, unlike one forced while his heart stays firm in faith, faces Allah's wrath for preferring this world; their hearts are sealed and they are losers.
Your Lord is Forgiving and Merciful to those who emigrated after being compelled to renounce their religion, then fought and were patient.
On the Day every soul will come disputing for itself, each will be fully repaid for what it did, and none will be wronged.
Allah gives the example of a safe, prosperous city that denied His favors and its messenger, so it tasted hunger and fear and was overtaken by punishment.
Eat what Allah provides, lawful and good; He forbids only dead animals, blood, swine and what is dedicated to others, and no one may falsely declare things lawful or unlawful.
Your Lord is Forgiving and Merciful to those who do wrong out of ignorance, then repent and reform.
Abraham was an obedient leader, upright and grateful, never a polytheist; Allah chose and guided him, and the Prophet was told to follow Abraham's upright religion.
The sabbath was appointed only for those who differed over it, and your Lord will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection.
Invite to your Lord's way with wisdom and good instruction and argue in the best way; your Lord knows best who has strayed and who is guided.
If you punish, match the harm done, but patience is better; the Prophet is told to be patient and not grieve, for Allah is with the God-fearing and good-doers.
Exalted is Allah, who took His Servant by night from al-Masjid al-Haram to al-Masjid al-Aqsa, whose surroundings He blessed, to show him His signs.
Moses' Scripture warned the Children of Israel they would twice cause corruption and each time face enemies sent by Allah; He may show mercy, but will return if they do.
This Quran guides to what is most suitable, gives believers who do good the news of a great reward, and warns deniers of the Hereafter of painful punishment.
Man prays for evil as he prays for good, for man is ever hasty.
Allah made night and day two signs, the day visible so people can seek His bounty and count the years, and He has set out everything in detail.
Each person's fate is fastened to his neck, and on Resurrection Day he reads his open record; no one bears another's burden, and Allah punishes none before sending a messenger.
When Allah intends to destroy a city, its affluent defiantly disobey and it is destroyed completely, as many generations after Noah were.
Whoever wants the immediate may get some of it, then Hell, while the believer striving for the Hereafter is appreciated; Allah gives to both, but the Hereafter's ranks are greater.
Do not set up another deity with Allah, or you will be censured and forsaken.
Worship none but Allah and treat parents well; in their old age never say even uff to them, speak nobly, show humble mercy and pray for them.
Give relatives, the poor and travelers their right without wasteful spending; speak gently if you must turn the needy away, and be neither tight-fisted nor fully open-handed.
Do not kill your children for fear of poverty; Allah provides for them and you, and killing them is a great sin.
Do not approach unlawful sexual intercourse, for it is an immorality and an evil way.
Do not kill a soul Allah has forbidden except by right; the heir of one killed unjustly is given authority but must not exceed limits in taking life.
Do not approach an orphan's property except in the best way until he matures, and fulfill every commitment, for commitments will be questioned.
Give full measure and weigh with an even balance, for that is best and best in result.
Do not pursue what you have no knowledge of, for hearing, sight and heart will be questioned, and do not walk the earth exultantly; all such evil is detested.
This is wisdom revealed to the Prophet: set up no other deity with Allah, and do not claim He gave you sons and took the angels as daughters.
The Quran sets out reminders in varied ways, yet it only increases the disbelievers in aversion.
Had there been other gods, they would have sought a way to the Owner of the Throne; Allah is far above that, and all things glorify Him.
When the Quran is recited, a hidden partition and coverings keep deniers of the Hereafter from understanding; they turn away in aversion, saying he is a man affected by magic.
They ask whether bones and dust will be raised as a new creation; whatever they become, He who first made them will restore them, perhaps soon.
Allah's servants are told to say what is best, for Satan sows discord among them and is a clear enemy to mankind.
Your Lord knows you best and has mercy or punishes as He wills; He favored some prophets over others and gave David the Psalms.
Those invoked besides Allah cannot remove harm; they themselves seek a way to their Lord, hoping for His mercy and fearing His punishment.
Every city will be destroyed or punished before Resurrection Day; signs are held back because former peoples denied them, Thamud wronging the she-camel, and come only as warning.
Your Lord encompasses the people; the vision shown to the Prophet and the accursed tree in the Quran were made a trial, and warnings only increase their transgression.
Iblees refuses to prostrate to Adam, vowing to destroy Adam's descendants but a few; he may incite them with voice, troops and promises, but has no authority over Allah's servants.
Allah drives ships for people, yet once rescued at sea they ungratefully turn away, though He could drown them; He honored the children of Adam above much of creation.
On the Day every people is called with its record, those given it in the right hand read it unwronged, and whoever was blind here is blind in the Hereafter.
They nearly tempted the Prophet away from the revelation, but Allah strengthened him; they nearly drove him out, yet as with earlier messengers, they would not remain long after.
Establish prayer from the sun's decline to the night's darkness and the dawn recitation, and pray extra at night, hoping your Lord raises you to a praised station.
Pray for a sound entrance and exit and a supporting authority, and declare that truth has come and falsehood, bound to vanish, has gone.
The Quran is sent down as healing and mercy for believers, but it only increases the wrongdoers in loss.
Given favor, the disbeliever turns away, and touched by evil he despairs; each acts in his own way, and your Lord knows best who is guided.
Asked about the soul, the Prophet is told to say it is of his Lord's affair, and mankind has been given only a little knowledge.
Allah could take back what He revealed but keeps it as mercy; mankind and jinn together could never produce its like, yet most people refuse all but disbelief.
Before believing, they demand a spring, a garden, the sky falling, Allah and the angels, a house of gold or a book; but humans are sent a human messenger.
Those Allah leaves astray are gathered on their faces, blind, dumb and deaf, into an ever-blazing Hell for denying His verses and the resurrection.
Allah, who created the heavens and earth, can create their like and has set them a sure term, yet the wrongdoers refuse all but disbelief.
Even owning the treasuries of Allah's mercy, people would hold back for fear of spending, for man is ever stingy.
Moses brought nine signs; Pharaoh, calling him bewitched, sought to expel them but was drowned with his followers, and the Children of Israel were told to dwell in the land.
The Quran came down in truth, revealed in stages to be recited over time; those given knowledge before it fall prostrate in tears when it is recited.
Call on Allah or the Most Merciful, for His are the best names; pray neither too loud nor too quiet, and praise Allah, who has no son or partner.
Praise be to Allah, who sent down to His Servant a straight Book without deviance, to warn of punishment and give righteous believers good tidings of lasting reward.
The Book warns those who say Allah has taken a son, a lie spoken without knowledge by them or their fathers.
The Prophet is told he might destroy himself with grief over those who do not believe in this message.
Allah made the earth's adornment a test of who is best in deeds, and He will turn it into barren ground.
Believing youths withdraw from their people's deities to a cave, sleep there for years, wake to send one for food, and are found, showing Allah's promise true.
Never say you will do something tomorrow without adding if Allah wills, and remember your Lord when you forget.
They stayed in their cave three hundred years and nine more; Allah knows best how long, for His is the unseen of the heavens and earth.
Recite what has been revealed of your Lord's Book; none can change His words, and there is no refuge but Him.
Stay patiently with those who call on their Lord morning and evening, do not look past them for worldly adornment, and do not obey the heedless who follow desire.
Truth is from your Lord, so let whoever wills believe or disbelieve; wrongdoers face fire and scalding drink, while believers who do good have gardens, gold bracelets and silk.
A man proud of his two gardens doubts their end and the Hour; his companion warns him, they are ruined, and he regrets associating anyone with his Lord.
Worldly life is like rain-fed plants that dry into chaff scattered by the wind; wealth and children are its adornment, but lasting good deeds are better with your Lord.
On the Day the mountains are moved, all are gathered and presented in rows, and the record is laid open, missing nothing small or great, and no one is wronged.
The angels prostrated to Adam except Iblees, who was of the jinn and departed from his Lord's command; he and his descendants are enemies, not allies to take besides Allah.
Those taken as allies besides Allah did not witness the creation of the heavens and earth or of themselves, and He would not take misguiders as assistants.
On the Day they are told to call the partners they claimed for Allah, none will answer, and the criminals will see the Fire with no way out.
Though the Quran gives every kind of example, man is most argumentative, and disbelievers mock the verses; their hearts are covered, but their punishment is deferred to an appointed time.
Moses follows a servant given knowledge from Allah but cannot stay patient as he damages a ship, kills a boy and repairs a wall, until the reasons are explained.
Dhul-Qarnayn, established on earth, travels to the sun's setting and rising places, deals with wrongdoers and believers, and builds an iron and copper barrier against Gog and Magog.
On that day they surge over one another, the Horn is blown and all are gathered, and Hell is displayed, prepared as a lodging for disbelievers blind to His remembrance.
The greatest losers think they do well while their efforts are lost; they disbelieved in their Lord's verses and meeting Him, and mocked His signs, so their recompense is Hell.
Believers who do righteous deeds will have the Gardens of Paradise as their lodging, abiding there forever with no wish to leave.
If the sea were ink for the words of my Lord, it would run out before His words did, even with another sea added.
The Prophet is only a man to whom it is revealed your god is one God, so whoever hopes to meet his Lord should do good and associate no one.
Zechariah, old and with a barren wife, privately asks his Lord for an heir and is given news of a son named John, with the sign of three nights' silence.
John is told to take the Scripture firmly, given judgement as a boy and purity, and is dutiful to his parents; peace is on him at birth, death and resurrection.
Mary is told by an angel of a pure boy, gives birth by a palm trunk, vows silence, and when her people reproach her she points to the baby.
From the cradle Jesus declares he is Allah's servant and prophet and calls people to worship Allah, who takes no son; yet the factions differed about him.
They will hear and see clearly on the Day they come to Allah; the heedless are warned of the Day of Regret, and all will return to Him.
Abraham urges his father not to worship what neither hears nor sees, nor Satan; threatened with stoning, he leaves him and his gods, and is given Isaac and Jacob.
Moses was a chosen messenger and prophet, called from the side of the mount and brought near, and given his brother Aaron as a prophet.
Ishmael was true to his promise, a messenger and prophet who enjoined prayer and zakah on his people and pleased his Lord.
Idrees was a man of truth and a prophet whom Allah raised to a high station.
These were the prophets Allah favored, descendants of Adam, of those carried with Noah, and of Abraham and Israel, who fell weeping in prostration at His verses.
Later generations neglected prayer and followed desires and will meet evil, except those who repent, believe and do righteousness, who will enter Paradise unwronged.
Paradise is gardens of perpetual residence promised in the unseen, with greetings of peace and provision morning and afternoon, inherited by those who feared Allah.
The angels descend only by your Lord's command, and He never forgets; so worship the Lord of the heavens and earth patiently, for nothing is like Him.
The disbeliever asks if he will be raised alive after death, forgetting that Allah created him before when he was nothing.
They and the devils will be gathered on their knees around Hell, the most insolent of each sect singled out; all will come to it, but the God-fearing are saved.
Disbelievers boast to believers of their better standing, though richer generations were destroyed; they will learn who is worst, while Allah increases the guided in guidance.
One who disbelieved in Allah's verses claims he will be given wealth and children, but his words are recorded, his punishment extended, and he will come to Allah alone.
They take gods besides Allah for honor, but those gods will deny their worship and turn against them.
Allah has sent devils upon the disbelievers to incite them, so do not be impatient over them, for their time is counted.
On the Day the righteous are gathered to the Most Merciful as a delegation and the criminals driven thirsty to Hell, only those with a covenant from Him may intercede.
Saying the Most Merciful has taken a son is so atrocious the heavens almost burst; it does not befit Him, as all in the heavens and earth are His servants.
The Most Merciful will appoint affection for those who believe and do righteous deeds.
The Quran is made easy in Arabic so the Prophet can give good tidings to the righteous and warn a hostile people.
Many generations before them were destroyed, and not one of them can be seen or heard now.
The Quran was not sent to distress the Prophet but as a reminder for the God-fearing, a revelation from the Creator of the earth and the highest heavens.
The Most Merciful, above the Throne, owns everything to beneath the soil and knows what is most hidden; there is no deity but Allah, whose are the best names.
Called by his Lord at a fire in the sacred valley, Moses sees his staff become a snake and his hand come out white, and is sent to Pharaoh.
Moses asks his Lord to ease his task and give him Aaron as minister; it is granted, and Allah recalls His favors since his mother cast him into the river.
Allah sends Moses and Aaron to Pharaoh to speak gently and ask for the Children of Israel; Moses tells him their Lord gave each thing its form, then guided it.
Pharaoh denies the signs and summons magicians; Moses' staff swallows their tricks, they believe despite his threats, and Hell awaits the criminal while believers have the highest ranks.
Moses leads Allah's servants by night on a dry path through the sea; Pharaoh pursues with his soldiers and is overwhelmed by the sea, having misled his people.
The Children of Israel are reminded of their rescue, manna and quails; in Moses' absence the Samiri leads them astray with a calf, and Moses confronts Aaron and the Samiri.
Allah relates these past accounts and has given the Quran; whoever turns away from it will carry a heavy burden on the Day of Resurrection.
When the Horn is blown, criminals murmur that they stayed briefly, mountains are blown away, voices are hushed, only permitted intercession helps, and believers fear no injustice.
The Quran is sent down in Arabic with varied warnings; the Prophet is told not to hasten its recitation before revelation is complete and to ask for more knowledge.
Adam forgot his promise; Iblees refused to prostrate, Satan whispered to Adam, he and his wife ate from the tree, and his Lord forgave him and sent them down.
Whoever turns from Allah's remembrance has a depressed life and is raised blind, forgotten as he forgot Allah's signs, and the Hereafter's punishment is more severe.
They walk among the dwellings of many destroyed generations, which are signs for people of intelligence.
But for a prior word and set term, punishment would be immediate, so be patient over what they say and glorify your Lord before sunrise and sunset and at night.
Do not long for the worldly splendor given to some of them as a test, for your Lord's provision is better and more lasting.
Enjoin prayer on your family and be steadfast in it; Allah asks no provision of you but provides for you, and the best outcome is for righteousness.
They demand a sign though earlier scriptures are evidence; had they been destroyed first they would have asked for a messenger; each waits, and they will know who is guided.
As their reckoning nears, people hear revelation heedlessly, call the Prophet a mere human and it magic, dreams, invention or poetry, and demand a sign, though destroyed cities never believed.
The messengers before were men given revelation, who ate food and were not immortal; Allah kept His promise, saving them and those He willed and destroying the transgressors.
Allah has sent down a Book in which is your mention, and calls on you to reason.
Many unjust cities were shattered and replaced; their people fled on sensing the punishment, confessing they were wrongdoers, until they were mown down and extinguished.
Allah did not create the heavens and earth in play; He dashes truth upon falsehood, everyone in them is His, and those near Him exalt Him tirelessly night and day.
Had there been other gods, the heavens and earth would be ruined; every messenger was told there is no deity but Allah, and those called His son are honored servants.
The heavens and earth were joined and parted, every living thing was made from water, and Allah made mountains, a protected sky, night and day, and orbiting sun and moon.
No one before was granted immortality; every soul will taste death, Allah tests people with evil and good, and to Him they return.
Disbelievers mock the Prophet and impatiently ask when the promise will come; the Fire will reach them suddenly, as earlier mockers of messengers were overwhelmed by what they ridiculed.
No one protects them from the Most Merciful, and their gods cannot help themselves; long given good things, they ignore warnings, yet a whiff of punishment makes them confess wrongdoing.
Allah sets the scales of justice for the Day of Resurrection, so no soul is wronged, and even a mustard seed's weight is brought forth.
Moses and Aaron were given the criterion, a light and a reminder for the righteous, and this Quran is also a blessed message sent down by Allah.
Abraham challenges his father and people over their statues and breaks them; they order him burned, but Allah makes the fire cool and safe, and gives him Isaac and Jacob.
Lot was given judgement and knowledge and saved from the city committing wicked deeds, an evil, defiantly disobedient people, and admitted into Allah's mercy.
Noah called to Allah, who answered him, saving him and his family from the great flood and drowning the people who denied His signs.
David and Solomon judged a case of sheep overrunning a field, with Solomon given understanding; the mountains and birds glorified Allah with David, who was taught to make armor.
Allah subjected the wind to Solomon, blowing by his command to the blessed land, and some devils dived and worked for him under Allah's guard.
Job called to his Lord in adversity, and Allah removed it and restored his family with as many more, as a mercy and a reminder for worshippers.
Ishmael, Idrees and Dhul-Kifl were all patient, admitted into Allah's mercy and counted among the righteous.
The man of the fish left in anger, then called from the darknesses that there is no deity but Allah and he had done wrong; Allah answered and saved him.
Zechariah asked not to be left without an heir; Allah answered, gave him John and amended his wife; they hastened to good deeds and supplicated in hope and fear.
The woman who guarded her chastity was breathed into through Allah's angel, and she and her son were made a sign for the worlds.
Your religion is one religion and Allah is your Lord, so worship Him; yet they divided their affair among themselves, and all will return to Him.
Whoever does righteous deeds as a believer will not have his effort denied, for Allah records it.
The people of a destroyed city will not return until Gog and Magog are let loose from every height and the true promise nears, when the disbelievers stare in horror.
Disbelievers and what they worship besides Allah will be fuel for Hell, while those promised the best are far from it, untroubled by the greatest terror and welcomed by angels.
On that Day Allah will fold the heaven like a scroll of records and repeat creation as He began it, a promise binding on Him.
Allah wrote in the Psalms, after the earlier mention, that His righteous servants will inherit the land, and this Quran is a notification for worshipping people.
The Prophet, sent as a mercy to the worlds, announces your god is one God, does not know when the promise comes, and asks his Lord to judge in truth.
Mankind is told to fear their Lord, for the convulsion of the Hour is terrible: nursing mothers will be distracted, pregnant women will miscarry, and people will seem intoxicated.
Some dispute about Allah without knowledge and follow every rebellious devil, and whoever turns to a devil is misguided by him and led to the punishment of the Blaze.
Doubters of the Resurrection are reminded of their creation from dust in stages and barren earth revived by rain; Allah revives the dead and will raise those in graves.
Some dispute about Allah without knowledge, guidance or scripture, twisting away in arrogance to mislead; they face disgrace in this world and the Burning Fire on the Day of Resurrection.
Some worship Allah on an edge, content when good touches them but turning away when trial strikes, and so lose both this world and the Hereafter.
Invoking instead of Allah what neither harms nor benefits is extreme error, and what is invoked has harm closer than its benefit, a wretched protector and associate.
Allah will admit those who believe and do righteous deeds to gardens beneath which rivers flow, for Allah does what He intends.
Whoever thinks Allah will not support the Prophet in this world and the Hereafter is told to stretch a rope to the ceiling and see if that removes his rage.
Allah has sent the Quran down as verses of clear evidence, and Allah guides whom He intends.
Allah will judge on the Day of Resurrection between the believers, Jews, Sabeans, Christians, Magians and those who associate others with Him, for He witnesses all things.
All in the heavens and earth prostrate to Allah, with the sun, moon, stars, mountains, trees, creatures and many people, while punishment is justified upon many others.
Two adversaries dispute over their Lord, a verse revealed about the duel at Badr: disbelievers get garments of fire, scalding water and iron maces, believers wear gold, pearl and silk.
Those who disbelieve and bar people from Allah's way and from al-Masjid al-Haram, equal for resident and visitor, will taste painful punishment, as will anyone intending wrongdoing there.
Abraham is given the site of the House to purify it and proclaim the Hajj; pilgrims come, mention Allah over sacrificial animals, feed the poor and circle the House.
Honoring Allah's sacred ordinances is best; livestock is permitted except what is recited, idols and false statements must be avoided, and associating with Allah is like falling from the sky.
Honoring Allah's symbols comes from piety; every religion has a rite of sacrifice, camels and cattle are offered in Allah's name, eaten and shared, and only piety reaches Allah.
Allah defends those who believe and does not like anyone treacherous and ungrateful.
In the first permission to fight, Muslims wronged and driven from Makkah for saying their Lord is Allah may fight; given authority, they establish prayer, give zakah and enjoin right.
Before the Prophet, the peoples of Noah, 'Aad, Thamud, Abraham, Lot and Madyan denied, as Moses was denied; Allah let them enjoy, then seized them, leaving cities in ruin.
They urge the Prophet to hasten the punishment, but Allah never fails His promise, a day with Him is like a thousand years, and He seized many cities after respite.
The Prophet is only a clear warner: believers who do righteous deeds receive forgiveness and noble provision, while those who strive against Allah's verses are companions of Hellfire.
Satan threw something into the speech of every messenger or prophet, but Allah abolishes it and makes His verses precise, a trial for diseased hearts while the knowledgeable believe.
Disbelievers stay in doubt until the Hour comes suddenly; that Day all sovereignty is Allah's, believers enter the Gardens of Pleasure and deniers of His signs face humiliating punishment.
Those who emigrated for Allah's cause and then were killed or died will receive a good provision from Allah and an entrance that pleases them.
Whoever responds to harm with its equivalent and is then wronged again will be aided by Allah, who is Pardoning and Forgiving.
Allah merges night and day, sends rain that greens the earth, owns all, subjects the earth and ships to people, holds up the sky, and gives life and death.
Every religion has its rites; the Prophet should not let disbelievers contend but invite them to his Lord, for he is rightly guided, and Allah will judge their differences.
Allah knows what is in the heaven and earth; it is all in a Record, and that is easy for Allah.
They worship besides Allah that for which He sent no authority and of which they have no knowledge, and the wrongdoers will have no helper.
When Allah's clear verses are recited, disbelievers show disapproval and almost attack the reciters, and they are told the Fire promised to disbelievers is worse.
Those invoked besides Allah could never create a fly even together, nor recover what a fly takes from them; people have not appraised Allah as He deserves.
Allah chooses messengers from the angels and from people, knows what is before and after them, and to Him all matters return.
Believers are told to bow, prostrate, worship, do good and strive for Allah in Abraham's religion, without hardship, named Muslims, establishing prayer, giving zakah and holding to Allah.
The successful believers are humble in prayer, avoid ill speech, give zakah, guard their private parts, keep trusts and promises, and maintain their prayers; they will inherit al-Firdaus forever.
Allah created man from clay, then a sperm-drop, clot, lump, bones and flesh, making him another creation; then people die and will be resurrected on the Day of Resurrection.
Allah created seven heavens and sends measured rain, bringing forth palms, grapevines and an oil tree from Mount Sinai, and gives livestock for drink and food, and ships for carrying.
Noah calls his people to worship Allah alone; the chiefs call him mad, so Allah has him build the ship for his family and pairs, as the wrongdoers will drown.
After Noah's people, a generation, said to be 'Aad or Thamud, rejects its messenger as a mere man and denies resurrection until the shriek seizes them.
Other generations follow, none able to advance or delay its term; each denies the messenger sent to it, so they are destroyed one after another and made into narrations.
Allah sends Moses and Aaron with signs to Pharaoh and his chiefs, who arrogantly reject two men like themselves and are destroyed; Moses is then given the Scripture.
Allah made the son of Mary and his mother a sign and sheltered them on high ground with level areas and flowing water.
Allah tells the messengers to eat good food and do righteous work, for their religion is one, but people split it into sects, each rejoicing in its own.
Those given wealth and children should not think Allah is hastening good things to them; they do not perceive.
Those who fear their Lord, believe in His signs, associate none with Him and give with fearful hearts, knowing they will return to Him, hasten to good deeds.
No soul is burdened beyond its capacity and a truthful record is kept, yet disbelievers' hearts are confused, and their affluent, once seized by punishment, cry for help in vain.
They neither reflect on the Quran nor acknowledge their Messenger, calling him mad, though he brought the truth, asks no payment and invites them to a straight path.
Those who do not believe in the Hereafter deviate from the path; even shown mercy they would persist, suffering did not humble them, and severe punishment will bring despair.
Allah gave people hearing, sight and hearts, spread them through the earth to be gathered to Him, gives life and death and alternates night and day, yet few are grateful.
Like former peoples, they ask whether they will be resurrected after becoming dust and bones, calling the promise legends of the former peoples.
Asked who owns the earth, who is Lord of the seven heavens and the Great Throne, and who holds the realm of all things, they answer Allah, yet are deluded.
Allah has taken no son and no deity is with Him, or each would take what it created and seek to overcome others; He knows the unseen and the witnessed.
The Prophet asks not to be placed among the wrongdoers, is told to repel evil with what is best, and seeks refuge in his Lord from the devils.
When death comes to a disbeliever he asks to be sent back to do righteousness, but it is only words, and a barrier lies behind them until they are resurrected.
When the Horn is blown no ties remain; those with heavy scales succeed, while those with light scales lose themselves in Hell, their faces seared by the Fire.
In Hell the deniers beg to leave, are refused for mocking the believers, say they stayed a day or part of one, and are asked if they were created uselessly.
Exalted is Allah, the Sovereign, the Truth, Lord of the Noble Throne, with no deity but Him; whoever invokes another deity without proof answers to Him.
The Prophet is told to ask his Lord for forgiveness and mercy, for He is the best of the merciful.
This surah is sent down by Allah with obligations and verses of clear evidence so that people may remember.
An unmarried woman or man found guilty of sexual intercourse receives a hundred lashes witnessed by believers, and a fornicator marries only a fornicator or a polytheist.
Those who accuse chaste women without four witnesses receive eighty lashes, their testimony is never accepted, and they are defiantly disobedient, except those who repent and reform.
A husband accusing his wife without witnesses swears four times by Allah he is truthful and invokes Allah's curse if lying; she averts punishment by swearing four times he lies.
In the slander against Aisha, a group spread falsehood without four witnesses; believers should have thought well of each other, not spoken of it, and must never repeat it.
Believers must not follow Satan's footsteps, for he enjoins immorality and wrongdoing, and none would be pure without Allah's favor and mercy.
Those of virtue and wealth should not swear to stop giving to relatives, the needy and emigrants, but should pardon and overlook, as they would like Allah to forgive them.
Those who falsely accuse chaste, unaware believing women are cursed in this world and the Hereafter, their tongues and limbs will testify against them, and the good are declared innocent.
Believers should not enter others' houses without welcome and greeting, must go back if told to, and may enter uninhabited houses that serve them.
Believing men and women are told to lower their gaze and guard their private parts, and women to cover their chests with headcovers and show adornment only to those listed.
Marry the unmarried and righteous slaves; those without means abstain, slaves seeking freedom contracts get them where goodness is known, and slave girls must not be forced into prostitution.
Allah has sent down distinct verses, examples from those who passed before, and an admonition for those who fear Him.
Allah is the Light of the heavens and earth, His light like a lamp in a niche lit from a blessed olive tree; He guides to it whom He wills.
In mosques Allah ordered raised, men exalt Him morning and evening, undistracted by commerce from His remembrance, prayer and zakah, fearing the Day, and Allah rewards them from His bounty.
The deeds of disbelievers are like a mirage that proves to be nothing, or like layered darkness in a deep sea; whoever Allah gives no light has no light.
All in the heavens and earth, and the birds in flight, exalt Allah, each knowing its prayer, and His are the dominion and the final destination.
Allah drives clouds that bring rain and hail, alternates night and day, and created every creature from water, some moving on bellies, some on two legs, some on four.
Allah has sent down distinct verses and guides whom He wills to a straight path.
Hypocrites claim belief and obedience, but a party turns away when called to Allah and His Messenger for judgement, coming promptly only when in the right; they are wrongdoers.
True believers say they hear and obey when called to Allah and His Messenger; oath-swearers are told obedience is known, and obeying the Messenger, charged only with notification, brings guidance.
Allah promises believers who do righteous deeds succession on earth, an established religion and security after fear, and tells them to pray, give zakah and obey the Messenger.
Disbelievers cannot cause Allah failure on the earth, and their refuge will be the Fire.
Slaves and children must ask permission at three private times of day, children past puberty at all times, and women past menstruation may set aside outer garments without displaying adornment.
There is no blame on the blind, lame or ill, or on eating in relatives' or friends' houses, together or apart, and people should greet one another on entering houses.
Believers ask the Messenger's permission before leaving a gathering, should not call him as they call each other, and those dissenting from his order should beware.
All in the heavens and earth belong to Allah, who knows people's state and will inform them of their deeds on the Day they return to Him.
Blessed is He who sent down the Criterion to His Servant; He owns the heavens and earth, has no son or partner, and created all, while their gods create nothing.
Disbelievers call the Quran an invented falsehood and dictated legends of former peoples, but it was revealed by Him who knows every secret in the heavens and earth.
They ask why this messenger eats food and walks in markets without an angel, treasure or garden, calling him bewitched, though Allah could give him better gardens and palaces.
Those who deny the Hour face a roaring Blaze, chained in a narrow place crying for destruction, while the righteous are promised the Garden of Eternity with whatever they wish.
On the Day Allah gathers them with what they worshipped, the worshipped deny taking allies besides Him and say comforts made the worshippers forget the message.
Every messenger before the Prophet ate food and walked in the markets, and Allah has made some people a trial for others to see who is patient.
Those not expecting to meet Allah demand to see angels; when they do, criminals get no good tidings, the heaven splits, and the wrongdoer regrets his friend.
The Messenger complains his people abandoned the Quran; every prophet has enemies among criminals, and the Quran came in stages to strengthen his heart, answering every argument with the truth.
Those gathered on their faces to Hell are the worst in position and the farthest astray.
Moses and Aaron's deniers were destroyed, Noah's people drowned, and 'Aad, Thamud, the companions of the well and many generations were destroyed, as was the town rained upon.
They ridicule the Prophet as nearly misleading them from their gods; whoever takes his own desire as a god is like livestock, or even further astray.
Allah extends the shadow, makes night a covering, sleep a rest and day a resurrection, and sends winds and pure water to revive dead land and water livestock and people.
Allah could have sent a warner to every city but sent the Prophet to all, so he must not obey the disbelievers but strive against them with the Quran.
Allah released two seas, fresh and salty, with a barrier between them, and created humans from water, joined by lineage and marriage.
They worship besides Allah what neither benefits nor harms them, and the disbeliever is ever an assistant against his Lord.
The Prophet is sent only to give good tidings and warn, asking no payment except that whoever wills may take a way to his Lord.
Rely on the Ever-Living who does not die and exalt Him with praise; He created the heavens and earth in six days and established Himself above the Throne.
Told to prostrate to the Most Merciful, they ask what the Most Merciful is, and it increases them in aversion.
Allah placed great stars, a burning lamp and a luminous moon in the sky, and made night and day succeed each other for those who remember or give thanks.
The servants of the Most Merciful walk easily, pray at night, spend moderately, invoke no other deity, avoid unlawful killing and intercourse, repent, shun falsehood, and are given the Chamber.
The Prophet is told to say his Lord would not care for people but for their supplication, warning Makkah's deniers that their denial will cling to them.
These are verses of the clear Book; the Prophet grieves at their disbelief, but they turn from every new revelation and will learn the news of what they ridiculed.
The earth produces every noble kind, a sign most do not believe, and the Lord is the Exalted in Might, the Merciful.
Allah sends Moses and Aaron to Pharaoh to release the Children of Israel; Moses answers Pharaoh's reproach over his upbringing and past deed and describes the Lord of the worlds.
Pharaoh threatens Moses with prison and is shown the staff and white hand; magicians are gathered, Moses' staff devours what they falsified, and they believe despite Pharaoh's threats.
Moses is told to leave by night with Allah's servants; Pharaoh pursues them at sunrise, the sea parts at Moses' strike, saving him and those with him; the others drown.
Abraham asks his father and people whether their idols hear or benefit them, praises the Lord who created, guides, feeds and heals him, and prays for forgiveness and the Garden.
Paradise is brought near the righteous and Hellfire to the deviators, who are thrown in with what they worshipped and Iblees' soldiers, confess their error and wish for a return.
Noah calls his people to fear Allah and obey him; they scorn his lowly followers and threaten stoning, so Allah saves him in the laden ship and drowns the rest.
Hud warns 'Aad, who build palaces and fortresses and strike as tyrants, to fear Allah who gave them livestock, children, gardens and springs; they dismiss him and are destroyed.
Salih warns Thamud, secure among gardens and carved mountain homes, to fear Allah; they demand a sign, he gives them a she-camel, they hamstring her and the punishment seizes them.
Lot warns against approaching males instead of the mates Allah created; threatened with eviction, he and his family are saved except an old woman, and the rest destroyed.
Shu'ayb tells the companions of the thicket, the people of Madyan, to give full measure; calling him a liar, they are seized on the day of the black cloud.
The Quran is the Lord's revelation, brought by the Trustworthy Spirit in clear Arabic, mentioned in former scriptures and recognized by scholars of the Children of Israel.
The criminals will not believe in it until the painful punishment comes suddenly; years of enjoyment will not help them, and no city was destroyed without warners.
The devils did not bring the revelation down; it is not allowable for them, they could not, and they are removed from hearing it.
Do not invoke another deity with Allah and so be among the punished.
The Prophet is told to warn his closest kindred, lower his wing to believing followers, disown the disobedient's deeds, and rely on Allah who sees him among those who prostrate.
The devils descend upon every sinful liar, passing on what is heard, and most of them are liars.
Poets are followed by the deviators, roam every valley and say what they do not do, except those who believe, do good, remember Allah often and defend after being wronged.
These are verses of the Quran and a clear Book, guidance and good tidings for believers who establish prayer, give zakah and are certain of the Hereafter.
Those who do not believe in the Hereafter find their deeds made pleasing so they wander blindly, and they will have the worst punishment and be the greatest losers.
The Prophet receives the Quran from One who is Wise and Knowing.
Moses sees a fire and is called by Allah; his staff writhes like a snake and his hand comes out white, among nine signs for Pharaoh and his people.
Shown the visible signs, Pharaoh's people call them obvious magic and reject them out of injustice and haughtiness though inwardly convinced, and the corrupters meet their end.
Solomon inherits David, knows the language of birds, smiles at an ant's words, and learns from the hoopoe of a sun-worshipping woman ruling Sheba, then sends her a letter.
Bilqis, ruler of Sheba, consults her chiefs and sends a gift, which Solomon rejects; her throne is brought and disguised, and on arriving she submits with Solomon to Allah.
Salih calls Thamud to worship Allah; they call him a bad omen and nine corrupters plot to kill him and his family, but Allah destroys them and saves the believers.
Lot condemns his people for approaching men with desire instead of women; they move to expel his family, so Allah saves them except his wife and rains upon the rest.
Praise is Allah's, who created the heavens and earth, sends rain, steadies the earth, answers the desperate and guides through darkness, and there is no deity with Him.
Only Allah knows the unseen; people do not perceive when they will be resurrected and doubt the Hereafter, and disbelievers call being brought out after becoming dust old legends.
The Prophet tells people to see the end of the criminals, is told not to grieve over their plots, and answers those demanding the promise that some may be close.
The Lord is full of bounty though most are ungrateful, knows what breasts conceal and declare, and everything concealed in heaven and earth is in a clear Register.
The Quran relates most of what the Children of Israel disagree over and is guidance and mercy for believers; the Lord will judge between them, so rely on Allah.
The Prophet cannot make the dead or the deaf hear, nor guide the blind from error; only those who believe in Allah's verses will hear.
When the word befalls them, Allah will bring forth a creature from the earth to tell them that people were not certain of His verses.
On the Day deniers from every nation are gathered and the Horn is blown, all are terrified and mountains pass like clouds; good deeds bring better, evil deeds the Fire.
The Prophet is commanded to worship the Lord of this sacred city, be a Muslim and recite the Quran; the guided benefit themselves, and Allah will show His signs.
The news of Moses and Pharaoh is recited: Pharaoh split the people into factions, oppressing one and slaughtering its sons, while Allah willed to make the oppressed leaders and inheritors.
Moses' mother, inspired by Allah, casts him into the river; Pharaoh's family picks him up, and through his sister Allah restores him to his mother.
Grown and given judgement and knowledge, Moses strikes and kills a man fighting one of his faction, is forgiven, and is warned that the chiefs plot to kill him.
Leaving in fear for Madyan, Moses waters two women's flocks at the well; their father invites him and offers a daughter in marriage for eight or ten years' service.
Moses sees a fire while traveling with his family, is called by Allah from the tree, is given two proofs for Pharaoh, and is strengthened through his brother Aaron.
Moses' signs are called invented magic; Pharaoh knows no god for them but himself and orders a tower, so Allah throws him and his soldiers into the sea.
Allah gave Moses the Scripture after destroying former generations, as enlightenment, guidance and mercy for people.
The Prophet was not present when Moses received the command, nor in Madyan, but is sent as a mercy to warn a people who had no warner before him.
Given the truth, they demand what Moses was given and call both scriptures magic; challenged to bring better guidance, they follow desires, though the Quran was conveyed to remind them.
Those given the Scripture before believe in the Quran as truth, are rewarded twice for their patience, repel evil with good, spend, and turn away from ill speech.
The Prophet cannot guide whom he likes, but Allah guides whom He wills; some fear following the guidance would uproot them, though Allah gave them a safe sanctuary.
Allah destroyed many cities insolent in their living, leaving their dwellings empty, but never before sending a messenger to their mother city and only when their people were wrongdoers.
Whatever people are given is enjoyment of worldly life, while what is with Allah is better and lasting; one promised good is not like one given worldly enjoyment then punished.
On the Day Allah asks for their claimed partners, the misleaders disown them, the partners do not answer, none can answer about the messengers, and the repentant believers succeed.
The Lord creates and chooses as He wills and knows what breasts conceal; He is Allah, with no deity but Him, owner of praise and decision, to whom all return.
If Allah made night or day endless until the Day of Resurrection, no other deity could bring light or rest; in mercy He made both for rest and bounty.
On the Day Allah asks for their claimed partners, a witness is taken from every nation, they are told to bring proof, and what they invented is lost.
Qarun of Moses' people, given vast treasures, credits his own knowledge; those wanting worldly life wish for his fortune until Allah makes the earth swallow him and his home.
The home of the Hereafter is for those seeking neither exaltedness nor corruption, the righteous; a good deed brings better, and evil is repaid only in kind.
He who imposed the Quran will return the Prophet to a place of return; the Book is a mercy, so he must not aid disbelievers but invite to his Lord.
Invoke no other deity with Allah, for there is no deity but Him; everything will be destroyed except His Face, and His is the judgement and the return.
People who say they believe will be tried as those before them were, so Allah makes evident the truthful and the liars, and evildoers cannot outrun Him.
Allah's term is coming for whoever hopes to meet Him; striving benefits only the striver, and believers doing righteous deeds have misdeeds removed and are rewarded by their best deeds.
People are enjoined to be good to parents but not to obey them in associating others with Allah, and believers who do righteous deeds will be admitted among the righteous.
Some say they believe but treat harm from people as Allah's punishment, then claim to be with believers at victory; Allah will make evident the believers and the hypocrites.
The disbelievers of Quraysh offer to carry believers' sins if followed, but they lie; they will carry their own burdens and more, and be questioned on the Day of Resurrection.
Noah stays among his people nine hundred and fifty years until the flood seizes them, while he and the companions of the ship are saved as a sign.
Abraham tells his people to worship and fear Allah, for their idols cannot provide for them; if they deny, nations before denied too, and the messenger must only convey clearly.
Allah begins creation and repeats it, which is easy for Him; He punishes or shows mercy as He wills, none escapes Him, and deniers of meeting Him despair of mercy.
Abraham's people say kill or burn him; Allah saves him from the fire, he warns idol bonds end in cursing, Lot believes him, and he is given Isaac and Jacob.
Lot condemns his people's immorality; messengers tell Abraham they will destroy Lot's city but save him and his family except his wife, and punishment comes down from the sky.
Shu'ayb tells Madyan to worship Allah, expect the Last Day and avoid corruption; they deny him, and the earthquake leaves them fallen in their home.
'Aad, Thamud, Qarun, Pharaoh and Haman were each seized for their sin, by stones, blast, the earth swallowing or drowning, wronged not by Allah but by themselves.
Those taking allies other than Allah are like the spider whose home is weakest; Allah knows what they call upon, and only those of knowledge understand such examples.
Allah created the heavens and the earth in truth, a sign for the believers.
Recite the revealed Book and establish prayer, for prayer prohibits immorality and wrongdoing, and the remembrance of Allah is greater.
Argue with the People of the Scripture only in the best way, except the unjust among them, saying that our God and their God is one.
Some given earlier Scripture and some Makkans believe in the Quran; the Prophet read or wrote no scripture before it, and for those demanding signs the Book suffices.
They urge the punishment on, but it will come suddenly at its appointed term, and Hell will encompass the disbelievers, covering them from above and below.
Believers are told Allah's earth is spacious, so they may emigrate to worship Him alone; the patient who rely on Him get chambers in Paradise, and Allah provides for all.
Asked who created the heavens and earth, subjected the sun and moon and sends rain, they say Allah, yet they are deluded; He extends or restricts provision as He wills.
Worldly life is only diversion and amusement, while the home of the Hereafter is the true life.
At sea they supplicate Allah sincerely, but once delivered to land they associate others with Him, denying what He granted and enjoying themselves.
Allah made Makkah a safe sanctuary while people around are taken away, yet they believe falsehood and deny His favor; none is more unjust than one who lies about Allah.
Allah will guide those who strive for Him to His ways, and Allah is with the doers of good.
The Byzantines, defeated in the nearest land, will overcome within three to nine years, when the believers will rejoice in Allah's victory, a promise He never fails.
Most people know only the outward side of worldly life and are unaware of the Hereafter.
Allah created the heavens and the earth only in truth and for a specified term, yet many people disbelieve in meeting their Lord.
Earlier peoples were stronger and built more, yet they denied and ridiculed Allah's signs brought by their messengers, wronging themselves, so their end was the worst.
Allah begins creation, then repeats it, and to Him all will be returned.
When the Hour arrives the criminals will despair, their claimed partners will not intercede for them, and people will be separated.
Believers who did righteous deeds will be delighted in a garden, while those who disbelieved and denied the verses and the Hereafter will be brought into punishment.
Exalt Allah in the evening and morning, at night and at noon, the times of the daily prayers; all praise in the heavens and earth is His.
Allah brings the living from the dead and the dead from the living and revives the lifeless earth, and so will people be brought out.
Among Allah's signs are humans made from dust, mates who bring tranquillity, varied languages and colors, sleep, lightning and rain, and the heavens and earth standing by His command.
All in the heavens and earth belong to Allah and obey Him; He begins creation and repeats it, which is easier for Him, and His is the highest attribute.
Allah gives an example from people themselves, asking whether they would make those their right hands possess equal partners in their provision, fearing them as each other.
Wrongdoers follow their own desires without knowledge, and none can guide one whom Allah has sent astray, nor will they have helpers.
Turn to the true religion, the fitrah Allah created people upon, turning to Him in repentance, fearing Him, establishing prayer, and not associating others with Him or splitting into sects.
People call on their Lord in hardship, but once He lets them taste mercy some associate others with Him, and they are asked what revealed authority supports this.
People rejoice when given mercy and despair when evil befalls them for their own deeds, yet Allah extends provision for whom He wills and restricts it.
Give relatives their right, and the needy and the traveler; that is best for those seeking Allah's countenance, and they will succeed.
Wealth given in interest to grow within people's wealth does not grow with Allah, but zakah given for His countenance is multiplied.
Allah creates, provides, causes death and gives life, and none of the claimed partners does any of that; He is exalted above what they associate.
Corruption has appeared on land and sea because of what people's hands have earned, so Allah may let them taste part of what they have done, that perhaps they return.
People are told to travel the land and see the end of those before them, most of whom associated others with Allah.
Turn to the correct religion before an unavoidable Day when people divide: disbelievers bear their disbelief, and believers who do righteousness are rewarded from Allah's bounty.
Among Allah's signs are the winds bringing good tidings and mercy, and letting ships sail by His command so people may seek His bounty and perhaps be grateful.
Allah sent messengers with clear evidence to their peoples before the Prophet, took retribution on those who committed crimes, and supporting the believers was due upon Him.
Allah's winds bring rain on whom He wills after despair, reviving the earth as He will revive the dead, yet if a wind yellowed their crops they would disbelieve.
The Prophet cannot make the dead or the deaf hear or guide the blind from error; only those who believe in Allah's verses will listen.
Allah creates people from weakness, then gives strength, then weakness and white hair again; He creates what He wills.
When the Hour comes, criminals will swear they stayed only an hour, those given knowledge say they stayed as Allah decreed, and the wrongdoers' excuses will not help.
The Quran gives every kind of example, yet whatever sign is brought, disbelievers call believers falsifiers, and so Allah seals the hearts of those who do not know.
The Prophet is told to be patient, for Allah's promise is true, and not to be unsettled by those without certainty.
These are verses of the wise Book, guidance and mercy for doers of good who establish prayer, give zakah and are certain of the Hereafter; they are the successful.
Some buy amusing talk to mislead from Allah's way without knowledge, ridicule it, and turn arrogantly from His verses as if deaf, facing humiliating and painful punishment.
Believers who do righteous deeds will abide forever in the Gardens of Pleasure, Allah's true promise.
Allah created the heavens without visible pillars, set firm mountains, spread creatures and sent rain for plants, and challenges others to show what those besides Him created.
