Allah gave Luqman wisdom and told him to be grateful, and Luqman told his son not to associate anything with Allah, for that is great injustice.
Allah enjoins care for parents, the mother bearing weakness upon weakness; be grateful to Him and them, but if they urge associating partners, do not obey, yet stay kind.
Luqman told his son Allah brings out even a mustard seed's weight of wrong, and to pray, enjoin right, forbid wrong, be patient, shun arrogance and lower his voice.
Though Allah subjected all in the heavens and earth to people, some dispute about Him without knowledge and follow their fathers, even if Satan invites them to the Blaze.
Whoever submits to Allah while doing good holds the most trustworthy handhold, and the Prophet need not grieve over disbelievers, who enjoy a little before a massive punishment.
Asked who created the heavens and earth, they would say Allah, though most do not know; all in the heavens and earth is His, the Free of need, the Praiseworthy.
If all trees on earth were pens and the sea ink, replenished by seven more seas, Allah's words would still not be exhausted.
Creating and resurrecting all people is, for Allah, like doing so for a single soul.
Allah merges night into day, runs the sun and moon, and sails ships to show His signs; amid waves people call on Him sincerely, but once ashore some stay moderate.
People are told to fear their Lord and a Day when no father or son can help the other, and not be deluded by worldly life or the Deceiver.
Allah alone knows the Hour, sends the rain and knows what is in wombs, while no soul knows what it will earn tomorrow or where it will die.
The Book is revealed beyond doubt from the Lord of the worlds, not invented but the truth, so the Prophet may warn a people who had no warner before.
Allah created the heavens and earth in six days, established Himself above the Throne, arranges every matter, and made man from clay, proportioning him and giving hearing, sight and hearts.
Disbelievers ask if they will be created anew after being lost in the earth; the angel of death will take them, and then they return to their Lord.
Criminals will hang their heads before their Lord begging to return, but Allah will fill Hell with jinn and people, who taste eternal punishment for forgetting this Day.
Believers in Allah's verses prostrate when reminded, shun arrogance, rise from bed to call on their Lord in fear and hope, spend, and have hidden comfort as reward.
Believers and the defiantly disobedient are not equal: believers have the Gardens of Refuge, the disobedient the Fire, and a nearer punishment short of the greater, that perhaps they repent.
None is more unjust than one reminded of his Lord's verses who turns away, and Allah will take retribution from the criminals.
Allah gave Moses the Scripture and made the Torah guidance for the Children of Israel, raised patient guiding leaders among them, and will judge their differences on Resurrection Day.
Many generations were destroyed before them, whose dwellings they walk among, and in that are signs, if they would hear.
Allah drives water to barren land and brings forth crops that feed their livestock and themselves, if they would see.
Disbelievers ask when the conquest will be; then their belief will not benefit them nor will they be reprieved, so the Prophet is to turn away and wait.
The Prophet is told to fear Allah, not obey the disbelievers and hypocrites, follow what is revealed to him, and rely on Allah.
Wives declared unlawful do not become mothers, nor adopted sons true sons; adopted children are called by their fathers' names, or as brothers in religion if unknown.
The Prophet is more worthy of the believers than themselves and his wives are their mothers, while blood relatives are more entitled to inherit than other believers and emigrants.
Allah took a solemn covenant from the prophets, including the Prophet, Noah, Abraham, Moses and Jesus, to question the truthful about their truth, and prepared punishment for disbelievers.
Believers are reminded how Allah sent a wind and unseen armies against the Confederates who came from above and below, when eyes shifted, hearts reached throats and believers were shaken.

At the Trench, hypocrites called Allah's promise delusion, urged Yathrib's people home, sought leave claiming exposed houses, held back from battle, and lashed believers with sharp tongues once fear passed.
The Messenger of Allah is an excellent example for anyone hoping in Allah and the Last Day and remembering Allah often.
Seeing the companies, believers said Allah and His Messenger spoke the truth and grew in faith; some have fulfilled their vow and others await, and Allah rewards the truthful.
Allah repelled the disbelieving Confederates in their rage with no gain, and He sufficed the believers in battle.
Allah brought the Confederates' supporters among the People of the Scripture down from their fortresses, some killed and some captured, and gave the believers their land, homes and properties.
The Prophet's wives are to choose worldly adornment or Allah and the Hereafter, face double punishment or reward, speak properly, stay in their houses, pray, give zakah and obey.
Allah has prepared forgiveness and great reward for Muslim and believing men and women who are obedient, truthful, patient, humble, charitable, fasting, chaste and remember Allah often.
When Allah and His Messenger decide a matter, no believing man or woman has a choice in it, and whoever disobeys them has clearly strayed.
Once Zayd no longer needed his wife Zaynab, Allah married her to the Prophet, removing believers' discomfort over adopted sons' wives; Muhammad is Allah's Messenger and last of the prophets.
Believers are told to remember Allah much and exalt Him morning and afternoon; He blesses them to bring them into light, and their greeting on meeting Him will be Peace.
The Prophet is sent as witness, bringer of good tidings, warner, caller to Allah and illuminating lamp, told not to obey disbelievers and hypocrites but to rely on Allah.
Believing women divorced before being touched have no waiting period to count, and are to be given provision and a gracious release.
Allah sets out the women lawful for the Prophet, lets him choose among his wives, then forbids him more wives or exchanges, except those his right hand possesses.
Enter the Prophet's houses only when invited for meals, leave after eating, ask his wives from behind a partition, and never harm him or marry his wives after him.
There is no blame on women before their fathers, sons, brothers, brothers' and sisters' sons, their women and those their right hands possess, and they are to fear Allah.
Allah blesses the Prophet and His angels ask for it, and believers are told to ask Allah to bless him and grant him peace.
Those who abuse Allah and His Messenger are cursed in this world and the Hereafter, and those who undeservedly harm believing men and women bear slander and clear sin.
The Prophet is to tell his wives, daughters and believing women to draw their outer garments over themselves, so they will be known and not abused.
If hypocrites, the sick-hearted and rumor-spreaders in al-Madinah do not stop, they will not stay neighbors for long, and wherever found will be accursed, seized and massacred.
People ask the Prophet about the Hour; its knowledge is only with Allah, and perhaps it is near.
Allah cursed the disbelievers and prepared an eternal Blaze, where, faces turned in the Fire, they wish they had obeyed and seek double punishment for the leaders who misled them.
Believers are told not to be like those of the Children of Israel who abused Moses, whom Allah cleared of what they said, for he was distinguished before Allah.
Believers are told to fear Allah and speak justly, so He will amend their deeds and forgive their sins, and obeying Allah and His Messenger is a great attainment.
The heavens, earth and mountains declined the Trust, but man bore it, unjust and ignorant, so Allah may punish hypocrites and those associating others with Him and accept believers' repentance.
All praise belongs to Allah, owner of the heavens and earth, who knows what enters and leaves the earth and what descends from and ascends to the sky.
Disbelievers say the Hour will not come, but it will; the Knower of the unseen records every atom's weight to reward believers and punish those who strive against His verses.
Those given knowledge see that what is revealed to the Prophet is the truth, guiding to the path of the Exalted in Might, the Praiseworthy.
Disbelievers ask whether the man who tells of new creation after disintegration has invented a lie about Allah or is mad, though Allah could make the earth swallow them.
Allah favored David: the mountains and birds echoed praises with him, iron was made pliable for him, and he was told to make coats of mail and do righteous work.
Solomon was given the wind, a copper spring and working jinn, David's family were told to work in gratitude, and a creature eating his staff revealed his death.
Sheba, given two gardens, turned away, so Allah sent the dam's flood and replaced them with bitter fruit; given safe journeys, they asked for longer ones and were dispersed.
Iblees found his assumption about them true and they followed him, except some believers; he had no authority, but Allah would make clear who believes in the Hereafter.
The claimed deities own not an atom's weight in heavens or earth, intercession helps only whom Allah permits, He provides and will judge between people, and He alone is Allah.
The Prophet is sent to all mankind as a bringer of good tidings and a warner, though most people do not know.
Disbelievers ask when the promised Day comes; it is fixed, and there the oppressed and the arrogant who rejected the Quran will blame each other before their Lord.
The affluent of every city rejected their warner, claiming more wealth and children, but Allah extends and restricts provision, and only faith and righteous deeds bring people near Him.
Those who strive against Allah's verses to make them fail will be brought into the punishment.
Allah extends and restricts provision for His servants, and whatever they spend He will replace, for He is the best of providers.
When Allah gathers all and asks the angels whether these people worshipped them, the angels say it was the jinn, and the wrongdoers are told to taste the Fire.
When the verses are recited, disbelievers say a man wants to turn them from their fathers' worship, call it an invented lie and obvious magic, though they had no scripture.
Earlier peoples, given far more than these, also denied Allah's messengers, and how terrible was His reproach.
The Prophet urges people to stand for Allah in pairs or singly and reflect: he is no madman but a warner, asking no payment and guided by revelation.
Terrified and seized with no escape, disbelievers will then claim belief though they disbelieved before, and will be barred from what they desire, as their kind were before.
Allah, Creator of the heavens and earth, made winged angels messengers and adds to creation as He wills; none can withhold the mercy He grants or release what He withholds.
People are told to remember Allah's favor, for no creator but Him provides from the heaven and earth, and there is no deity except Him.
If they deny the Prophet, messengers before him were also denied, and all matters return to Allah.
Allah's promise is true, so people must not be deluded by worldly life or the Deceiver; Satan is their enemy, inviting his party to the Blaze.
Disbelievers will have severe punishment, while believers who do righteous deeds will have forgiveness and great reward.
Some see their evil deeds as good, but Allah sends astray and guides whom He wills, so the Prophet should not perish in regret over them.
Allah sends winds that drive clouds to dead land and revive the earth after its lifelessness, and so is the resurrection.
All honor belongs to Allah; good speech rises to Him, raised by righteous work, while those who plot evil face severe punishment and their plotting will perish.
Allah created people from dust, then a sperm-drop, then made them mates, and every pregnancy, birth and lifespan happens with His knowledge and is in a register.
The fresh and salty waters are not alike, yet from each people eat tender meat and take ornaments, and ships plow through them as people seek His bounty.
Allah merges night and day, runs the sun and moon; those invoked besides Him own not a date seed's membrane, cannot answer, and will deny that worship on Resurrection Day.
People need Allah while He is Free of need and Praiseworthy, and if He willed He could remove them and bring a new creation, which is not difficult for Him.
On the Day of Resurrection no soul will carry another's burden, even a relative's; the Prophet can warn only those who fear their Lord unseen and establish prayer.
The blind and seeing, darkness and light, shade and heat, living and dead are not equal; Allah makes hear whom He wills, but the Prophet cannot make the buried hear.
The Prophet is only a warner sent with truth; every nation had a warner, and earlier messengers bringing clear proofs and scripture were also denied, so Allah seized the disbelievers.
Rain brings fruits of many colors, and mountains, people, creatures and livestock also vary in color; only those of His servants with knowledge fear Allah.
Those who recite Allah's Book, pray and spend secretly and openly expect a profit that will never perish, and He will give them their rewards in full and more.
The Book revealed to the Prophet is the truth confirming what came before, and its chosen heirs include those who wrong themselves, the moderate, and the foremost in good deeds.
They will enter gardens of perpetual residence, wearing gold bracelets, pearls and silk, praising Allah who removed their sorrow and settled them where no fatigue or weariness touches them.
Disbelievers in Hell neither die nor find relief, and when they cry to be let out to do good, they are told they had time and a warner.
Allah knows the unseen of the heavens and earth and what is within the breasts.
Allah made people successors on earth, and whoever disbelieves bears his own disbelief, which only increases disbelievers in their Lord's hatred and in loss.
Those who invoke partners are asked what those partners created on earth, what share they hold in the heavens, or what scripture backs them; the wrongdoers promise only delusion.
Allah holds the heavens and earth from ceasing, and if they ceased no one after Him could hold them.
Quraysh and the Arabs swore a warner would make them better guided than any nation, yet when one came their aversion grew, through arrogance and evil plotting.
Traveling the land shows the end of earlier, stronger peoples, and nothing in the heavens or earth can thwart Allah.
If Allah held people to account for what they earned He would leave no creature on earth, but He defers them for a specified term.
By the wise Quran, the Prophet is among the messengers on a straight path, with revelation from the Exalted, the Merciful, to warn a people whose forefathers were not warned.
Most will not believe, shackled and screened so warning them makes no difference; the warning reaches only one who follows the message and fears the Most Merciful unseen.
Allah brings the dead to life and records what they sent ahead and left behind, with all things counted in a clear register.
Messengers to a city were called liars and threatened with stoning; a man urging his people to follow them was told to enter Paradise, and one shout extinguished his people.
Alas for the servants who ridiculed every messenger; many generations were destroyed and will not return, yet all will be brought before Allah.
Signs for them include the revived dead earth with grain and gardens, night, the sun and moon each set on its course, and the laden ship that carried their forefathers.
Disbelievers turn from every sign, answer the call to spend by asking why feed those Allah could feed, and ask when the promise comes; one blast will seize them disputing.
When the Horn is blown they hasten from their graves, asking who raised them, and with one blast all are brought before Allah, where no soul is wronged.
The people of Paradise and their spouses will be joyfully occupied, reclining in shade on adorned couches, with fruit and whatever they request, greeted with Peace from a Merciful Lord.
Criminals will be set apart and reminded that Allah forbade the children of Adam to worship Satan, a clear enemy, and told to burn in the Hellfire they were promised.
On that Day mouths will be sealed, and hands will speak and feet testify about what people earned.
Had Allah willed, He could have obliterated their eyes so they could not find the path, or deformed them in their places so they could neither go forward nor return.
Whomever Allah grants long life He reverses in creation.
Allah did not teach the Prophet poetry, which does not suit him; this is a message and a clear Quran to warn the living and justify the word against disbelievers.
Allah created and tamed livestock for people to own, ride and eat, with other benefits and drinks, so they should be grateful.
They took deities besides Allah hoping for help, but these cannot help them; the Prophet should not grieve at their words, for Allah knows what they hide and show.
Man, made from a sperm-drop, asks who will give life to disintegrated bones; He who made them the first time will, for He need only say Be, and it is.
By those lined up in rows, those who drive and those who recite, your God is One, Lord of the heavens, the earth, all between them and the sunrises.
Allah adorned the nearest heaven with stars as protection from every rebellious devil, which cannot listen to the exalted assembly and is pelted and pursued by a piercing flame.
Mocking signs as magic, disbelievers ask whether they and their forefathers will be raised after becoming dust and bones; yes, they will be made contemptible, raised by one shout.
On the Day of Recompense, wrongdoers and what they worshipped are led to the path of Hellfire and questioned; followers and misleaders blame each other, but all share the punishment.
Told there is no deity but Allah, they arrogantly asked whether to leave their gods for a mad poet, though the Prophet brought truth; they will taste painful punishment.
Allah's chosen servants enjoy fruits, thrones and a cup that does not intoxicate in gardens, and one looks to see his former companion, who doubted recompense, in the Hellfire.
The tree of zaqqum rises from the bottom of Hellfire; wrongdoers fill their bellies from it, drink scalding water and return to Hellfire, having hastened after fathers they found astray.
Most former peoples went astray though warners were sent among them; see how the warned ended, except Allah's chosen servants.
Noah called on Allah, who saved him and his family from the great affliction, made his descendants the survivors, left him peace among later generations, and drowned the disbelievers.
Abraham asked his father and people what they worshipped, said he was about to be ill, struck their carved gods, and Allah debased those who plotted to burn him.
Abraham, granted a forbearing boy, Ishmael, saw in a dream he must sacrifice him; both submitted and the boy was ransomed, then came good tidings of Isaac.
Allah favored Moses and Aaron, saved them and their people from great affliction under Pharaoh, made them prevail, gave them the clear Scripture, and left them peace among later generations.
Elias, a messenger, asked his people why they called on Ba'l and left Allah, the best of creators; they denied him and will be brought for punishment.
Lot, a messenger, was saved with all his family except his wife, the others were destroyed, and people pass by them morning and night.
Jonah fled to a ship, lost the lot, was swallowed by the fish, saved for exalting Allah, cast ashore ill, and sent to a hundred thousand or more, who believed.
Claims that Allah has daughters, that angels are female, that He has begotten, or has lineage with the jinn are lies, and Allah is exalted above what they describe.
The angels say each of them has a known position, and that they line up in rows and exalt Allah.
Quraysh used to say that with a message like the former peoples' they would be Allah's chosen servants, yet they disbelieved in it and will come to know.
Allah's word went before that His messengers would be helped to victory and His soldiers would overcome, so the Prophet is told to leave the disbelievers awhile until punishment descends.
Allah, Lord of might, is exalted above what they describe; peace be upon the messengers, and praise to Allah, Lord of the worlds.
By the Quran with its reminder, the disbelievers are in pride and dissension, though many generations before them were destroyed, crying out when there was no escape.
Disbelievers call the warner a lying magician who made the gods one God, urge patience over their gods and doubt the message, yet own no dominion and will be defeated.
The people of Noah, 'Aad, Pharaoh, Thamud, Lot's people and the companions of the thicket all denied the messengers, so Allah's penalty upon them was justified.
These disbelievers await only a single blast that will not be delayed, yet ask their Lord to hasten their share before the Day of Account.
Be patient and remember David, with whom mountains and birds praised Allah; tested by two disputants, he sought forgiveness and was told to judge with truth.
Allah did not create the heaven and earth aimlessly, as disbelievers assume, nor will He treat righteous believers like corrupters or the God-fearing like the wicked.
The Quran is a blessed Book revealed so people reflect on its verses and those of understanding are reminded.
Solomon, given to David, said love of good things diverted him from remembering his Lord; tried, he sought forgiveness and an unmatched kingdom and was given the wind and devils.
Job called to his Lord about Satan's hardship, was told to strike the ground for water, was given his family and as many more, and was found patient.
Abraham, Isaac and Jacob were chosen for remembering the Hereafter, and Ishmael, Elisha and Dhul-Kifl are among the outstanding.
The righteous have a good return in gardens of perpetual residence, reclining with fruit and drink, with women of equal age limiting their glances, a provision that never runs out.
Transgressors have an evil return in Hell, with scalding water and purulence, where followers and leaders quarrel and wonder where the men they ridiculed have gone.
The Prophet says he is only a clear warner, that there is no deity but Allah, the One, and that he had no knowledge of the exalted assembly's dispute.
All the angels prostrated to Adam, the human Allah made from clay, except Iblees, who arrogantly refused, was expelled, cursed and reprieved, and vowed to mislead all but the chosen.
The Prophet asks no payment for the Quran and is not pretentious; it is a reminder to the worlds whose truth they will know after a time.
The Quran is revealed in truth from Allah, the Exalted in Might, the Wise, so the Prophet is to worship Him with sincere religion.
Pure religion is Allah's; those worshipping protectors to draw nearer will be judged, and had He wanted a son He could have chosen one, but He is the One.
Allah created the heavens and earth in truth, wraps night over day, runs the sun and moon, and created people from one soul, forming them in wombs creation after creation.
If people disbelieve Allah is free of need of them, and He does not approve disbelief but approves gratitude; no soul bears another's burden, and all return to Him.
Man calls on his Lord in adversity but, once favored, forgets Him and sets up equals, unlike one praying devoutly at night, fearing the Hereafter and hoping for mercy.
Believers are told to fear their Lord; those who do good have good in this world, Allah's earth is spacious, and the patient are rewarded without account.
The Prophet is commanded to worship Allah sincerely and be the first Muslim, fearing a tremendous Day, while the losers lose themselves and their families amid canopies of fire.
Those who avoid worshipping Taghut and turn to Allah, listening to speech and following its best, receive good tidings; Allah has guided them, and they have understanding.
None can save one deserving punishment in the Fire, while those who feared their Lord have chambers built high above chambers, with rivers flowing beneath, Allah's promise.
Allah sends rain that flows as springs and grows crops of varied colors that dry, yellow and crumble, a parable of worldly life and a reminder for people of understanding.
Some breasts Allah opens to Islam, others harden against His remembrance; His Book, the best statement, makes the God-fearing shiver then soften, guiding whom He wills.
One shielding himself with his face from the worst punishment on Resurrection Day is not like the secure, and wrongdoers are told to taste what they earned.
Those before them denied, and punishment came from where they did not perceive, bringing disgrace in this life, while the punishment of the Hereafter is greater.
Allah has presented every kind of example in this Arabic Quran, free of any deviance, that people might remember and become righteous.
Allah's example of a slave owned by quarreling partners and one belonging to a single man shows they are not equal, though most people do not know.
The Prophet will die and so will Quraysh, and on the Day of Resurrection they will dispute before their Lord.
Liars about Allah who deny the truth have a residence in Hell, while those who bring and believe the truth will have whatever they desire with their Lord.
Allah suffices His Servant, though threatened with other gods that cannot remove harm or withhold mercy; relying on Him, the Prophet tells his people they will know who is disgraced.
Allah sent down the Book in truth for the people; whoever is guided benefits himself, whoever strays harms himself, and the Prophet is not their manager.
Allah takes souls at death and during sleep, keeping those decreed to die and releasing the others for a specified term.
Intercession belongs entirely to Allah, not to powerless intercessors people take, yet deniers of the Hereafter shrink at Allah's name alone and rejoice when others are mentioned.
The Prophet calls on Allah, Creator of the heavens and earth and Knower of the unseen and witnessed, to judge between His servants in their differences.
Wrongdoers would give the whole earth and as much again to ransom themselves on Resurrection Day, as the unexpected and the evils they earned appear before them.
Man calls on Allah in hardship but credits favor to his own knowledge, though it is a trial; earlier people said the same and suffered what they earned.
Allah tells His servants who sinned against themselves not to despair of His mercy, for He forgives all sins and is the Forgiving, the Merciful.
Turn to your Lord and submit before punishment comes suddenly, lest a soul regret its neglect, blame its lack of guidance or wish for another turn after denying His verses.
On Resurrection Day liars about Allah will have blackened faces and Hell will house the arrogant, while Allah saves the God-fearing from evil and grief.
Allah is the Creator and Disposer of all things and holds the keys of the heavens and earth, and those who disbelieve in His verses are the losers.
The Prophet refuses to worship other than Allah, for he and those before were told associating partners voids one's work, and he is to worship Allah alone and be grateful.
People have not valued Allah rightly; on Resurrection Day the earth is in His grip, the Horn is blown twice, records are placed, and all are judged justly.
Disbelievers will be driven in groups to Hell and the God-fearing in groups to Paradise, which they enter praising Allah, while angels surround the Throne exalting their Lord.
The Book is revealed from Allah, the Exalted in Might, the Knowing, who forgives sin, accepts repentance and is severe in punishment; there is no deity but Him.
Only disbelievers dispute Allah's signs; Noah's people and later factions also denied, plotted against their messengers and were seized, and the disbelievers are companions of the Fire.
The angels carrying the Throne and those around it praise their Lord and ask Him to forgive believers, admit them and their righteous families to gardens, and protect them.
Disbelievers are told Allah's hatred of them exceeded their hatred of themselves; they confess their sins and ask for a way out, having disbelieved when Allah was called upon alone.
Allah shows His signs and sends provision from the sky, but only those who turn back remember; so invoke Allah sincerely in religion, though the disbelievers dislike it.
Allah inspires whom He wills to warn of the Day of Meeting, when nothing is hidden, all sovereignty is His, every soul is recompensed and wrongdoers have no intercessor.
Those before, stronger and more established in the land, disbelieved in the clear proofs their messengers brought, so Allah seized them for their sins.
Moses is sent with signs to Pharaoh, Haman and Qarun, who call him a magician and liar, order the believers' sons killed, and Pharaoh threatens to kill Moses.
A believer from Pharaoh's family warns his people against killing Moses and calls them to Allah; Pharaoh orders a tower, Allah protects the believer and Pharaoh's people face the Fire.
In the Fire the weak ask the arrogant they followed for relief, and all ask Hell's keepers to pray for them, who remind them their messengers brought clear proofs.
Allah will support His messengers and the believers in this world and on the Day the witnesses stand, when the wrongdoers' excuses will not benefit them.
Allah gave Moses guidance and made the Children of Israel inherit the Scripture as guidance and a reminder for people of understanding.
The Prophet is told to be patient, for Allah's promise is true, to ask forgiveness for his sin, and to exalt his Lord with praise evening and morning.
Those who dispute Allah's signs without any authority have only pride in their breasts that they will never attain, so seek refuge in Allah, the Hearing, the Seeing.
The creation of the heavens and earth is greater than the creation of mankind, so recreating people is easy for Allah, but most people do not know.
The blind and the seeing are not equal, nor are those who believe and do righteous deeds equal to the evildoer.
The Hour is certainly coming, without doubt, but most people do not believe.
Your Lord says to call upon Him and He will respond, and those too proud to worship Him will enter Hell in disgrace.
Allah made night for rest and day for sight, the earth a settlement and the sky a ceiling, and formed and provided for people; He is Creator of all things.
There is no deity but the Ever-Living, so call on Him sincerely; the Prophet is forbidden to worship others and commanded to submit to the Lord of the worlds.
Allah creates people from dust, a sperm-drop and a clinging clot, bringing them to childhood, maturity and old age; He gives life and death and says 'Be' and it is.
Those who dispute Allah's signs and deny the Book will be dragged in chains through boiling water into the Fire, find their partners gone, and enter Hell's gates forever.
The Prophet is told to be patient, for Allah's promise is true; whether he sees some of it or is taken in death first, they will be returned to Allah.
Messengers were sent before, some whose stories are told and some not, and no messenger brought a sign except by Allah's permission.
Allah made grazing animals for riding, eating and other benefits, and ships to carry people; these are His signs, and they are asked which of them they deny.
Earlier, stronger nations rejoiced in their own knowledge and rejected their messengers; when they saw the punishment they believed in Allah alone, but that faith did not benefit them.
A revelation from the Entirely Merciful: a detailed Arabic Quran bringing good tidings and warning, though most turn away, saying their hearts are covered and their ears deaf.
The Prophet is only a man to whom it is revealed that God is one; woe to those who associate others with Allah, give no zakah and deny the Hereafter.
Those who believe and do righteous deeds will have an uninterrupted reward.
Allah created the earth in two days, its mountains and sustenance in four, then turned to the heaven, which was smoke, making seven heavens and adorning the nearest with lamps.
Those who turn away are warned of a thunderbolt like that of 'Aad and Thamud; arrogant 'Aad met a screaming wind, Thamud preferred blindness to guidance, and believers were saved.
The enemies of Allah gathered to the Fire find their hearing, eyes and skins testifying against them, ruined by assuming Allah did not know much of what they did.
Companions make their sins attractive; disbelievers urge others to speak noisily over the Quran, and in the Fire they ask to trample the jinn and men who misled them.
Angels descend on those who say 'Our Lord is Allah' and stay on a right course, telling them not to fear or grieve and giving them good tidings of Paradise.
None speaks better than one who invites to Allah and does righteousness; good and evil are not equal, so repel evil with what is better, granted only to the patient.
If an evil suggestion comes from Satan, seek refuge in Allah, the Hearing, the Knowing.
Night and day, the sun and moon are His signs, so prostrate to Allah, not to them; rain reviving the still earth shows He gives life to the dead.
Those who inject deviation into Allah's verses are not hidden; the Quran is a mighty Book falsehood cannot approach, guidance and cure for believers, deafness and blindness for others.
Moses was given the Scripture but it came under disagreement, and only a prior word from Allah kept it from being settled; they are in doubt about the Quran.
Whoever does good does it for himself, whoever does evil does it against himself, and Allah is never unjust to His servants.
Knowledge of the Hour, of every fruit and every pregnancy is with Allah alone; on the Day He asks for His 'partners', those they invoked will be lost to them.
Man never tires of asking for good yet despairs in evil; given mercy he claims it as his due and doubts the Hour, and favored he turns away.
If the Quran is from Allah, rejecting it is extreme error; He will show His signs in the horizons and in themselves until it is clear it is the truth.
Allah, the Exalted in Might, the Wise, reveals to the Prophet as He revealed to those before him.
All in the heavens and earth belongs to Allah, the Most High; the heavens almost break as the angels exalt Him and ask forgiveness for those on earth.
Allah is Guardian over those who take allies other than Him, and the Prophet is not their manager.
The Arabic Quran warns the Mother of Cities of the Day of Assembly: one party in Paradise, one in the Blaze; Allah admits whom He wills to His mercy.
Those who take protectors besides Allah are told that Allah is the Protector, who gives life to the dead and is competent over all things.
Any disagreement is referred to Allah for judgement; the Prophet declares that Allah is his Lord, on whom he relies and to whom he turns back.
The Creator of the heavens and earth made mates for people and cattle; nothing is like Him, and He holds their keys, extending or restricting provision.
Allah ordained the religion He enjoined on Noah, Abraham, Moses and Jesus, to establish it undivided; people divided out of jealousy; the Prophet must invite to it and stay upright.
Those arguing about Allah have invalid arguments; Allah sent down the Book and the balance, the Hour may be near, and disputers about it are in extreme error.
Allah is Subtle with His servants, provides for whom He wills, and is the Powerful, the Exalted in Might.
Whoever seeks the harvest of the Hereafter is given more of it, while whoever seeks this world is given some of it but no share in the Hereafter.
They are asked whether other deities ordained for them a religion Allah did not consent to; but for the decisive word it would be settled, and wrongdoers face painful punishment.
Wrongdoers will fear what they earned, while believers who do righteous deeds will have whatever they wish in gardens; the Prophet asks no payment, only good will through kinship.
Some say the Prophet invented a lie about Allah, but Allah could seal his heart if He willed, and He erases falsehood and establishes truth by His words.
Allah accepts repentance, pardons misdeeds and answers believers; He sends provision in measure lest people commit tyranny, and sends rain after despair, spreading His mercy.
Among Allah's signs are the creation of the heavens and earth and the creatures He dispersed in them, and He is able to gather them when He wills.
Whatever disaster strikes you is for what your hands earned, though Allah pardons much; you cannot escape Him on earth or find any protector besides Him.
Ships like mountains are His signs; He could still the wind or destroy them for what they earned, but pardons much, and disputers of His signs have no escape.
Worldly things are passing enjoyment; what is with Allah is better for believers who rely on Him, avoid major sins, forgive, pray, consult, spend and defend themselves against tyranny.
An evil may be repaid with its like, and the wronged who avenge themselves are not blamed, but whoever pardons and reconciles is rewarded by Allah, and forgiving shows resolve.
Those Allah sends astray have no protector; the wrongdoers will ask to return, be exposed to the Fire in humiliation, and the believers will call them the true losers.
People are told to respond to their Lord before a Day comes from Allah that cannot be repelled, when they will have no refuge and no denial.
If they turn away, the Prophet's duty is only to convey; man rejoices when given mercy but, when evil strikes for his own deeds, is ungrateful.
To Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and earth; He gives daughters or sons or both to whom He wills, and makes whom He wills barren.
Allah speaks to a human only by revelation, from behind a partition or through a messenger; so He revealed to the Prophet a light that guides to Allah's straight path.
By the clear Book, Allah made it an Arabic Quran to be understood, exalted in the Mother of the Book, and will not turn the message away from transgressors.
Every prophet sent to former peoples was ridiculed, and Allah destroyed peoples greater in power than these.
They admit the Exalted, the Knowing created the heavens and earth; He made the earth a bed, sends rain, and gave ships and animals to ride, exalting Him when mounted.
They assign Allah daughters, leaving sons for themselves, grieve at such news, call the angels females, and claim Allah willed their worship, without knowledge.
They follow their fathers' religion without any book, as every city's affluent told its warners; offered better guidance they still disbelieved, and Allah took retribution on them.
Abraham disassociated himself from what his father and people worshipped, except his Creator who will guide him, and left this word among his descendants.
When truth and a clear Messenger came, they called it magic and asked why the Quran was not sent to a great man; Allah apportions livelihood, His mercy being better.
Were it not that people would become one community, Allah would give disbelievers houses of silver and gold, yet that is worldly enjoyment, and the Hereafter is for the righteous.
Whoever is blinded from the remembrance of the Most Merciful is given a devil companion who averts him while he thinks himself guided, until he regrets it on the Day.
The Prophet cannot make the deaf hear; Allah will take retribution whether or not he sees it, so he holds to the revelation, a reminder for him and his people.
The earlier messengers can be asked whether Allah ever made deities to be worshipped besides the Most Merciful.
Moses brought signs to Pharaoh and his establishment, who laughed and broke their word when affliction lifted; Pharaoh boasted of his kingdom and belittled Moses, and his people were drowned.
When the son of Mary was given as an example, people laughed; Jesus was a favored servant who brought clear proofs and told them to worship Allah, but sects differed.
They await only the Hour coming suddenly, when close friends will become enemies to each other except the righteous.
Allah's servants who believed in His verses and were Muslims enter Paradise without fear or grief, with gold vessels, whatever souls desire and much fruit, forever, for what they did.
The criminals abide in Hell's punishment in despair, calling on Malik to end them, but are told they will remain, having been averse to the truth.
If they devise a plan, Allah also devises; He hears their secrets and private talk, and His messengers with them are recording.
The Lord of the heavens and earth is above having a son; He alone is deity in heaven and earth, knows the Hour, and those invoked besides Him cannot intercede.
The Prophet's saying that these people do not believe is acknowledged; he is told to turn aside from them and say 'Peace', for they will come to know.
By the clear Book, Allah sent it down to warn on a blessed night, the Night of Decree, when every precise matter is made distinct, as mercy from your Lord.
He is Lord of the heavens and earth; there is no deity but Him, who gives life and death, Lord of you and of your first forefathers.
Doubters are to watch for the Day the sky brings visible smoke covering people; they will plead belief despite rejecting a clear Messenger, and once relieved will return.
Pharaoh's people were tried when Moses, a noble messenger, asked for Allah's servants; he left by night with them, and the army drowned, leaving gardens and springs to another people.
Allah saved the Children of Israel from Pharaoh's humiliating torment, chose them knowingly over the worlds, and gave them signs containing a clear trial.
These people say there is only the first death and no resurrection, demanding their forefathers back; yet the people of Tubba' and those before them were destroyed as criminals.
Allah did not create the heavens, the earth and what is between them in play, but in truth, though most do not know.
The Day of Judgement is the appointed time for all, when no relative can help another, except those on whom Allah has mercy.
The tree of zaqqum is food for the sinful, boiling in their bellies; the sinner is dragged into Hellfire, scalding water poured on his head, and mocked as 'the honored'.
The righteous are secure among gardens and springs, in silk, married to fair women with large eyes, with every fruit, tasting no death but the first, protected from Hellfire.
The Quran is made easy in the Prophet's tongue so they may be reminded; so watch, for they are watching.
The revelation of the Book is from Allah, the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
The heavens and earth, people and creatures, night and day, provision sent from the sky to revive the earth, and the winds are signs for those who believe and reason.
Woe to every sinful liar who hears Allah's verses yet persists arrogantly or takes them in ridicule; Hell is before him, while this Quran is guidance.
Allah subjected the sea for ships and all in the heavens and earth to people, signs for those who give thought.
Believers are told to forgive those who do not expect Allah's days, for He will recompense each people; good and evil deeds count for or against the doer.
Allah gave the Children of Israel the Scripture, judgement and prophethood, provision and preference, but they differed after knowledge out of jealousy, and He will judge between them.
The Prophet must follow an ordained way, not the desires of those who do not know; wrongdoers ally together, Allah protects the righteous, and this Quran is guidance.
Evildoers will not be made equal to righteous believers in life and death; Allah created the heavens and earth in truth so every soul is recompensed without wrong.
Whoever takes his own desire as his god, Allah sends astray and seals his hearing and heart; none can guide him after Allah.
They say there is only worldly life and time destroys them, and demand their forefathers back; Allah gives life and death and will assemble them for the Day of Resurrection.
When the Hour comes every nation kneels, called to its record; believers enter Allah's mercy, while disbelievers who mocked His verses and doubted the Hour are left in the Fire.
All praise and grandeur in the heavens and earth belong to Allah, Lord of the worlds, the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
The revelation of the Book is from Allah, the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
Allah created the heavens and earth in truth and for a specified term, but the disbelievers turn away from what they are warned of.
Worshippers are challenged to show anything their invoked partners created; these will not answer them until the Day of Resurrection, then become their enemies and deny their worship.
Disbelievers call the recited verses magic, invention or ancient falsehood; the Prophet only follows revelation as a warner, and after Moses' scripture this is a confirming Book in Arabic.
Those who say 'Our Lord is Allah' and stay on a right course will have no fear or grief, abiding in Paradise as a reward.
Man is enjoined to treat his parents well; the grateful and repentant are accepted, while one scorning his parents and denying resurrection is lost, among those exposed to the Fire.
Hud, the brother of 'Aad, warned his people at al-Ahqaf to worship only Allah; they demanded the punishment, and the cloud they thought brought rain was a destroying wind.
Allah destroyed the cities around them after varied signs, and the deities they took besides Allah did not help them.
A few jinn listened to the Quran and returned as warners, telling their people of a Book revealed after Moses and urging them to respond to Allah's Messenger.
Allah, who created the heavens and earth without failing, can give life to the dead, and disbelievers exposed to the Fire will confess it is the truth.
The Prophet is told to be patient like the messengers of determination; on the Day they see what they are promised, it will seem they stayed only an hour.
Allah wastes the deeds of disbelievers who avert people from His way, and removes the misdeeds of believers who believe in what was sent down upon Muhammad, the truth.
In battle believers are to strike the disbelievers' necks and, after slaughter, bind captives to free by favor or ransom; those killed in Allah's cause will enter Paradise.
Allah supports believers who support Him; disbelievers who disliked His revelation have misery and wasted deeds and face the fate of those before, for they have no protector.
Believers enter gardens while disbelievers eat like livestock and dwell in the Fire; stronger cities were destroyed; Paradise's rivers of water, milk, wine and honey are set against scalding water.
Hypocrites listen to the Prophet then ask what he just said, their hearts sealed as they follow desires, while Allah increases the guided in guidance and righteousness.
They wait only for the Hour to come suddenly, though its indications have come, and remembrance will not help them then.
The Prophet is told to know that there is no deity but Allah and to ask forgiveness for his sin and for believing men and women.
When a surah mentions fighting, those with hypocrisy look as if dying; obedience would be better, and those who turn away, cause corruption and sever kinship are cursed.
They are asked whether they do not reflect upon the Quran, or whether there are locks upon their hearts.
Those who turned back after guidance, enticed by Satan, will die with angels striking them; Allah will expose the hidden hatred of those with diseased hearts, known by their speech.
Allah will test the believers until He makes evident those who strive and are patient.
Disbelievers who avert people from Allah's path and oppose the Messenger cannot harm Him and are not forgiven if they die so; believers must obey Allah and the Messenger.
Believers are told not to weaken and call for peace while they are superior, for Allah is with them and will not deprive them of their deeds.
Worldly life is amusement and diversion; Allah does not ask believers for their wealth, yet some withhold when invited to spend in His cause, withholding only from themselves.
Revealed after Hudaybiyyah: Allah gave the Prophet a clear conquest, to forgive his past and future sins, complete His favor, guide him and aid him with mighty victory.
Allah sent tranquillity into the believers' hearts at Hudaybiyyah to increase their faith, and will admit believing men and women to eternal gardens and remove their misdeeds.
Allah will punish the hypocrite and polytheist men and women who assume evil of Him, curse them and prepare Hell; the soldiers of the heavens and earth are His.
The Prophet is sent as a witness, bringer of good tidings and warner, so people believe in Allah and His Messenger, honor him and exalt Allah morning and afternoon.
Those who pledged allegiance to the Prophet at Hudaybiyyah pledged to Allah, His hand over theirs; whoever breaks it harms himself, and whoever fulfills it earns great reward.
Bedouins who stayed behind from Hudaybiyyah make excuses and seek booty; called to face a mighty people, they are rewarded if they obey; the blind, lame and ill are excused.
Allah was pleased with the believers who pledged allegiance under the tree at Hudaybiyyah, sent them tranquillity, and rewarded them with an imminent conquest, much booty and further victories.
Allah held back each side's hands within Makkah, where disbelievers barred believers from al-Masjid al-Haram; He sent tranquillity and showed His Messenger a true vision of entering it safely.
Allah sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth to make it prevail over all religion, and Allah is sufficient as Witness.
Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, and those with him are forceful against disbelievers, merciful among themselves, marked by prostration, and described in the Torah and Gospel.
Believers must not put themselves before Allah and His Messenger or raise voices above the Prophet's; those lowering them are rewarded, and callers from behind the chambers should be patient.
If a disobedient person brings information, investigate it, lest you harm a people out of ignorance and come to regret it.
The Messenger of Allah is among them; Allah has made faith beloved and disbelief hateful to them, as bounty and favor from Him.
If two groups of believers fight, make settlement, fight the one that oppresses until it returns to Allah's ordinance, then settle justly, for believers are brothers.
Believers must not ridicule, insult or use offensive nicknames, nor assume much, spy or backbite, which is likened to eating a dead brother's flesh.
Allah created people from male and female, made them peoples and tribes to know one another, and the most noble of them before Allah is the most righteous.
Bedouins who say they believe are told to say they submitted, as faith has not entered their hearts; believers do not doubt but strive; guidance to faith is Allah's favor.
By the honored Quran, the disbelievers wonder at a warner from among them and reject returning after becoming dust, though Allah knows what the earth takes of them.
The built and adorned heaven, the spread earth with mountains and plants, and rain bringing gardens, grain and palms to dead land are reminders, and thus is the resurrection.
Noah's people, the companions of the well, Thamud, 'Aad, Pharaoh, Lot's brothers, the companions of the thicket and Tubba's people all denied the messengers and met the threat.
Allah did not fail in the first creation, yet they are in confusion over a new creation.
Allah created man and knows what his soul whispers, being closer than his jugular vein, while two receivers on his right and left record every word.
The intoxication of death brings the truth that man was trying to avoid.
When the Horn is blown each soul comes with a driver and a witness; every obstinate disbeliever is thrown into Hell, his companion disowns him, and Allah wrongs no one.
Hell is asked if it is full and asks for more, while Paradise is brought near to the righteous who returned to Allah, entering in peace with whatever they wish.
Allah destroyed many generations greater in power who explored the lands, with no escape; that is a reminder for whoever has a heart or listens attentively.
Allah created the heavens, the earth and what is between them in six days, and no weariness touched Him.
The Prophet is told to be patient over what they say and to exalt his Lord with praise before sunrise and sunset, in the night and after prostration.
On the Day the Caller calls and the blast is heard, people emerge from the earth swiftly; Allah gives life and death, and this gathering is easy for Him.
Allah knows what they say; the Prophet is not a tyrant over them but is to remind with the Quran whoever fears the threat.
By the scattering winds, laden clouds, sailing ships and apportioning angels, what you are promised is true and the recompense will occur.
By the heaven with pathways, people differ in speech; the heedless falsifiers deluded from the Quran ask when the Day of Recompense is, and will be tormented over the Fire.
The righteous, doers of good who slept little at night, asked forgiveness before dawn and gave the needy their right, will be among gardens and springs.
There are signs on earth and in yourselves, and in the heaven is your provision and what you are promised; by the Lord of heaven and earth, it is true.
Abraham serves his honored guests a fat calf; they give him tidings of a learned boy, and his wife cries out that she is a barren old woman.
The messengers tell Abraham they are sent against Lot's criminal people with stones of clay; the one household of believers is brought out, and a sign is left there.
Moses was sent to Pharaoh with clear authority, but Pharaoh turned away calling him a magician or madman, so Allah cast him and his soldiers into the sea.
'Aad were destroyed by a barren wind, Thamud were seized by a thunderbolt after defying their Lord, and Noah's people before them were defiantly disobedient.
Allah built the heaven with strength and expands it, spread out the earth, and created all things in pairs so you may remember.
People are told to flee to Allah and not set up another deity with Him, by a clear warner from Him.
Every messenger before was called a magician or madman by a transgressing people; the Prophet is told to leave them, not being blamed, and to remind, for reminding benefits believers.
Allah created jinn and mankind only to worship Him; He wants no provision or food from them, for He is the Provider, the firm possessor of strength.
The wrongdoers will have a portion of punishment like their predecessors', so let them not hasten it; woe to the disbelievers from their promised Day.
By the mount, an inscribed Book, the frequented House, the raised heaven and the filled sea, your Lord's punishment will occur, on the Day the heaven sways and mountains depart.
Woe that Day to the deniers amusing themselves; thrust into Hell, they are asked whether the Fire they denied is magic, and burn, patient or not, for what they did.
The righteous enjoy gardens, food and drink on thrones, married to fair women with large eyes, joined by believing descendants, with fruit, meat and a sinless cup, recalling Allah's protection.
The Prophet, no soothsayer or madman, is told to keep reminding; to those who call him a poet and await his misfortune, he says, 'Wait,' for he waits with them.
Those who say he made it up do not believe; let them produce a statement like it if they are truthful.
They are asked whether they created themselves or the heavens, hold their Lord's depositories, know the unseen or have a deity besides Allah, who is exalted above what they associate.
Even seeing part of the sky fall, they would call it heaped clouds; so leave them to their Day, when their plan fails, and the wrongdoers face punishment before that.
The Prophet is told to be patient for his Lord's decision, being in His sight, and to exalt Him with praise on rising, at night and after the stars set.
By the star, the Prophet has not strayed; his words are revelation taught by Gabriel, intense in strength, whom he saw near and again at the Lote Tree.
Al-Lat, al-'Uzza and Manat are mere names without authority from Allah, an unjust division giving Him females; those who named them follow assumption and desire, though guidance came.
The angels' intercession avails only with Allah's permission; those who disbelieve in the Hereafter give angels female names, following assumption without knowledge.
Turn away from whoever ignores the message and wants only worldly life; that is all they know, and Allah knows best who strays and who is guided.
Allah repays evildoers for their deeds and rewards those who do good, who avoid major sins and immoralities, with the best; He is vast in forgiveness, so claim no purity.
One who turned away and gave little is reminded that the scriptures of Moses and Abraham say no one bears another's burden and each has only what he strives for.
To Allah is the final return; He makes people laugh and weep, gives death and life, creates male and female from a sperm-drop, enriches, and is Lord of Sirius.
Allah destroyed the first 'Aad, Thamud and Noah's people, who were more unjust, and hurled down the overturned towns, then asks which of His favors people doubt.
The Prophet is a warner like those before; the Approaching Day has drawn near and none but Allah can remove it, so prostrate to Allah and worship Him.
The Hour has come near and the moon has split, yet seeing a miracle they turn away calling it passing magic, follow their inclinations, and warning does not avail them.
The Prophet is to leave them; when the Caller calls, they will emerge from graves like spreading locusts, racing to him, and disbelievers will call it a difficult Day.
Noah's people called him a madman, so he prayed for help; rain poured and springs burst, he was carried on planks, and the Quran is made easy to remember.
'Aad, the people of Hud, denied, so Allah sent a screaming wind on a day of continuous misfortune, uprooting people like palm trunks; the Quran is made easy for remembrance.
Thamud rejected following Salih, one human among them, as an insolent liar; the she-camel was a trial with shared water, their companion hamstrung her, and one blast destroyed them.
Lot's people denied the warning and demanded his guests, so Allah sent a storm of stones and obliterated their eyes, saving Lot's family before dawn as a favor.
A warning came to Pharaoh's people through Moses and Aaron, but they denied all Allah's signs, so He seized them with the seizure of one Exalted in Might.
The disbelievers of Quraysh are asked if they are better than earlier peoples or immune by scripture; their assembly will be defeated and flee, and the Hour is their appointment.
The criminals are in error and madness; on the Day they are dragged into the Fire on their faces, they will be told to taste the touch of Saqar.
Allah created all things with predestination, His command is done like a glance of the eye, and He has already destroyed your kinds.
Everything they did is in written records, and every small and great thing is inscribed.
The righteous will be among gardens and rivers, in a seat of honor near a Sovereign, Perfect in Ability.
The Most Merciful taught the Quran, created man and taught him eloquence.
The sun and moon move by precise calculation, and the stars and trees prostrate.
Allah raised the heaven and set the balance, so do not transgress in it; establish weight in justice and do not make the balance deficient.
Allah laid out the earth for the creatures, with fruit, palm trees, grain and scented plants, then asks which of your Lord's favors you would deny.
Allah created man from clay like pottery and the jinn from a smokeless flame of fire.
He is Lord of the two sunrises and two sunsets, released the two seas with a barrier between them yielding pearl and coral, and owns ships like mountains.
Everyone on earth will perish, and the Face of your Lord, Owner of Majesty and Honor, will remain.
All in the heavens and earth ask of Him, and every day He is bringing about a matter.
Jinn and mankind will be attended to and cannot pass beyond heaven and earth without authority; flame and smoke will come, the heaven will split, and none asked about sin.
The criminals are known by their marks and seized by forelocks and feet; this is the Hell they denied, where they go between it and scalding water.
Whoever feared his Lord's position will have two gardens with flowing springs, two kinds of every fruit, silk-lined beds and women of restrained glance; the reward for good is good.
Below these two are two other dark green gardens with two spouting springs, fruit, palm trees and pomegranates, good and beautiful women reserved in pavilions, and green cushions and carpets.
Blessed is the name of your Lord, Owner of Majesty and Honor.
When the Occurrence comes it lowers some and raises others; the earth shakes, mountains crumble to dust, and people become three groups: right, left and forerunners.
The forerunners, brought near, many from the former peoples and few from the later, recline on thrones in the Gardens of Pleasure with drink, fruit, fowl and fair women.
The companions of the right, from the former and the later peoples, enjoy thornless lote trees, extended shade, flowing water, abundant fruit, raised beds and the women of Paradise.
The companions of the left, who lived in luxury, persisted in the great violation and doubted being raised, will have scorching fire, scalding water, black smoke and the zaqqum tree.
Allah, who created people from the fluid they emit and decreed death among them, can recreate them in a form they do not know, as the first creation shows.
Allah asks who grows the sown seed, sends down drinking water and produced the tree for fire; He could ruin crops and water, so exalt the name of your Lord.
By the setting stars, this is a noble Quran in a protected Register, touched only by the purified and revealed by the Lord of the worlds, yet people are indifferent.
No one can bring back a dying soul; those brought near get rest and a garden, the right are greeted with peace, and astray deniers get scalding water and Hellfire.
All in the heavens and earth exalts Allah, who holds their dominion, gives life and death, created them in six days, knows all things and merges night and day.
Believe and spend from what Allah made you successors over; those who spent and fought before the conquest rank higher, and a goodly loan to Allah is multiplied.
On the Day believers walk with their light, the hypocrites beg to share it, a wall with a door separates them, and no ransom saves the hypocrites from the Fire.
Believers are asked whether their hearts should not humble at Allah's remembrance, unlike earlier Scripture holders whose hearts hardened; Allah gives life to the earth after its lifelessness.
Men and women who give charity and loan Allah a goodly loan will have it multiplied and receive a noble reward.
Believers in Allah and His messengers are the supporters of truth and the martyrs with their Lord, while those who disbelieve and deny His verses are companions of Hellfire.
Worldly life is amusement, adornment, boasting, rivalry in wealth and children, withering like plants after rain; race toward Allah's forgiveness and a Garden as wide as the heavens and earth.
Every disaster is in a register before it happens, so people neither despair over loss nor exult over gain; Allah does not like the boastful who are stingy.
Allah sent messengers with Scripture and the balance for justice and sent down iron; He sent Noah and Abraham, then Jesus with the Gospel, whose followers innovated monasticism.
Believers who fear Allah and believe in His Messenger receive a double portion of mercy, a light and forgiveness, and the People of the Scripture learn all bounty is Allah's.
Allah heard a woman's complaint about her husband; a man who pronounces thihar and retracts must free a slave, fast two months or feed sixty poor before touching his wife.
Those who oppose Allah and His Messenger are abased like those before them, and on the Day Allah resurrects them He will inform them of what they did.
Allah knows all in the heavens and earth; no three converse privately but He is the fourth, nor five but He is the sixth, wherever they are.
The Jews, forbidden secret talk, returned to conversing about sin and disobeying the Messenger, talk from Satan to grieve believers; believers may confer only about righteousness and piety.
Believers should make room in gatherings and rise when told; Allah raises the believers and those given knowledge by degrees.
Believers wishing to consult the Messenger privately should first give charity, and if they do not, establish prayer, give zakah and obey Allah and His Messenger.
Hypocrites who ally with a people Allah is angry with, belonging to neither side, swear falsely, avert others from Allah's way and are the losing party of Satan.
Allah's opponents will be most humbled, as Allah and His messengers prevail; believers keep no affection for them, even close kin, and are Allah's successful party.
Allah expelled Banu An-Nadir, disbelievers among the People of the Scripture, from their homes and fortresses, casting terror into their hearts for opposing Him and His Messenger.
Property restored to the Messenger without fighting belongs to Allah, the Messenger, relatives, orphans and travelers, not the rich alone; take what he gives, refrain from what he forbids.
Shares also go to the poor emigrants driven from their homes, to those settled in al-Madinah who love and prefer them, and to those after them who pray for forgiveness.
Hypocrites falsely promised to stand by Banu An-Nadir, their disbelieving brothers among the People of the Scripture, but would desert them as Satan deserts man; both end in the Fire.
Believers must fear Allah, look to what they send ahead for tomorrow and not be like those who forgot Allah; the people of the Fire and Paradise are not equal.
Had this Quran been sent down on a mountain, it would have humbled itself and split apart from fear of Allah.
He is Allah, besides whom there is no deity: Knower of the unseen, Most Merciful, Sovereign, Pure, Creator, Fashioner, to whom belong the best names and whom all things exalt.
Believers must not take Allah's enemies as allies with affection, for they drove out the Prophet and the believers and would harm them; relatives will not help on Resurrection Day.
Abraham and his companions set an excellent example, disowning their people and their worship besides Allah, except Abraham's promise to seek forgiveness for his father, and relying on Allah.
Allah does not forbid kindness and justice toward those who neither fight believers over religion nor expel them, but forbids taking as allies those who do.
Believing women who emigrate are examined and not returned to the disbelievers; believers may marry them after giving their due, and what each side spent on wives is repaid.

Believing women pledging to the Prophet not to associate others with Allah, steal, commit unlawful intercourse, kill their children, slander or disobey him are accepted, with forgiveness sought for them.
Believers must not ally with a people Allah is angry with, who have despaired of the Hereafter.
All creation exalts Allah; believers are asked why they say what they do not do, which is greatly hateful to Allah.
Allah loves those who fight in His cause in ranks, as though they were one firmly joined structure.
Moses asked his people why they harmed him though they knew he was Allah's messenger; when they deviated, Allah made their hearts deviate.
Jesus, son of Mary, told the Children of Israel he was Allah's messenger, confirming the Torah and giving good tidings of a messenger named Ahmad, but they called it magic.
None is more unjust than one who lies about Allah; disbelievers want to extinguish Allah's light, but He perfects it, sending His Messenger with the religion of truth.
Believers are offered a saving transaction: believe and strive with wealth and lives, gaining forgiveness, gardens, lasting dwellings, victory from Allah and an imminent conquest.
Believers are told to be Allah's supporters as the disciples of Jesus were; some of the Children of Israel believed, and Allah supported them against their enemy.
Allah, whom all creation exalts, sent the unlettered a Messenger from among them to recite His verses, purify them and teach them the Book and wisdom, a bounty from Allah.
Those entrusted with the Torah who did not take it on are like a donkey carrying books; Jews claiming to be Allah's allies are challenged to wish for death.
When called to prayer on Friday, believers must leave trade for Allah's remembrance, then disperse and seek His bounty; some left the Prophet standing for trade or amusement.

The hypocrites swear they believe the Messenger but lie, hide behind oaths, arrogantly refuse his seeking forgiveness for them, urge withholding spending and boast of expelling the humble from al-Madinah.
Believers must not let their wealth and children divert them from remembering Allah, or they will be the losers.
Spend from Allah's provision before death comes and one begs for a brief delay to give charity, for Allah delays no soul when its time has come.
All creation exalts Allah, who owns dominion and praise; He created people, some disbelieving and some believing, created the heavens and earth in truth and perfected human forms.
Allah knows what is in the heavens and earth, what people conceal and declare, and what lies within the breasts.
Earlier disbelievers tasted the result of their deeds because they rejected their messengers' clear evidences, asking whether mere humans would guide them.
Disbelievers claim they will never be resurrected, but they surely will be and will be told what they did, so believe in Allah, His Messenger and the Quran.
On the Day of Assembly, the Day of Deprivation, believers who do righteousness enter gardens with misdeeds removed, while those who deny Allah's verses abide in the Fire.
No disaster strikes except by Allah's permission and He guides the believer's heart, so obey Allah and the Messenger and rely on Allah, besides whom there is no deity.
Some wives and children are enemies to believers, so beware, yet if they pardon, Allah is Forgiving; wealth and children are only a trial, and Allah has a great reward.
Fear Allah as far as able, listen, obey and spend; whoever is saved from his soul's stinginess succeeds, and Allah multiplies a goodly loan and forgives.
Divorce women for their waiting period, keep them housed, retain or part fairly before two witnesses, keep the set term for each case, and spend on pregnant and nursing women.
Many towns that defied their Lord and His messengers were severely punished and lost, so those of understanding should fear Allah, who has sent down the Quran.
Allah sent a Messenger reciting His clear verses to bring those who believe and do righteous deeds out of darkness into light, and into gardens forever.
Allah created seven heavens and of the earth the like of them, His command descending among them, so people know His power over all things and all-encompassing knowledge.
The Prophet forbade himself the lawful to please his wives; after a wife disclosed his secret, two are urged to repent, and all told he could have better wives.
Believers must guard themselves and their families from a Fire fueled by people and stones, kept by stern angels; disbelievers are told that Day that excuses are useless.
Believers are told to repent sincerely so Allah may remove their misdeeds and admit them to gardens, their light running before them as they ask Him to perfect it.
The Prophet is told to strive against the disbelievers and hypocrites and be harsh with them; their refuge is Hell.
Allah's examples: the wives of Noah and Lot, who betrayed their husbands and were told to enter the Fire, and the believing wife of Pharaoh and Mary, daughter of 'Imran.
Blessed is He who holds dominion, created death and life to test who is best in deeds, and made seven flawless heavens, adorning the nearest with stars thrown at devils.
Hell boils and nearly bursts with rage; its keepers ask each company whether a warner came, and they admit they denied him and wish they had listened or reasoned.
Those who fear their Lord unseen will have forgiveness and a great reward.
Whether people hide or publicize their speech, Allah knows what is within the breasts, for He created them and is the Subtle, the Acquainted.
Allah made the earth easy to walk and eat from; none is safe from Him making it swallow them or sending a storm of stones, as earlier deniers found.
Only the Most Merciful holds birds aloft, aids and provides; He produced people with hearing, sight and hearts, spread them over the earth and will gather them.
Disbelievers ask when the promise will come; its knowledge is with Allah alone, and when they see it approaching their faces will be distressed.
The Prophet asks who would protect disbelievers from punishment whatever Allah does with him, and declares that he believes in and relies on the Most Merciful.
People are asked who could bring them flowing water if their water sank into the earth.
By the pen, the Prophet is not mad by his Lord's favor; he has an unending reward and a great moral character, and his Lord knows who has strayed.
Do not obey the deniers or the habitual swearer, scorner and gossip, proud of wealth and children, who calls Allah's verses legends; he will be branded on the snout.
The owners of a garden swore to harvest it early, making no exception and keeping the poor out, but found it ruined overnight, admitted their wrong and hoped for better.
The righteous have Gardens of Pleasure; deniers are asked whether Muslims would be treated like criminals, and what scripture, oath or partners support their claims.
On the Day the shin is uncovered, disbelievers called to prostrate will be unable, eyes humbled and disgraced, though they were called to it while sound.
Allah will lead those who deny the Quran gradually to punishment and give them time; they are asked whether a payment burdens them or they know the unseen.
Be patient for your Lord's decision, unlike Jonah, the companion of the fish, who called out in distress; his Lord's favor reached him, choosing him and making him righteous.
Disbelievers nearly make the Prophet slip with their eyes when they hear the message and call him mad, but it is only a reminder to the worlds.
The Inevitable Reality, a name for the Day of Judgement, is announced, and people are asked what can make them know what it is.
Thamud and 'Aad, who denied the Striking Calamity, were destroyed by a blast and a violent wind; Pharaoh and the overturned cities were seized; ancestors were carried in a ship.
When the Horn blows once, earth and mountains are crushed, the heaven splits, angels stand at its edges, eight bear the Throne, and people are exhibited with nothing hidden.
Whoever is given his record in his right hand invites others to read it and enjoys a pleasant life in an elevated garden, eating and drinking for his past deeds.
Whoever receives his record in his left hand regrets it, his wealth and authority gone; he is chained in Hellfire for disbelief and neglecting to urge feeding the poor.
The Quran is the word of a noble Messenger, not a poet or soothsayer, but revelation; had Muhammad invented sayings, Allah would have seized him; it is the certain truth.
A supplicant asked for the disbelievers' punishment on a Day of fifty thousand years, when the sky is like murky oil and the criminal would offer his family as ransom.
Hell's Flame, a remover of exteriors, calls whoever turned away and hoarded wealth.
Man is anxious and withholding, except those constant in prayer, giving the needy their right, believing in the Recompense, guarding their private parts and true to trusts and testimony.
Disbelievers crowding around the Prophet hoping for Paradise were created from what they know; Allah can replace them, so leave them until they rush from the graves on their Day.
Allah sent Noah to warn his people; he called them to worship Allah, fear Him and obey him, so Allah would forgive them and delay them for a specified term.
Noah tells his Lord he called his people night and day, openly and secretly, but they fled; he urged forgiveness, promising rain and wealth, and pointed to Allah's creation.
Noah's people disobeyed, plotted and clung to Wadd, Suwa', Yaghuth, Ya'uq and Nasr; they were drowned for their sins, and Noah prayed against the disbelievers and for the believers.
A group of jinn heard the Quran and believed; they said their Lord has no wife or son, the heaven is now guarded, and they include Muslims and the unjust.
It was revealed that had they remained straight on the way, they would have been given abundant provision as a test; whoever turns from his Lord's remembrance faces arduous punishment.
The masjids are for Allah, so none may be invoked with Him; when Allah's Servant stood supplicating, they almost crowded around him.
The Prophet says he invokes only his Lord, has no power to harm or guide them, finds no refuge but Allah and only conveys His messages; disobeyers face Hell.
The Prophet does not know whether the promised Hour is near; Allah alone knows the unseen, disclosing it only to approved messengers guarded by observers, and has counted all things.
The one wrapped in garments is told to stand in prayer much of the night, recite the Quran slowly, remember his Lord's name and take Him as Disposer of affairs.
Be patient with what they say and leave the well-off deniers to Allah, who has shackles, fire and choking food for them on the Day the earth and mountains convulse.
Allah sent a Messenger as a witness over them, just as He sent a messenger to Pharaoh, who disobeyed him and was seized with a ruinous seizure.
Disbelievers are asked how they will guard against a Day that turns children white-haired, when the heaven breaks apart, for Allah's promise is always fulfilled.
This Surah is a reminder, so whoever wills may take a way to his Lord.
Allah knows the Prophet and others stand much of the night; He turned to them in forgiveness, so recite what is easy, pray, give zakah, lend Allah a goodly loan.
The one covered in a garment is told to arise and warn, glorify his Lord, purify his clothing, avoid uncleanliness, not give to gain more, and be patient.
When the trumpet is blown, that Day will be hard and not easy for the disbelievers.
A man given wealth and children still wants more, though obstinate toward Allah's verses; after deliberating he frowned, turned away in arrogance and called it imitated magic and human speech.
He will be driven into Saqar, which spares nothing and blackens skin, kept by nineteen angels whose number is a trial for disbelievers; the Fire is a warning to humanity.
Every soul is held for its deeds except the companions of the right, who ask criminals what put them in Saqar: no prayer, no feeding the poor, idle talk, denial.
Disbelievers flee from the reminder like alarmed donkeys from a lion, each wanting scriptures of his own, for they do not fear the Hereafter.
