The Quran is a reminder for whoever wills, though none remember unless Allah wills; He is worthy of fear and of granting forgiveness.
By the Day of Resurrection and the reproaching soul, Allah can reassemble man's bones, even his fingertips, yet man wants to keep sinning and asks when that Day is.
When sight is dazzled and the sun and moon are joined, man will seek escape but find none; he will be told his deeds and be a witness against himself.
The Prophet is told not to hurry his tongue in reciting the Quran, for Allah will gather it, recite it and explain it.
People love the fleeting life and neglect the Hereafter; that Day some faces will be radiant, looking at their Lord, and others contorted, expecting a backbreaking blow.
When the soul reaches the collarbones, the dying one knows it is the parting, and that Day the procession is to his Lord.
The disbeliever neither believed nor prayed, but denied, turned away and went to his people swaggering; woe to him, and woe.
Man will not be left neglected; Allah, who formed him from a drop of semen and a clot into male and female, is able to give life to the dead.
Man was once nothing mentioned; Allah created him from a mixed drop to test him, gave him hearing and sight and showed him the way, grateful or ungrateful.
Allah has prepared chains, shackles and a blaze for the disbelievers.
The righteous fulfill vows, fear a dreadful Day and feed the needy, orphan and captive only for Allah, who protects them and rewards their patience with a garden and silk.
In Paradise they recline on couches in shade with neither sun nor cold, served silver vessels and ginger-mixed drink by eternal youths, wearing green silk and silver bracelets.
Having sent down the Quran progressively, Allah tells the Prophet to be patient, not obey sinners, and remember his Lord's name morning, evening and long into the night.
Disbelievers love the fleeting life, though Allah made them and can change them; this is a reminder, yet none wills unless Allah wills; He admits whom He wills to mercy.
By the winds and the message-bringing angels, what is promised will happen: stars are obliterated, the heaven opens, mountains are blown away, and woe that Day to the deniers.
Allah destroyed the former peoples and will follow them with the later ones; thus He deals with criminals, and woe that Day to the deniers.
Allah created people from a disdained fluid placed in a firm lodging for a known term; woe that Day to the deniers.
Allah made the earth a container for the living and the dead, set lofty mountains and gave sweet water to drink; woe that Day to the deniers.
Deniers will be sent to a three-columned shadow of smoke giving no shade from the flame, which throws sparks as huge as fortresses.
On the Day of Judgement the deniers will not speak or be allowed excuses; all peoples are assembled, and they are challenged to plan against Allah if they can.
The righteous will be among shade, springs and fruits they desire, told to eat and drink in satisfaction for what they did, as Allah rewards the doers of good.
The criminals may eat and enjoy briefly; they refuse to bow when told, and are asked in what statement after the Quran they will believe.
People question one another about the great news, the Day of Judgement, over which they disagree; they will soon come to know.
Allah made the earth a resting place, mountains as stakes, people in pairs, sleep for rest, night and day, seven heavens, a burning lamp, and rain for grain and gardens.
The Day of Judgement is appointed: the Horn is blown, people come in multitudes, the heaven opens into gateways and the mountains become a mirage.
Hell lies in wait for transgressors, who will stay for ages tasting only scalding water and purulence, a fit recompense for denying the account and Allah's verses.
The righteous attain gardens, grapevines, companions of equal age and a full cup, hearing no ill speech or falsehood, a reward and gift from their Lord.
On the True Day the Spirit and angels stand in rows, none speaking without permission; each will see what he sent ahead, and the disbeliever will wish he were dust.
By the angels who take souls and arrange affairs, on the Day of the blast and the one that follows, hearts will tremble and eyes be humbled.
They ask whether they will be returned to life after becoming decayed bones, calling it a losing return, yet one shout will bring them onto the earth's surface.
Allah called Moses in the valley of Tuwa to go to transgressing Pharaoh, who denied the great sign, proclaimed himself most exalted lord, and was seized in exemplary punishment.
Allah built the heaven, raised it, darkened its night and brought out its brightness, then spread the earth, brought out its water and pasture and set the mountains as provision.
When the great Calamity comes and Hellfire is exposed, whoever transgressed and preferred worldly life goes to Hellfire, and whoever feared his Lord and restrained his desires goes to Paradise.
They ask the Prophet when the Hour comes; its time rests with his Lord, he is only a warner, and they will feel they stayed but an afternoon or morning.
The Prophet frowned and turned from a blind man, Ibn Umm Maktum, who came seeking purification, while attending to one who thought himself without need.
These verses are a reminder for whoever wills, recorded in honored, purified sheets carried by noble, dutiful messenger-angels.
Man is cursed for disbelief; Allah created him from a sperm-drop, eased his way, causes his death and burial and will raise him, yet he has not fulfilled His command.
Man should consider his food: Allah pours rain, splits the earth and grows grain, grapes, olives, palms, gardens, fruit and grass for people and their livestock.
When the Deafening Blast comes, a man flees from his brother, parents, wife and children; some faces will be bright and joyful, others dark with dust, the disbelievers.
When the sun is darkened, stars fall, seas are aflame, the buried girl is asked why she was killed, Hellfire blazes and Paradise nears, each soul knows what it brought.
The Quran is a noble messenger's word, not an expelled devil's; their companion, who saw Gabriel, is not mad; it is a reminder to the worlds for whoever wills.
When the sky breaks apart, stars scatter, seas erupt and graves are overturned, each soul will know what it sent forth and kept back.
Man is asked what deceived him about his Generous Lord, who created, proportioned and balanced him and assembled him in whatever form He willed.
People deny the Recompense, though noble keepers are appointed over them, recording and knowing whatever they do.
The righteous will be in pleasure and the wicked in Hellfire, burning there on the Day of Recompense and never absent from it.
The Day of Recompense is when no soul can do anything for another, and the command that Day is entirely Allah's.
Woe to those who take full measure from people but give less by measure or weight, as if they will not be resurrected before the Lord of the worlds.
The record of the wicked is in sijjeen; woe to those who deny the Day of Recompense and call Allah's verses legends; their hearts are stained, and they will burn.
The record of the righteous is in 'illiyyun; they recline on couches, faces radiant, drinking sealed wine ending in musk, mixed from Tasneem, the spring of those brought near.
Criminals used to laugh and wink at the believers and call them lost; on that Day the believers, on couches, will laugh at the disbelievers.
When the sky splits and the earth is stretched out and casts out its contents, obeying its Lord, mankind is told it labors toward its Lord and will meet it.
Whoever gets his record in his right hand has an easy account and returns happy; whoever gets it behind his back burns, having thought he would never return.
By the twilight, night and full moon, people will pass from state to state; yet disbelievers do not believe or prostrate at the Quran, and face punishment, unlike righteous believers.
Cursed were the companions of the fiery trench, who witnessed what they did to the believers, resenting them only for believing in Allah; unrepentant torturers face Hell, believers gardens.
Allah's vengeance is severe; He originates and repeats, and He is the Forgiving, the Affectionate, the honorable Owner of the Throne, doing whatever He intends.
The story of the soldiers of Pharaoh and Thamud is recalled, yet disbelievers persist in denial while Allah encompasses them.
This is an honored Quran inscribed in a Preserved Slate.
By the sky and the piercing star, every soul has a protector; Allah can return man, created from an ejected fluid, on the Day secrets are put on trial.
By the sky that returns rain and the earth that cracks open, the Quran is a decisive word, not amusement; the disbelievers plot, Allah plots, so give them time.
Exalt the name of your Lord, the Most High, who created and proportioned, destined and guided, and brings out pasture then turns it to black stubble.
Allah will make the Prophet recite so he does not forget, except as Allah wills, and will ease him toward ease.
Remind, for whoever fears Allah takes heed while the wretched avoid it and burn in the greatest Fire; whoever purifies himself, remembers his Lord's name and prays succeeds.
People prefer worldly life though the Hereafter is better and more lasting, as stated in the former scriptures of Abraham and Moses.
On the Overwhelming Day some faces will be humbled and weary, burning in a hot Fire, drinking from a boiling spring and eating a thorny plant that does not nourish.
Other faces will be joyful, pleased with their effort, in an elevated garden free of unsuitable speech, with a flowing spring, raised couches, cups, cushions and spread carpets.
People are asked to look at how camels are created, the sky raised, the mountains set up and the earth spread out.
The Prophet is only a reminder, not a controller; Allah will punish whoever turns away and disbelieves, for their return and account are with Him.
By the dawn and ten nights, Allah dealt with 'Aad of Iram, Thamud who carved rocks, and Pharaoh of the stakes, who spread corruption, pouring punishment upon them.
Man thinks Allah's generosity honors him and restricted provision humiliates him, yet people neglect the orphan and feeding the poor, devour inheritance and love wealth intensely.
When the earth is crushed, the Lord comes with angels in ranks and Hell is brought near, man will remember too late, wishing he had sent good ahead.
The reassured soul is told to return to its Lord, pleased and pleasing, and enter among His servants into His Paradise.
By this city, Makkah, man is created into hardship; he boasts of wealth spent as if unseen, though Allah gave him eyes, tongue and lips and showed him two ways.
The difficult pass is freeing a slave or feeding an orphaned relative or a needy person on a day of hunger, then being among believers who urge patience and compassion.
Such believers are the companions of the right, while those who disbelieve in Allah's signs are the companions of the left, with fire closed over them.
By the sun, moon, day, night, sky, earth and the soul inspired with its wickedness and righteousness, whoever purifies the soul succeeds and whoever corrupts it fails.
Thamud rejected their messenger, Salih, and hamstrung Allah's she-camel he warned them about, so their Lord destroyed them all for their sin.
By night, day and the creation of male and female, efforts differ: whoever gives and fears Allah is eased toward ease, the stingy denier toward difficulty, his wealth no help.
Allah has taken upon Himself to show guidance, and to Him belong the Hereafter and the first life.
Allah warns of a blazing Fire in which only the most wretched, who denied and turned away, will burn.
The righteous one, who gives his wealth to purify himself, repaying no favor but seeking only his Lord's countenance, will be kept from the Fire and be satisfied.
Allah has not left the Prophet; He sheltered him as an orphan, guided and enriched him, so he must not oppress orphans or repel petitioners, and must report His favor.
Allah expanded the Prophet's breast, lifted his burden and raised his repute; with hardship comes ease, so after finishing, stand up in worship and long for your Lord.
By the fig, olive, Mount Sinai and this secure city, man is created in the best stature then returned to the lowest, except righteous believers; Allah judges most justly.
The first revelation: recite in the name of your Lord, who created man from a clinging substance and, most Generous, taught by the pen what man did not know.
Man transgresses when he sees himself self-sufficient, yet to his Lord is the return.
Abu Jahl, who forbids a servant from praying and turns away, will be dragged by his lying forelock unless he stops; do not obey him, but prostrate and draw near.
Allah sent down the Quran on the Night of Decree, better than a thousand months, when the angels and the Spirit descend, and it is peace until dawn.

Disbelievers among the People of the Scripture and polytheists would not leave disbelief until clear evidence came, a Messenger reciting purified scriptures, though commanded only to worship Allah sincerely.
Disbelievers among the People of the Scripture and the polytheists abide in Hell, the worst of creatures, while righteous believers, the best of creatures, abide in gardens, pleased with Allah.
When the earth quakes, throws out its burdens and reports its news, people come forth in groups to see their deeds, every atom's weight of good or evil.
By the panting chargers raising dust at dawn, mankind is ungrateful to his Lord, witnesses it himself and is intense in love of wealth.
When the graves' contents are scattered and what is in the breasts is laid bare, their Lord will be fully acquainted with them that Day.
On the Day of the Striking Calamity people are like scattered moths and mountains like fluffed wool; heavy scales bring a pleasant life, light scales an intensely hot Fire.
Competing for more distracts people until they visit the graves; they will surely see Hellfire with certainty and be asked that Day about their pleasures.
By time, mankind is in loss, except those who believe, do righteous deeds and urge one another to truth and patience.
Woe to every scorner and mocker who hoards and counts his wealth, thinking it will make him immortal.
He will be thrown into the Crusher, Allah's ever-fueled fire that rises over the hearts and closes upon them in extended columns.
Allah foiled the plan of the companions of the elephant, sending flocks of birds that struck them with stones of hard clay, leaving them like eaten straw.
For the Quraysh's accustomed security in their winter and summer caravans, let them worship the Lord of this House, who fed them against hunger and secured them from fear.
The one who denies the Recompense is he who drives away the orphan and does not urge feeding the poor.
Woe to those who pray but are heedless of their prayer, who make a show of their deeds and withhold simple help.
Allah granted the Prophet al-Kawthar, so he should pray to his Lord and sacrifice, and his enemy is the one cut off.
The Prophet tells the disbelievers he will not worship what they worship nor they what he worships; they have their religion and he has his.
When Allah's victory and the conquest come and people enter Allah's religion in crowds, exalt your Lord with praise and seek His forgiveness, for He accepts repentance.
May Abu Lahab's hands be ruined; his wealth will not avail him, and he and his wife, Umm Jamil, the carrier of firewood with a fiber rope, will burn.
Allah is One, the Eternal Refuge; He neither begets nor is born, and nothing is equal to Him.
Seek refuge in the Lord of daybreak from the evil of His creation, of settling darkness, of those who blow on knots, and of the envier when he envies.
Seek refuge in the Lord, Sovereign and God of mankind, from the evil of the retreating whisperer who whispers into people's breasts, from among jinn and mankind.
